market.question: Will "Sinners" win Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture at the 32nd Actor Awards?
market.resolution_criteria:
The 32nd Annual Screen Actors Guild Awards, honoring the best achievements in film and television performances for the year 2025, will be presented on March 1, 2026, at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, California, United States. Nominations are scheduled to be announced January 7, 2026.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed film wins the Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture, otherwise it will resolve to "No".

If for any reason no winner is announced by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No". In the case of a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the listed film whose name comes first in alphabetical order.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Screen Actors Guild, including data from their website (e.g., https://www.sagawards.org/) and the live broadcast of the award ceremony. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.title: 2026 Oscars Preview: Who will win, who should win, and who already has won - campustimes.org
evidence.text: The article says *Sinners* is one of five nominees for the Oscars’ new Achievement in Casting award, alongside *Hamnet*, *Marty Supreme*, *One Battle After Another*, and *The Secret Agent*. All five are also Best Picture nominees. It does not discuss the 32nd Actor Awards’ Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture race or predict whether *Sinners* will win it.

evidence.title: ‘Sinners’ and ‘One Battle After Another’ lead the 2026 Screen Actors Guild Awards nominees - TheGrio
evidence.text: “Sinners” received five SAG nominations, including an ensemble nomination for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture. Michael B. Jordan was nominated for best actor, while Miles Caton and Wunmi Mosaku received supporting-acting nominations. The article also cites awards momentum after director Ryan Coogler won Best Screenplay at the Critics’ Choice Awards. “One Battle After Another” led films with a record seven SAG nominations. The article reports nominations, not a winner; the 32nd Actor Awards are scheduled for March 1.

market.question: Will US GDP growth in Q1 2026 be less than 1.0%?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q1 of 2026, scheduled for April 30, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

If the advance estimate is not released, this market will resolve based on the first officially published figure for real GDP for the specified quarter (e.g., the ‘second’ or ‘third’ estimate, etc.), as reported by the BEA. If no official estimate is released by the date the next quarter's advanced estimate is scheduled to be published, this market will resolve based on the most recent previous figure released by the BEA.

evidence.title: GDP growth revised down to 0.7% for Q4 2025 as U.S. economy slowed - Yahoo Finance
evidence.text: The BEA revised U.S. GDP growth for Q4 2025 down to 0.7%, half its initial estimate, citing downward revisions to exports, consumer spending, government spending, and investment. It also said consumer spending had decelerated from Q3. For January, the first month of Q1 2026, BEA data released Friday showed inflation-adjusted consumer spending rose just 0.1% from the previous month, described in the article as essentially flat. These figures indicate weak momentum entering Q1 but do not establish Q1 GDP growth.

evidence.title: The business environment Q1 2026 - bbh.com
evidence.text: The Bureau of Economic Analysis revised U.S. GDP growth for Q4 2025 down by 0.7 percentage point to a 0.7% annual rate, below the 1.5% consensus forecast and sharply slower than Q3’s 4.4%. The revision reflected weaker exports, consumer and government spending, and investment, plus a smaller-than-previously-estimated decline in imports. The article provides no Q1 2026 GDP estimate. It notes that the Q4 data predate a Supreme Court tariff ruling and the early-March U.S.–Israel war against Iran, which raised energy prices.

evidence.title: Q4 GDP Revision And January PCE: Growth Downgraded While Core Inflation Firms (SPX) - Seeking Alpha
evidence.text: The BEA’s second estimate put US real GDP growth in Q4 2025 at 0.7%, down from its initial 1.4% estimate and below the 1.4% expected by economists polled by LSEG. The article says downward revisions were broad-based, including consumer spending and investment; real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 1.9%, revised down 0.5 percentage points. The BEA estimated that a partial government shutdown reduced Q4 growth by about 1 percentage point, though it could not quantify the shutdown’s full effects. These figures show weaker growth heading into Q1 2026, but the article provides no Q1 2026 GDP estimate or forecast.

market.question: Will Goldman Sachs or any of its underwriting affiliates serve as the lead underwriter in SpaceX’s initial public offering?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the bank that serves as the lead underwriter in the initial public offering of SpaceX.

If no IPO occurs by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, or SpaceX completes an initial public offering without a designated lead underwriter, this market will resolve to “Other.”

If multiple banks are identified as lead underwriters, this market will resolve according to the primary lead underwriter. If the hierarchy between them is unclear, this market will resolve once it is conclusively evident which bank is the primary lead underwriter, for example, through the order in which the banks are listed in the underwriting section of SpaceX’s final initial public offering prospectus, once released.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official disclosures from SpaceX. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.text: The article says, citing sources, that Goldman Sachs is among the lead underwriters for SpaceX’s planned IPO, alongside Bank of America, Citi, JPMorgan, and Morgan Stanley. It says those banks will take senior roles and that an online meeting with the lead underwriters to discuss financial models is planned for May 4. The IPO had not yet occurred; the article says SpaceX could go public as early as June.

market.question: Will Republican Senate incumbents win all their nominating elections in the 2026 cycle?
market.resolution_criteria:
The 2026 midterm elections are scheduled to be held on November 3, 2026, with congressional primaries running from March through September.

This market will resolve according to the number of Republican Senate incumbents who do not win their nominating election to move on to the general election as a result of the 2026 midterm primary elections.

An incumbent will be considered not to have won their election if they are not declared the winner of the election they sought, including if they withdraw, suspend, or otherwise leave the race at any point after officially registering as a candidate, regardless of the reason. Incumbents who do not officially register as candidates for reelection will not be considered.

This market will resolve based on the results of all Senate nominating elections, including party primaries, top-two or jungle primaries, and primaries for special elections, that are scheduled to occur between March 1 and September 30, 2026. If a required runoff for any such election or a subsequent qualifying round in a non-partisan primary system could change the market’s outcome, the market will remain open until that contest is conclusively called by this market’s resolution sources.

A candidate's party will be determined by their ballot-listed or otherwise identifiable affiliation with that party at the time of their nominating election. A candidate without a ballot-listed affiliation to either the Democratic or Republican parties will be considered a member of one of these parties based on the party with which they most recently expressed their intent to caucus prior to the conclusion of the relevant nominating election.

The resolution source for this market will be the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources have conclusively called all relevant nominating elections. If all three sources do not achieve consensus in calling the relevant races for this market, it will resolve based on official state certification of the nominating election results.

market.question: Will Nicolás Maduro visit Venezuela by March 31, 2026?

If the listed individual visits Venezuela between market creation and March 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as the individual physically entering the terrestrial territory of Venezuela. Whether or not the individual enters Venezuelan airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Viktor Orbán be the next leader out before 2027?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the first individual who ceases to occupy their listed office.

An announcement of a resignation/removal, or a scheduled departure from office due to the outcome of an election, will not alone qualify.

Only permanent removal from office will qualify for resolution. Temporary removals, such as impeachment suspensions (e.g., Yoon Suk Yeol's recent impeachment), temporary invocation of the 25th Amendment, or any similar provisional transfers of power, will not count.

Additionally, if an individual continues in a caretaker or interim role (e.g., Gabriel Attal remaining as caretaker Prime Minister of France), they will not be considered to have ceased occupying the office for the purposes of this market.

If this criteria has not been met for any of the listed individuals by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”. No additional individuals will be added to this market after its creation.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

In a January Publicus Institute survey for Népszava, the opposition Tisza Party led Orbán’s governing Fidesz by 33% to 28% among the general population, unchanged from December. Among committed party supporters, Tisza led 48% to 40%. The survey questioned 1,001 adults and had a 3.1-point sampling error. Publicus also found 63% dissatisfied with the country’s direction. A government-aligned Nézőpont poll released the same day gave a contrasting result: 46% considered Orbán the most suitable prime minister, versus 35% for Tisza’s Péter Magyar. The conflicting polls leave the election outcome uncertain.

evidence.title: Hungarians have had enough of Viktor Orbán. But Trump’s tailwind could save his skin | András Bíró-Nagy - The Guardian
evidence.text:
Viktor Orbán faces his biggest electoral challenge after 16 years in power. Péter Magyar’s Tisza party has unified the opposition ahead of the April 12 parliamentary election, and nearly half of Hungarians say they want a change of government. Tisza leads in independent and opposition-leaning polls but trails in Fidesz-friendly polling.

The article says Orbán still has a credible path to victory. Under an electoral system Fidesz designed in 2010, smaller Fidesz-leaning constituencies could let it win a parliamentary majority despite narrowly losing the popular vote; Tisza would probably need a national lead of at least five percentage points. Orbán is also campaigning as the safer choice amid fears of war and instability, bolstered by his relationship with Donald Trump. The article describes the outcome as genuinely open.

market.question: Israel strike on Yemen by March 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Yemeni soil or any official Yemen embassy or consulate by the listed date, 11:59 PM Israeli local time. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact Yemen ground territory or any official Yemen embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Yemen soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on Yemen territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Water emerges as a dangerous new war target - straitstimes.com
evidence.text: One week into the Iran war, the Houthis had not joined Iran’s defense, though official communications warned that their “fingers are on the trigger.” The article says resuming attacks on Israel would be their lowest-risk option and would invite renewed Israeli airstrikes on Yemen. Most Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Israel during the Gaza war were intercepted or fell short, but some penetrated Israeli airspace, causing dozens of casualties and damage to Ben Gurion Airport. Previous Israeli strikes on Yemen were militarily and economically costly for the Houthis, particularly strikes on Hudaydah Port, an essential import lifeline and a source of illicit Houthi oil revenue. Such strikes also helped rally domestic support. An Israeli strike killed some Houthi political leaders in Sanaa, but the article says the group’s military leaders and principal power brokers remained untouched. It reports no renewed Israeli strike; its case for one is conditional on Houthi attacks resuming.

evidence.title: What to Know About Iran and the Widening Fighting in the Middle East - The New York Times
evidence.text: Al-Ain reported that the Houthis in Yemen, while monitoring the war in Iran, evacuated sites and facilities, deployed weapons, and fortified tunnels because they feared a possible US-Israeli attack. The article says they could still enter the conflict, but the timing and nature of any intervention were unclear. It also raises the possibility of pre-emptive strikes if surveillance shows they are preparing to enter the war. These are reported preparations and possibilities, not a report that Israel has struck Yemen.

evidence.title: Watch: Moment of drone strike close to Dubai Airport - BBC
evidence.text: The article reports that Israeli air strikes in Sanaa last August killed at least 12 high-ranking Houthi government members, including Prime Minister Ahmed al-Rahawi and chief of staff Mohammed al-Ghumari. It says those losses, along with other attacks last year, have made Houthi leaders wary of further Israeli retaliation. In the week after US-Israeli attacks on Iran began on February 28, the Houthis had not joined the fighting beyond rhetoric and a protest. An analyst said they were prioritizing avoidance of direct US or Israeli retaliation, but could resume attacks if struck directly. The article reports no new Israeli strike on Yemen during that week.

evidence.title: Maps and photos show the Iran war has seeped into the wider Middle East - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

evidence.text: The article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or predict one by March 31, 2026. Houthi leader Abdul-Malik Al-Houthi says an “Israeli shipping ban” remains in force and his forces are ready to resume strikes. Experts describe this as “controlled escalation”: retaining threats and capability without taking actions that could invite retaliation or endanger Houthi control of Yemen’s coastline.

evidence.title: Iran War’s Impact On The Red Sea And Horn Of Africa: Africa File Special Edition - Critical Threats
evidence.text: A fact-check identifies the first clip in a viral video as showing an Israeli attack on Yemen in August 2025, not a recent Iranian attack on Israel. It cites a report published August 24, 2025, saying the Israeli Air Force struck suspected Houthi targets, and a Reuters report published August 25 saying Israeli strikes hit Sanaa in retaliation for Houthi missiles fired toward Israel. The Israeli military said it targeted a military compound housing the presidential palace, two power plants, and a fuel storage site. A Houthi health official reported six people killed and 86 wounded. The fact-check identifies the video’s second clip as an Israeli attack on Damascus, Syria, in July 2025.

There were no reports that the missiles hit any targets. The Houthis also said they would prevent Israeli-linked ships from sailing in the Red Sea. The article reports Israeli strikes on Iran, but no Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Israel, Iran Trade Fire as Trump-Netanyahu Rift Widens - The Media Line
evidence.text: The article reports that Israel intercepted one missile launched from Yemen, apparently the first Houthi attack on Israel since an April ceasefire. The Iran-backed Houthis also declared a blockade of Red Sea and Bab el Mandeb shipping associated with Israel and warned that Israel-linked vessels would be treated as military targets. These developments indicate renewed Israel-Houthi tensions, but the article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or a decision to carry one out.

evidence.title: After escalating strikes, Israel and Iran signal end to attacks - The Washington Post
evidence.text: Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthi rebels fired at Israel and warned they would target Israeli-affiliated ships in the Red Sea. The Houthis announced a missile attack on Israel on Monday—their first since early April—and declared a “complete and total ban” on Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea. This raises the possibility of further escalation, but the article reports Israeli strikes on Iran, not Yemen, and does not say Israel plans to strike Yemen by June 30, 2026.

evidence.title: Israel and Iran trade strikes, imperiling already fragile ceasefire in war's 100th day - CBS News
evidence.text: On Monday, Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis fired a missile toward central Israel, triggering air-raid sirens across large areas, including the central and Shefela regions. No injuries were reported. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed a missile barrage against targets in “occupied Jaffa,” announced a ban on Israeli maritime navigation in the Red Sea, and warned that Israeli targets would be attacked and escalation met with escalation. The article reports Israeli airstrikes inside Iran in response to overnight attacks, but does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Yemen's Houthis declare 'total ban' on Israeli ships in Red Sea - Algoa FM
evidence.text: Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said they launched a missile barrage at Israeli targets on Monday, their first announced missile attack on Israel since a fragile ceasefire began on April 8. The Israeli military said it had identified a missile launched from Yemen toward Israeli territory and that its aerial defences were operating to intercept it. The Houthis also declared a “complete and total ban” on Israeli shipping in the Red Sea and said enemy movements there would be military targets. The article reports no Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Israel and Iran trade strikes, threatening to drag region back to full-scale war - thenewsminute.com
evidence.text: On Monday, sirens sounded across Israel after its military reported a missile launched from Yemen toward the country. Israeli rescue services reported no casualties or impacts. Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels later claimed an attack on Israel and warned they would target Israel-affiliated ships in the Red Sea. The article describes Israeli strikes on Iran that Monday, but reports no Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Israel says intercepted aerial target from Yemen as fresh strikes in Lebanon kill 14 - WION
evidence.text: According to Channel 12, Israel temporarily closed its airspace on Monday after intercepting a missile launched from Yemen. The Israeli army said sirens sounded in greater Tel Aviv and parts of central and southern Israel, and the Home Front Command had warned of the launch. The article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or give a date for the Monday incident.

evidence.title: Israel temporarily closes its airspace after intercepting missile from Yemen - Anadolu Ajansı
evidence.text: In a June 8, 2026 update, the Israeli military said the Israeli Air Force intercepted a drone launched from Yemen over Eilat. Israeli reports said there were no injuries or damage. No group had claimed responsibility; the article noted that the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen had repeatedly launched drones and rockets at southern Israel. It does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Israel strikes back at Iran military targets hours after missile barrage over Lebanon attack - New York Post
evidence.text: On Sunday, Israel said it struck military targets in western and central Iran. Nearly two hours later, the Israeli air force said it was intercepting a missile “from the direction of Yemen toward Israeli territory.” The article says a missile had not been launched from Yemen at Israel since April 4. It does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Iran launches several missile barrages at northern Israel, Israel vows to respond | LIVE BLOG - i24NEWS
evidence.text: The article reports that a missile launched from Yemen targeted central Israel. The IDF said it detected the launch and that its aerial defenses successfully intercepted the missile; Israel’s Home Front Command then said residents could leave shelters. The article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or give a date for one.

evidence.title: Houthis emphasize solidarity and coordination with Iran-led Axis of Resistance - The Long War Journal
evidence.text: The Houthis launched a handful of drones and missiles at Israel between March 28 and April 2 during the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. The article says they had conducted no attacks since and had not violated the ceasefire that began April 7. In a June 5 speech, Houthi leader Abdulmalik al Houthi said the group was ready to respond to any escalation and was coordinating with partners in the Iran-led Axis of Resistance, but he did not specify any planned action. The article reports no Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Mixed messaging from Iran and US on ceasefire deal - DW.com
evidence.text: Amid tensions over Israeli strikes in Lebanon and a faltering US–Iran ceasefire, Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency said Tehran would ask the Houthis in northern Yemen to impose a second shipping blockade in the Bab al-Mandab strait, at the southern entrance to the Red Sea, as part of a potential escalation. The article reports a proposed move, not a blockade already underway. It does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or an Israeli plan to carry one out.

evidence.title: Israel seeks Trump administration approval for wider air strikes in Beirut - Middle East Monitor
evidence.text: The article reports that Israeli air strikes hit Sana’a, Yemen, in September 2025—before the June 30, 2026 cutoff. market.question: Israel strike on Yemen by June 30, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Yemeni soil or any official Yemen embassy or consulate by the listed date, 11:59 PM Israeli local time. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact Yemen ground territory or any official Yemen embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Yemen soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on Yemen territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 12 launch by February 28?

SpaceX said on March 9 that it planned to begin testing the Flight 12 booster in the coming days; the flight’s upper stage, Ship 39, had recently completed qualification tests. The article therefore points against a launch by March 31, though the target is not a confirmed launch date.

It does not identify a launch date for Flight Test 12; moreover, it inconsistently calls the next flight the ninth integrated test despite citing Flight 11 as the previous flight. These facts show preparations are underway but do not establish that Flight Test 12 will launch by March 31.

The article says these tests support safe reuse, while further Pad 2 activation and propellant-loading tests were still planned. A first V3 Super Heavy booster accident during testing in November had already caused months of delay. market.question: Will Elliot die in Euphoria: Season 3?

"Euphoria: Season 3" is scheduled to air eight episodes weekly on Sundays at 9PM ET, beginning April 12.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the specified character dies during "Euphoria: Season 3". Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying death must show the specified character dead on screen, or otherwise that character’s death must clearly be stated to have occurred, even if offscreen (e.g., characters confirm their death in conversation, the funeral of a character occurs, etc.). 

If a death is reversed through a revival, resurrection, or reanimation that occurs after the character has died, that death will NOT qualify. A death must be permanent to count toward resolution. Qualifying deaths occurring in any timeline or dimension depicted in "Euphoria: Season 3" will count toward resolution.

Flashback scenes showing a character alive before their death, as well as dream sequences, hallucinations, or visions of dead characters, will not affect resolution. Characters who were already confirmed dead before "Euphoria: Season 3" begins will not count toward this market’s resolution.

If a character’s fate is deliberately left ambiguous, it will not qualify toward the resolution of this market. Only deaths confirmed by the end of "Euphoria: Season 3" will qualify.

Only events depicted in official "Euphoria: Season 3" episodes will count toward resolution. Post-credits scenes count if they are part of the official episode, but supplementary materials such as podcasts, comics, or other media do not count unless they are explicitly referenced within the show itself. The market will resolve after the final episode of "Euphoria: Season 3" is released.

market.question: Nothing Ever Happens: Interest Rates
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve immediately to “No” if any of the following conditions are met at any point by March 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET:

- The United States Federal Reserve increases or decreases the upper bound of the Target Federal Funds Rate.
- The Bank of Japan increases or decreases the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate.
- The European Central Bank increases or decreases the upper bound of the deposit facility rate.
- The Bank of Canada increases or decreases the target for the overnight rate.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

The full rules for this market can be found here:
https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Nothing-Ever-Happens-Interest-Rates-e9f9058457.jpg

market.question: Will Trần Thanh Mẫn be the next President of Vietnam?
market.resolution_criteria:
Vietnam’s President is selected through internal decisions of the Communist Party of Vietnam and its National Assembly. The Party is holding its 14th National Congress from January 19 to January 25, 2026, after which the National Assembly of Vietnam is expected to elect leadership positions including President.

This market will resolve to the next individual who is formally elected by the National Assembly to assume the office of President of Vietnam.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally elected to assume the office of President. Any acting, interim, or caretaker President will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If the offices of President of Vietnam and General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam are merged such that an individual is elected to hold a joint office as leader of the party and head of state of Vietnam, this market will resolve to that individual.

If no such President is elected by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the National Assembly of Vietnam; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.title: Party, State leaders join Hanoi voters in Election Day - en.vietnamplus.vn
evidence.text: The article identifies Trần Thanh Mẫn as National Assembly Chairman, and elsewhere as National Assembly President—not as Vietnam’s State President. It identifies Lương Cường as State President at a March 15 election event. In the passage cited by the supporting quote, it calls Tô Lâm General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and President, and says his UNGA 81 speech demonstrated Vietnam’s consistent principles and spirit of dialogue and cooperation on international issues. The article does not say Trần Thanh Mẫn will become the next President.

evidence.title: General election begins nationwide - en.baochinhphu.vn
evidence.text: The article identifies Lương Cường as State President and Trần Thanh Mẫn as Chairman of the National Assembly; it says both, along with Prime Minister Phạm Minh Chính, cast ballots. The election will choose 500 deputies to the 16th National Assembly from 864 candidates, with results expected March 22, 2026. The Assembly is expected to hold its first plenary session April 6–11 and April 20–25, 2026. The article does not say whether Trần Thanh Mẫn is a candidate to succeed Lương Cường as president.

evidence.title: Party and State leaders join voters nationwide in elections for the 16th National Assembly and ... - moit.gov.vn
evidence.text: The article identifies Trần Thanh Mẫn as Parliament chairman, not as a prospective president. It says party officials are expected to announce nominees for state leadership before Parliament’s opening session in early April 2026, when lawmakers are expected to approve the party’s choices, including the president. Tô Lâm, confirmed as Communist Party general secretary in January, is widely expected to become president; the article describes his elevation as a formality. This evidence points against Mẫn being the next president.

evidence.title: Vietnam’s Coming National Elections - Asia Sentinel
evidence.text: Trần Thanh Mẫn became chairman of Vietnam’s National Assembly after the “forced resignation” of his predecessor, Vương Đình Huệ, and was reelected to the Politburo last January. He says national election results will be announced by March 25. The article says the president is usually chosen at the newly elected National Assembly’s first session, in July 2026, and must be a Politburo member. It does not say Mẫn is seeking the presidency; instead, it reports that reelected party chief Tô Lâm is seeking to hold both the party chief and president roles.

evidence.title: Vietnam, Cambodia exchange multiple cooperation agreements - Tuoi Tre News | The News Gateway to Vietnam
evidence.source: Tuoi Tre News | The News Gateway to Vietnam
evidence.text: The article identifies Trần Thanh Mẫn as Vietnam’s National Assembly chairman. He attended a Vietnam–Cambodia ceremony alongside Prime Minister Phạm Minh Chính and a high-ranking Vietnamese delegation, and later joined a leaders’ meeting. It does not say Mẫn is a candidate for president or discuss who will hold that office next.

market.question: Will Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami (BJI) win the Bangladesh parliamentary election by 6% or more?
market.resolution_criteria:
Parliamentary elections are scheduled to be held in Bangladesh on February 12, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two political parties in the election for the unicameral Bangladeshi parliament, the “House of the Nation” (Jatiya Sangsad).

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place parties. Percentages of the valid votes received by each party will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two parties receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If the two listed parties receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the party whose listed abbreviation comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by October 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Bangladeshi Government, specifically the Bangladesh Election Commission (https://www.ecs.gov.bd/?lang=en).

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

evidence.title: Bangladesh: Turning Point? – Analysis - Eurasia Review
evidence.text: In Thursday’s parliamentary election, the alliance led by Tarique Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party won 212 seats in the Jatiya Sangsad, while its main competitor, the alliance led by Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, won 77—a 135-seat deficit for the Jamaat-led alliance. Rahman was subsequently sworn in as prime minister. The article does not report vote shares or a percentage margin, but its seat results show that the Jamaat-led alliance did not win.

evidence.title: BNP wins nearly half the votes, Jamaat a third - The Daily Star
evidence.text: No. In the 13th National Parliament election, the Election Commission’s party-wise figures, published on Sunday, put the landslide-winning BNP at 49.97% of the vote and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami at 31.76%. Jamaat trailed the BNP by 18.21 percentage points, rather than winning by 6 points or more. Jamaat won 68 seats after fielding candidates in 224 constituencies.

evidence.title: Bangladesh Election 2026 Result: Nation Approve as BNP Leads in 175+ Seats, Jamaat at 15, NCP-6; Referendum Passes With 72% | All You Need to Know - The Sunday Guardian
evidence.text: The article reports that unofficial results from Bangladesh’s February 12, 2026 parliamentary election gave the BNP-led alliance 212 seats and the Jamaat-led bloc 78. Pollster Mohammad Rubaiyath Sarwar said that, as of 3:00 a.m. Friday, with up to 200 seats counted and no formal result yet, the vote stood at 58.4% for the BNP side versus 38.6% for the Jamaat–NCP side—a gap of about 20 percentage points, consistent with his projection. His January 27 survey had put the BNP 21.8 points ahead of Jamaat. These reported figures do not indicate a BJI win by 6% or more.

evidence.title: Bangladesh Nationalist Party Wins Big in Pivotal Election - The New York Times
evidence.text: The Election Commission’s gazette reported official results for 297 seats in Thursday’s parliamentary election: the BNP-led alliance won 212 seats, while the Jamaat-led alliance won 77. Jamaat-e-Islami emerged as the main opposition, and its leader conceded on Saturday. These results do not support BJI winning the election by 6% or more. The article gives alliance seat totals, not a vote-percentage margin.

evidence.title: Majority female candidates highly educated, 67pc working women - Prothom Alo English
evidence.text: Voting is under way in Bangladesh’s February 12, 2026 parliamentary election. The article says 127 million eligible voters are choosing a government 18 months after a student-led movement ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, led by Shafiqur Rahman, is contesting in an alliance with the National Citizen Party and other Islamic parties. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party is also contesting, while Hasina’s Awami League cannot field candidates because its registration is suspended. Jamaat was banned and could not contest the 2018 or 2024 elections. The article provides no polling, current results or projected vote margin to indicate whether Jamaat will win by at least 6%.

evidence.title: 13th JS elections: Total candidates 1,981 with 288 of BNP and 224 of Jamaat - Prothom Alo English
evidence.text: Election Commission data for 298 constituencies show that the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has fielded candidates in the most seats, 288, while Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami is contesting 224. Islami Andolan Bangladesh has candidates in 253 seats, the Jatiya Party in 192, and the National Citizen Party in 32. Voting for all 300 parliamentary seats is scheduled for 12 February; the nomination-withdrawal deadline for Pabna-1 and Pabna-2 was extended to 24 January. The article reports candidate counts, not vote projections or an expected winning margin, so it does not establish whether Jamaat will win by 6% or more.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If the two listed parties receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the party whose listed abbreviation comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the election aren’t known by October 31, 2026 ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Bangladeshi Government, specifically the Bangladesh Election Commission (https://www.ecs.gov.bd/?lang=en).

market.question: Will Ken Paxton win the Texas Republican Senate Primary by 9% or more?
market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Texas are scheduled to be held on March 3, 2026, with a runoff on May 26 if no candidate receives a majority.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Texas Republican Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If two candidates receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the specified election are not known definitively by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the State of Texas, such as official statewide results published by the Texas Secretary of State (https://elections.sos.state.tx.us/index.htm); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Texas are scheduled to be held on March 3, 2026, with a runoff on May 26 if no candidate receives a majority.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Texas Republican Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If two candidates receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the specified election are not known definitively by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the State of Texas, such as official statewide results published by the Texas Secretary of State (https://elections.sos.state.tx.us/index.htm); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Texas are scheduled to be held on March 3, 2026, with a runoff on May 26 if no candidate receives a majority.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Texas Republican Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If two candidates receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the specified election are not known definitively by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the State of Texas, such as official statewide results published by the Texas Secretary of State (https://elections.sos.state.tx.us/index.htm); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Texas are scheduled to be held on March 3, 2026, with a runoff on May 26 if no candidate receives a majority.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Texas Republican Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher placed bracket (ascending).

If two candidates receive the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve according to the candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically.

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the specified election are not known definitively by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the State of Texas, such as official statewide results published by the Texas Secretary of State (https://elections.sos.state.tx.us/index.htm); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

market.question: Will Clear Street Group Inc. not IPO before April 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve based on Clear Street Group’s market capitalization at the closing price on its first day of trading.

As of market creation, the IPO is scheduled to price on February 13, 2026 (ET). If no such IPO occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "No IPO before April 2026".

Market capitalization expresses the monetary value of a company’s outstanding shares, stated in its pricing currency. It is calculated as the number of shares outstanding multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day.

If the relevant value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Resolution will be based on the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on the specified company’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will resolve according to the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will resolve according to the next trading day on which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading for purposes of this market.

market.question: Ukraine hits Moscow by March 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Ukrainian armed forces initiate a drone, missile, or air strike on Moscow municipality's soil by the listed date Moscow Standard Time (MSK). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Ukrainian armed forces that impact Moscow municipality's ground territory.

A strike on any area within the terrestrial territory of the Moscow municipality counts.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on the Moscow municipality's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by the Ukrainian armed forces will not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be official government/military statements (Ukrainian or Russian), multilateral bodies (UN, etc.), or a consensus of credible reporting from major international media and national broadcasters/newspapers.

If the date/time of a strike cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting within 48 hours of this market's end date, it will resolve to "No" regardless of whether a strike was later confirmed to have taken place.

evidence.title: Ukraine Invasion Updates, January 2026 - Critical Threats
evidence.text: In a March 9 interview, Fire Point owner and chief engineer Denys Shtilierman said its planned FP-9 ballistic missile could strike Moscow, claiming its impact speed would exceed 1,200 meters per second and that roughly 25% could penetrate air defenses. The article says Russia has effectively ringed Moscow and St. Petersburg with air defenses, so Ukrainian drones and even cruise missiles almost never get through. Fire Point had previously hoped to have functional FP-9 models by June 2026, and the article describes reaching Moscow as a goal for the end of summer—not by March 31. It reports no Ukrainian hit on Moscow.

evidence.title: Ukraine Hits Russian Shahed Drone Base in Rare ‘Shoot the Shooter’ Strike - Kyiv Post
evidence.text: On March 9, Fire Point co-founder and chief designer Denys Shtilerman said the company was developing the FP-9 ballistic missile to strike targets up to 800 kilometers away, including Moscow. He claimed its arrival speed would exceed 1,000 meters per second, compared with about 800 meters per second for the Iskander, making interception by Moscow’s dense air defenses harder. Developers plan the FP-9’s first tests for early summer; the article reports no FP-9 strike on Moscow.

evidence.title: Missiles made in Ukraine are bringing Putin’s invasion home to Russia - Atlantic Council
evidence.text: The article reports that in late February 2026, Ukraine used domestically produced FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles to strike the Votkinsk military production complex deep inside Russia. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was at a range of 1,400 kilometers. The article calls this a significant advance in Ukraine’s long-range capabilities: the Flamingo reportedly has a maximum range of around 3,000 kilometers and a payload exceeding 1,000 kilograms, making it much more powerful than the drones Ukraine typically uses for strikes inside Russia. Ukrainian officials said multiple Flamingos were launched for one to hit. The article does not report a strike on Moscow or establish that one will occur by March 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Quantifying Ukraine’s Strikes on Russian Energy Infrastructure - Baker Institute
evidence.text: The article reports that on February 20, Ukraine targeted the Votkinsk Plant, described as a strategic Russian defence-industry enterprise, with domestically produced long-range FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles. It calls the strike successful and cites former Aidar Battalion company commander Yevhen Dykyi’s assessment that it could suspend Russian ballistic-missile production for up to six months. This is evidence of a Ukrainian long-range strike on a Russian target, but the article does not report a strike on Moscow or establish that one will occur by March 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Zelenskyy and Starmer urge con­tinuing support for Ukraine against Russia as Iran war steals focus - Spectrum News
evidence.text: Russia’s Defense Ministry said Tuesday that it intercepted and destroyed 206 Ukrainian drones overnight over Russian regions, annexed Crimea and the Azov Sea. It said 40 of the intercepted drones were flying toward Moscow. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was asked about an increase in Ukrainian drone attacks on Moscow over the preceding few days. The article does not report that a drone struck Moscow or give a calendar date for Tuesday.

evidence.title: Ukraine Pushes War Into Russia as Drones Swarm Skies Near Moscow - UNITED24 Media
evidence.text: Ukrainian forces launched large drone attacks toward Moscow and Moscow Oblast in mid-March 2026. More than 100 drones were reportedly shot down approaching the capital on 15 March. Russian sources said at least 494 drones were shot down across Russia on 16 March, including 46 near Moscow. Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 199 drones flying in or toward the city were neutralised from 14–16 March; Russia’s defence ministry reported a further 40 attacking the capital overnight on 17 March. The article explicitly says Ukraine scored no hits in Moscow or its vicinity, although the attacks temporarily suspended operations at local airports.

evidence.title: Largest Drone Raid Since Full-Scale War Hits Moscow, Oil Depot Burns in Krasnodar - Kyiv Post
evidence.text: The Russian Defense Ministry said air defenses intercepted 206 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight on March 17, including 40 heading toward Moscow. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said 39 drones had allegedly been downed by 6:15 a.m. local time; he also claimed more than 250 had been shot down over Moscow since March 14, excluding the latest wave. Russian authorities reported attacks on the capital for a fourth consecutive day but no casualties or damage. Ukraine had not commented, and the Kyiv Independent could not verify the Russian reports. The article documents reported drones heading toward Moscow, not a confirmed hit on the city.

evidence.title: Moscow Reports Interception of 28 Ukrainian Drones - rediff.com
evidence.text: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Russian air defences destroyed 28 Ukrainian drones heading to attack Moscow by noon on Sunday. The article describes this as a second consecutive day of reported attacks; Russia’s Defence Ministry said 47 drones were destroyed approaching Moscow on Saturday. Moscow airports temporarily suspended operations. Sobyanin gave no details of damage or casualties on the ground, so the report documents claimed attempted strikes and interceptions, not a confirmed hit on Moscow. The article does not provide a calendar date establishing whether these events occurred by March 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Moscow attacked by over 60 drones in single day, mayor says - The Kyiv Independent
evidence.text: On March 14, Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin claimed Russian air defenses shot down more than 60 Ukrainian drones headed toward Moscow. He said 65 had been countered by 11:25 p.m. local time. Russia’s Defense Ministry separately reported destroying 280 Ukrainian drones across Russian regions during a 10-hour period, including dozens over Moscow Oblast. The drone threat temporarily suspended flights at three Moscow airports, but no casualties or damage were reported. The Kyiv Independent said it could not verify the Russian reports. The article describes drones approaching Moscow, not a confirmed hit on the capital.

evidence.title: Analysis: Ukraine’s Drone Strikes vs. Russia So Far in 2026 – Bigger Swarms, More Explosions - Kyiv Post
evidence.text: Kyiv Post records show that from Feb. 1 to March 18, 2026, Ukrainian forces launched at least 110 drone strike packages against individual Russian targets, including energy infrastructure, military units, ammunition dumps, and factories producing military electronics, explosives, and munitions. The article says attacks had risen to around four targets per night in January–March, with 100–200 drones entering Russian airspace on average during the preceding six weeks. On March 16, Russian Security Council Secretary Sergei Shoigu said no Russian region could consider itself safe from Ukrainian strikes. The article does not report a strike on Moscow through March 18; its confirmed targets for March 17–18 were elsewhere.

evidence.title: Kremlin Slams ‘Irresponsible’ Ukrainian Drone Attacks on TurkStream and Blue Stream Compressor Stations - The Moscow Times
evidence.text: Ukraine’s General Staff said its troops struck the Aviastar aircraft manufacturing plant near Ulyanovsk on March 16, about 800 kilometers (500 miles) inside Russia. On March 18, it reported preliminary indications that aircraft shelters and parking areas were hit and that damage was still being assessed; it did not identify the weapons used. evidence.title: Iran war: Tuesday to be 'most intense day' of US strikes - dw.com

Recovering uranium from inland sites such as Natanz or Isfahan would be a larger operation: he estimated a security force of roughly 1,000–4,000 troops alongside special operators, air cover and transport.
