It says this was Israel’s third strike on the bridge since early March. Israeli forces were advancing in southern Lebanon, but the article does not report that they crossed the Litani. Commanders reportedly sought a buffer zone reaching as far as the river, potentially up to 30 kilometers from the border; the article says this would not necessarily require a permanent troop presence. A 10-day ceasefire was announced for Thursday, though neither Israel nor Lebanon had confirmed it. The article gives no evidence that Israeli forces will cross the river by June 30.

evidence.title: Israel army chief orders 'Hezbollah kill zone' in southern Lebanon - France 24
evidence.text: On March 24, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Israeli forces would “control the remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani,” a river about 30 kilometers north of Israel’s border. He described plans for a defensive buffer and said the Israeli military was tasked with accelerating the destruction of homes in Lebanese border villages. The article says Israel is planning to remove homes and residents from the area between the river and its border, while its military says it has destroyed numerous bridges to cut Hezbollah supply routes. An International Crisis Group analysis said Israeli officials intend, if given the go-ahead, to capture at least a 30-kilometer-deep strip north of the border, but are holding back to avoid angering the Trump administration. These statements point to control *up to* the Litani, not an explicit plan to cross it; the article gives no June 30 timetable.

evidence.title: Israel presses assault on Lebanon border town ahead of US-hosted talks - Reuters
evidence.text: The article reports that Israel appeared to be intensifying its ground invasion of southern Lebanon and intended to establish a security zone along the Litani River, almost 20 miles from the border. Israeli troops were operating in and around Bint Jbeil, a town just over 2 miles from the border and among dozens of communities south of the Litani that Israel had called to evacuate early in the war. On Monday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the military was expanding beyond five hilltops it had controlled since the 2024 ceasefire toward a “solid, deeper security zone.” The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River or give a timetable for doing so.

evidence.title: Lebanon’s bridges and Gaza’s hi-rises show limits of Israeli military force - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: The IDF warned residents of southern Lebanon not to move south of a specified line of villages or approach areas near the Litani River. It said its forces remained deployed in the area during a ceasefire, citing continued Hezbollah activity, and urged civilians not to return to several border villages. UNIFIL also reported IDF movement across the Blue Line. The article does not say Israeli forces crossed the Litani River or give a date for such a crossing.

evidence.title: IDF reveals Forward Defense Line in southern Lebanon - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: The article says an Israeli invasion of Lebanon has been underway alongside US-Israeli strikes on Iran since the war began on February 28. It reports that thousands of people have been killed in those strikes and the invasion combined. It does not say whether Israeli forces have crossed the Litani River or plan to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Lebanese army restores road, bridge damaged by Israeli strikes - The Peninsula Qatar
evidence.text: The article says Israeli forces aim to occupy Lebanon up to the Litani River, which reaches the Mediterranean about 30 km (20 miles) from Lebanon’s southern border. It does not say they have crossed the river. A 10-day Israel–Lebanon ceasefire began Friday, but Defense Minister Israel Katz said Sunday that the military had orders to use “full force,” on the ground and from the air, if its soldiers in Lebanon faced threats. The article also reports Israeli strikes on bridges crossing the Litani and says the military had established a “yellow line” marking the area it occupied, without locating that line relative to the river. These details indicate continued Israeli operations in southern Lebanon, but provide no confirmed crossing or stated plan to cross the Litani by June 30.

evidence.title: France blames Hezbollah for soldier’s death in Lebanon - Dawn
evidence.text: The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River. It says the IDF called on hundreds of thousands of southern Lebanese residents to flee north, then struck bridges over the river from mid-March through early April. On March 13, the IDF said it had struck the Zrarieh Bridge, calling it a key Hezbollah crossing. The article says Israeli ground forces advanced slowly in 2026 and, after a month and a half, had not taken all the area south of the Litani. Reports of people driving across improvised river passages, and of Lebanon’s military reopening a damaged road and bridge during a 10-day truce, concern civilian crossings—not an Israeli crossing.

evidence.title: IDF kills Hezbollah terrorists, uncovers weapons in southern Lebanon - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: On April 7, 2026, the IDF said it had struck a crossing over the Litani River on Monday. It said Hezbollah used the crossing to move weapons, including rockets and rocket launchers, south of the river. The IDF called it the seventh such crossing it had struck since operations resumed in March. The article says several IDF divisions were operating in southern Lebanon, but does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River.

evidence.title: IDF to continue to attack Hezbollah in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: Human Rights Watch reported that more than 100 Israeli strikes across Lebanon on April 8 damaged the last main bridge linking southern Lebanon with the rest of the country. It warned that strikes making crossings over the Litani River unusable threatened to cut tens of thousands of people in southern Lebanon off from humanitarian aid, food and healthcare. The article describes fears that Israeli attacks could precede a land grab or permanent security presence, but it does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River or give a plan to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Civilians keep dying in Israel’s shadow war on Lebanon - Daily Maverick
evidence.text: A 10-day ceasefire took effect on Thursday after more than six weeks of fighting between Israel and Hezbollah. Under the announced truce terms, Israel said it would maintain a 10-km security buffer along southern Lebanon’s border and retain the right to strike Hezbollah to stop “planned, imminent, or ongoing attacks.” The article says Hezbollah had been hit by Israeli airstrikes and ground operations, and an analyst referred to a possible gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces. It reports destruction south of the Litani River but does not say Israeli forces crossed the river or give a date for any such crossing.

evidence.title: Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire - Japan Wire by Kyodo News
evidence.text: The article says Israel destroyed all bridges over the Litani River during the war, including the bridge at Qasmiyeh on Thursday. By Friday, cars were using a makeshift crossing there. A 10-day Israel–Lebanon ceasefire had begun, but it did not require Israeli soldiers occupying parts of southern Lebanon to withdraw. The article does not say Israeli forces crossed the Litani or give a timetable for them to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Analysis: Israeli goals in Lebanon war shift from imminently disarming Hezbollah to reestablishing South Lebanon Security Zone - The Long War Journal
evidence.text: As of the article’s early-April account, open-source material indicated that the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) had begun pushing into southern Lebanon, in some cases seizing a second line of frontier villages about 6 kilometers from the border. The IDF was preparing to propose a security zone roughly 2–3 kilometers from the Blue Line, with no Israeli outposts in it. The article says it remains unclear whether the IDF intends to reach the Litani River along the coast and in the interior before falling back to that smaller zone. It does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River.

evidence.title: 'Our Compass is Broken'—Israel's Ongoing War in South Lebanon - Middle East Research and Information Project
evidence.source: Middle East Research and Information Project
evidence.text: Israel’s ground invasion of southern Lebanon was deepening, with troops seeking to strengthen control of towns and villages in the south. On Friday, an Israeli army spokesman said the military planned to bomb the Sohmor and Mashghara bridges over the Litani River in the western Bekaa Valley, claiming Hezbollah used them. A reporter said Israel had already destroyed at least six other bridges over the river since its intensified aerial and ground offensive began in early March. The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River or give a date for a possible crossing.

evidence.title: Reports: 11 dead in Lebanon strikes; last bridge linking south to rest of country destroyed - The Times of Israel
evidence.text: Israel launched a ground invasion of southern Lebanon after Hezbollah attacked Israel on March 2; the IDF said on March 16 that its troops had begun a ground operation against Hezbollah there. On March 22, Defence Minister Israel Katz ordered faster demolition of homes near the border. His plan for an Israeli-controlled security zone would extend from the border to the Litani River—about 30 km away—and cover roughly 10% of Lebanon. The article documents demolitions in border towns but does not report Israeli forces reaching or crossing the Litani. Evacuation orders later extended beyond the river, but those orders do not establish where troops had advanced.

evidence.title: Mapping Israel's destruction of Lebanese bridges - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.text: On March 24, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz announced plans to take control of southern Lebanon from the Israeli border to the Litani River. At a briefing in Tel Aviv, he said Israeli forces had destroyed five bridges over the river and would seek to control all other crossings. The article reports a new ground invasion and says Israeli soldiers reached the Litani during the 2024 invasion, but it does not report Israeli forces crossing the river in the current operation or set a timetable for doing so by June 30.

evidence.title: Israel to control large buffer zone in southern Lebanon, its defence minister says - bbc.com
evidence.text: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said Tuesday that Israeli forces would seize and hold southern Lebanese territory up to the Litani River, creating a buffer zone covering nearly a tenth of Lebanon. After Hezbollah fired missiles into northern Israel earlier this month, Israeli forces carried out sustained airstrikes and ground operations, moving beyond short incursions and pushing deeper toward the river. Hezbollah said it would fight an attempt to hold territory. The article reports neither that Israeli forces have crossed the Litani nor that they plan to cross it by June 30; the stated objective is to reach the river.

evidence.title: Israeli Officials Signal Stepped-Up Atrocities in Lebanon - Human Rights Watch
evidence.text: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the military would take control of southern Lebanon up to the Litani River. He claimed Israel had blown up all bridges over the river used by Hezbollah and said Israeli forces would “control the remaining bridges and the security zone up to the Litani.” His stated objective reaches the river, but the article does not report Israeli forces crossing it or announce plans to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Multiple Israeli strikes destroy key Litani River bridge in S. Lebanon - dailysabah.com
evidence.text: The IDF announced Tuesday that it intends to control southern Lebanese territory up to the Litani River, about 30 kilometers (20 miles) from Israel’s border. Defense Minister Israel Katz said Israeli forces were already operating inside Lebanon to establish a forward defensive line, had destroyed key Hezbollah-used crossings including bridges over the Litani, and would control remaining infrastructure. The article does not say Israeli forces have crossed the river or specify whether they will do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Israel asserts control over southern Lebanon; 82,000 civilian targets struck in Iran, Red Crescent says; Antibiotics, insulin scarce in Cuba - Drop Site News
evidence.text: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said troops had blown up five bridges on the Litani River, about 30 km (19 miles) from the Lebanon–Israel border, which he said Hezbollah used to move fighters and weapons. He said the IDF was manoeuvring into Lebanon to seize a defensive front line and would establish a security zone; displaced residents would not be allowed to return south of the Litani until northern Israel was safe. The article reports Israeli activity at the river and plans to control southern Lebanon, but does not say Israeli forces had crossed the Litani or give a timetable for doing so.

evidence.title: Israel bombs five bridges over Litani river in Lebanon - Punch Newspapers
evidence.text: Human Rights Watch said Israeli forces had expanded ground operations in southern Lebanon, but the article does not report that they crossed the Litani River. Israel ordered residents south of the Litani to evacuate on March 4–5, then expanded evacuation orders north to the Zahrani River, about 15 kilometers beyond the Litani, from March 12. On March 16, 2026, Defense Minister Israel Katz said hundreds of thousands of Shiite residents would not return south of the Litani until Israel’s northern residents were safe. On March 18, an Israeli military spokesperson said bridges over the Litani would be struck to prevent reinforcements and weapons moving south; the military said it struck at least four such bridges between March 13 and 22. Human Rights Watch also cited Katz’s March 22 order to accelerate demolition of homes in border villages and military warnings about strikes near Hezbollah as evidence of risks to civilians. These statements and operations bear on Israel’s intentions in the area, but do not establish a crossing by June 30.

evidence.title: Lebanon’s Aoun warns Israeli attack on bridge ‘prelude to ground invasion’ - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Israeli forces struck the Qasmiyeh Bridge, a key crossing linking southern Lebanon to the rest of the country, on Sunday. The strike followed Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz’s order to destroy all crossings over the Litani River and homes near the Israel-Lebanon border. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun called the attack a “prelude to ground invasion” and said it appeared aimed at severing the southern Litani region from the rest of Lebanon and establishing a border buffer zone. Israeli army chief Eyal Zamir said the operation against Hezbollah, which resumed on March 2, “has only begun,” would be “prolonged,” and that forces were preparing to advance targeted ground operations and strikes. The article reports two Israeli soldiers killed in fighting in southern Lebanon, but does not say Israeli forces have crossed the Litani River.

evidence.title: Hezbollah attack kills one in north Israel as assault on Lebanon continues - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Israel has sent more troops into southern Lebanon for its ground invasion. Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the army to immediately destroy bridges over the Litani River used by Hezbollah, to prevent its fighters and weapons from moving south. Hezbollah said it targeted Israeli soldiers and vehicles near Taybeh and Khiam. The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River or give a date for any planned crossing.

evidence.title: Risk to IDF soldiers in Lebanon 'extremely unreasonable,' parents tell Netanyahu - Haaretz
evidence.text: Parents of soldiers in the Nahal Brigade’s reconnaissance battalion urged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reconsider their sons’ deployment in southern Lebanon, calling the risk unreasonable. They said one goal of the current invasion is to draw Hezbollah fire toward IDF troops in Lebanon and away from northern Israeli residents. Hezbollah said on Wednesday that more than half its attacks targeted IDF soldiers in Lebanon. The article does not say Israeli forces have crossed the Litani River or give a plan to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: No red lines: Israel's new tactics in its war on Lebanon - with pages taken from the Gaza playbook - thenationalnews.com
evidence.text: The article says Israel’s renewed offensive in Lebanon followed an escalation beginning after February 27, 2026. It reports that more than one million people—almost one-fifth of Lebanon’s population—have been displaced, and that destruction of bridges across the Litani River has further cut off the south from the rest of the country. The author describes Israel as the de facto military power south of the Litani after the November 2024 ceasefire, citing continued attacks, restricted return, military posts near the border and incursions into southern villages. The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River or state that they plan to do so by June 30.

evidence.title: Israel's campaign to sever southern Lebanon in a new ‘buffer zone’ - Reuters
evidence.text: Israeli ground forces are increasing their presence in southern Lebanon, and officials say they aim to establish a “buffer zone.” Israel has ordered residents south of the Zahrani River to move north; the evacuation zone extends beyond the Litani River to roughly 40 km north of the Israeli border. The article also says Israel has destroyed bridges across the Litani River. These facts indicate activity around the river, but the article does not report Israeli forces crossing it or give a date for such a crossing.

evidence.title: Israel’s military to occupy swathe of southern Lebanon amid widening war - South China Morning Post
evidence.text: Israeli ground troops were expanding their de facto occupation of parts of southern Lebanon, and Israeli authorities said they wanted a “buffer zone.” Defence Minister Israel Katz had ordered the military the previous week to destroy all crossings over the Litani River and homes near the Israeli-Lebanese border. Israel subsequently struck six bridges crossing the river; verified footage and photos showed each had been made unusable. The article reports no Israeli forces crossing the Litani or stated plan to cross it by June 30.

evidence.title: Loud booms, smoke clouds: Israel bombs Qasmiya Bridge, Lebanon's key crossing link | Video | World News - Hindustan Times
evidence.text: On March 23, 2026, the article reported that an Israeli strike destroyed the Qasimyeh Bridge over the Litani River in southern Lebanon amid an escalation with Hezbollah. It said Israel was targeting bridges across the river, claiming Hezbollah used them to move fighters and weapons into southern Lebanon. The article does not report Israeli forces crossing the Litani River.

market.question: Israeli forces cross the Litani River by June 30?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israeli military personnel cross the Litani River in Lebanon by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

“Israeli military personnel” refers to members of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) or any other official military units acting under the authority of the State of Israel. Intelligence or other non-military personnel will not count.

A “crossing” will be considered to have occurred if Israeli military personnel are confirmed to have physically traversed the Litani River in Lebanon at any point, including but not limited to by bridge, boat, swimming, wading, or temporary or permanent crossing.

Aerial insertion, parachute drops, helicopter landings, or other forms of aerial infiltration that do not involve Israeli military personnel physically traversing the Litani River will not qualify.

Mere presence on one bank of the Litani River, without confirmation that Israeli military personnel traversed the river to the opposite bank, will not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: 'Israel destroyed houses, roads, even trees': People return to destruction in southern Lebanon - France 24
evidence.text: The article, dated May 1, 2026, states that Israeli troops crossed the strategic Litani River, which the Israeli military has used as a de facto boundary. It also says large areas south of the river remained under Israeli military control despite a ceasefire in place since April 17.

evidence.title: Israel issues evacuation warning for seven Lebanese towns beyond 'buffer zone' - tribune.com.pk
evidence.text: The article says soldiers from Israel’s Golani Brigade and Multidimensional Unit identified two armed Hezbollah members in the Litani River area and guided an air strike against them on Saturday. It also reports Israeli troops operating in southern Lebanon. It does not say Israeli forces crossed the Litani River or give a date for any such crossing, so the reported strike does not establish that they crossed by June 30.

evidence.title: Israel attacks villages north of Litani to ease pressure on troops occupying crucial axis - مدى مصر
evidence.text: The article says Israeli troops are stationed south of the Litani River, while new evacuation orders cover more than 10 southern Lebanese villages and towns, including several in Nabatieh district north of the river. Lebanon’s state news agency reported Israeli strikes across the south, and Israeli military chief Eyal Zamir threatened to eliminate threats “beyond the Yellow Line and north of the Litani.” A reporter said Israel’s area of operations was expanding. The article reports orders, strikes and threats north of the river, but does not report Israeli forces crossing it or give a date for any crossing.

evidence.title: IDF condemns soldier pictured hitting statue of Jesus - rte.ie
evidence.text: As of the article’s report, the IDF had publicized a new defense line roughly 5–10 kilometers into southern Lebanon in most places, with some forces reaching about 14 kilometers at one point. It warned civilians not to approach the line and subsequently named roughly 20 villages along it and another 50 elsewhere in southern Lebanon to avoid. IDF sources said the April 17 ceasefire applied only north of the Litani River and that Hezbollah fighters remaining in southern Lebanon could be attacked if they did not surrender. The article reports Lebanese civilians crossing the Litani into southern Lebanon, but does not explicitly report Israeli forces crossing the river or give a date for any such crossing.

evidence.title: Outrage as IDF soldier pictured smashing statue of Jesus with an axe in south Lebanon - The Independent
evidence.text: The IDF released a map of its new security zone in Lebanon on a Sunday after a 10-day cease-fire announced by President Trump on April 16. The article says the map shows Israel’s forward defense line crossing the Litani River—which divides southern Lebanon from the rest of the country—to include the strategic Beaufort Ridge. The IDF also said five divisions continued operating south of the cease-fire line. The map is evidence of the line’s position, but the article does not explicitly say when Israeli troops crossed the river.

evidence.title: Lebanese start returning home after ceasefire but many have nowhere to go - The Arab Weekly
evidence.text: The Israeli army said that five divisions and Israeli Navy forces were operating south of its “Forward Defense Line” in southern Lebanon to dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure and prevent threats to northern Israel. Its published map showed a zone from the Mediterranean Sea to the slopes of Mount Hermon, with the Litani River marked as a reference line within the territory shown. The article does not explicitly say Israeli forces crossed the Litani River or give a June 30 timetable. Defense Minister Israel Katz said forces could act with “full force” during the 10-day ceasefire if threatened.

evidence.title: Lebanese return to 'unliveable' areas as ceasefire with Israel mostly holds - Reuters
evidence.text: According to IDF sources, the military has committed to remaining in southern Lebanon indefinitely, treating the Litani River as its security line with Hezbollah unless the group disarms. The article says Hezbollah fires nearly all its rockets from north of the river, including some from the Bekaa Valley 100 kilometers or more away. IDF sources said stopping that fire might require invading all of Lebanon, but almost no senior Israeli official had considered an invasion beyond the Litani, citing Israel’s costly 1982 experience. The article reports no plan or date for Israeli forces to cross the river by June 30.

An observer who returned to the Tyre region on April 18 crossed Qasmiyeh despite a bomb crater that had been filled in. Another returnee reported Israeli tanks and bulldozers near Houla after the April 16 ceasefire. The article does not say whether Israeli forces crossed the Litani River or plan to do so by June 30.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israeli military personnel cross the Litani River in Lebanon by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

“Israeli military personnel” refers to members of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) or any other official military units acting under the authority of the State of Israel. Intelligence or other non-military personnel will not count.

A “crossing” will be considered to have occurred if Israeli military personnel are confirmed to have physically traversed the Litani River in Lebanon at any point, including but not limited to by bridge, boat, swimming, wading, or temporary or permanent crossing.

Aerial insertion, parachute drops, helicopter landings, or other forms of aerial infiltration that do not involve Israeli military personnel physically traversing the Litani River will not qualify.

Mere presence on one bank of the Litani River, without confirmation that Israeli military personnel traversed the river to the opposite bank, will not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Yemeni soil or any official Yemen embassy or consulate by the listed date, 11:59 PM Israeli local time. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact Yemen ground territory or any official Yemen embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Yemen soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on Yemen territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Iran rejects a U.S. ceasefire plan as Trump again threatens to bomb its infrastructure - NPR
evidence.text: The Houthis claimed their first attack on Israel in support of Iran on March 28 and pledged to continue their strikes. The article says their attacks had been limited and intercepted by Israel, and that they had not attacked Red Sea shipping. After the first Houthi attack, a senior Israeli military official said Israel had prepared for such a strike since the war against Iran began on February 28: “We will choose when and how to hit the Houthis, according to our considerations. They will pay the price.” Israel struck Yemen repeatedly in 2024 and 2025, but the article reports no new Israeli strike on Yemen following the March 28 Houthi attack.

evidence.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 37 of US-Israeli attacks? - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Yemen’s Houthis said they launched a coordinated attack on Israel with Iran and Hezbollah in Lebanon. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the three allies fired cruise missiles and drones at Israeli military and other “vital” sites on Monday. The article says the Houthis, who control most of northern Yemen, joined the war in support of Iran on March 28. It does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Houthi Rebels Launch Coordinated Attacks on Israel With Iran and Hezbollah: how 31 outlets split - newscord.org
evidence.text: On day 37 of the war on Iran, the Israeli military said it detected a missile launched from Yemen toward Israeli territory—the fifth such attack since the war began on February 28. Yemen’s Houthis, alongside Iranian forces and Hezbollah, claimed a joint long-range attack on Israel targeting Lod airport in the Jaffa area and key military targets. The article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen.

evidence.title: Trump gives Iran 48 hours to open Strait of Hormuz as search continues for missing US pilot - KSAT
evidence.text: In an article dated May 5, 2025, the Houthis said they had launched a joint missile-and-drone operation with Iran’s IRGC and Hezbollah against Israeli targets; the article describes it as their fifth attack since announcing direct engagement in the war. Israeli sources said missiles and drones launched from Yemen were intercepted, with no casualties reported. The Houthis warned of gradual escalation, while Israel said it was consulting Washington on how to respond. The article does not report an Israeli strike on Yemen or a decision to carry one out.

evidence.title: IDF may not know how many ballistic missiles Iran has left - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: The article says Houthi leaders moved from offices in Sana’a and other areas they control to more fortified locations, including mountainous areas, and restricted phone communications. These precautions reportedly began as the group started missile and drone strikes against Israel “last Saturday.” Sources cited by The Wall Street Journal said the Houthis fear Israel may respond with assassinations or targeted airstrikes against their leadership. The article also says past airstrikes reached Houthi leaders and vital installations inside Yemen. It reports concern about a future Israeli strike, not confirmation that one is planned or has occurred in the period asked about.

evidence.title: Houthi Escalation Calculus Following Cautious Entry Into The Iran War - Critical Threats
evidence.text: On March 28, the Houthis (Ansar Allah), which the article says control about 30% of Yemen’s territory and govern most of its population, joined Iran’s war against the US and Israel. They launched two ballistic missiles at southern Israel; both were intercepted. The article describes this as a limited entry into the fighting, not an Israeli strike on Yemen. It says the Houthis had not resumed attacks on Red Sea tankers or announced plans to do so, but assesses that such attacks would bring severe retaliation from US and Israeli air and naval forces.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the July 2026 meeting?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's July 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for July 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their July meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the July 2026 meeting?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's July 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for July 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their July meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the July 2026 meeting?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's July 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for July 28-29, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their July meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: Will Iran strike Habshan Field or any Processing Plants of the Habshan Complex by April 30?

For the purposes of this market, only strikes that cause physical damage to the infrastructure of the facility will be considered. Missile and drone strikes that are shot down or miss their targets, or make contact in open spaces or around the facility, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

Attacks by proxy forces (i.e., Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count toward the resolution of this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Note: Cyber attacks will not qualify, even if they have kinetic effects.

market.question: Will Turkey strike Iran by April 30?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed country initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between market creation and April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by the listed country's military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by a missile launched by the listed country, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by ground operatives of the listed country will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.text: During the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran, Türkiye’s Transport Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu said a third Turkish-owned ship had passed through the Strait of Hormuz. The article reports no Turkish threat, plan, or strike against Iran. The ship’s passage is evidence of maritime transit, not Turkish military action.

evidence.text: Egyptian, Pakistani and Turkish mediators sent Iran and the U.S. a proposal for a 45-day ceasefire and reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the AP. It describes Turkey as a mediator, not as planning or carrying out a strike on Iran; it provides no specific indication that Turkey will strike Iran by April 30.

market.question: Will Saudi Arabia strike Iran by April 30?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed country initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between market creation and April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by the listed country's military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by a missile launched by the listed country, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by ground operatives of the listed country will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Iran strike Qatar by April 30, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Iran initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the listed country's soil or any official embassy or consulate of the listed country between market creation and April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Iranian military forces that impact a listed country's ground territory or any official embassy or consulate of that country (e.g., if a weapons depot on a listed country soil is hit by an Iranian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on a listed country's territory or cause damage.

Strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will be counted as Israel.

Only military actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran, or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory, will count toward the resolution of this market. Attacks by proxy forces (i.e., Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count toward the resolution of this market.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US or Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

If the date/time of a strike cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting by the end of the third calendar date after this market's end date, it will resolve to "No" regardless of whether a strike was later confirmed to have taken place.

An unidentified air-to-air missile downed the drone. The article does not say the drone struck Qatar or provide a calendar date for the interception.

evidence.title: Iranian drones and missiles hit ports, oil and gas facilities, and US bases in the region (March 17-19 updates) - The Long War Journal
evidence.text: The article reports that Iran attacked Qatar on March 17 and 18. Qatar said it intercepted two separate Iranian missile attacks on March 17, then nine missiles and an unspecified number of drones in another attack. On March 18, a ballistic missile struck Ras Laffan Industrial City, causing a fire at the major liquefied natural gas hub. Qatari defenses also intercepted two ballistic missiles targeting Ras Laffan, then four more, and later reported another Iranian missile attack of unspecified size. The same day, Iranian attacks remained intense in Saudi Arabia: defenses intercepted missiles and drones around Riyadh, Al Kharj, and the Eastern Province, including four ballistic missiles in each of two Riyadh attacks. In the UAE, an Iranian projectile damaged facilities near Dubai’s Al Minhad Air Base and started a fire without reported casualties; the UAE also reported confronting 13 ballistic missiles and 27 drones in one wave. The reported strike on Ras Laffan is direct evidence bearing on whether Iran will strike Qatar by April 30, 2026.

evidence.title: Iran war escalates, energy prices spike after Israeli strike on South Pars gas field - CBS News
evidence.text: CBS News reported on March 20, 2026, that Iranian missile strikes had already hit Ras Laffan Industrial City, a liquefied natural gas export terminal in Qatar. Qatar’s energy minister, Saad Sherida al-Kaabi, said two LNG units were struck Wednesday night, reducing the country’s LNG capacity by 17%. He estimated the extensive damage would cause $20 billion in annual revenue losses and take three to five years to repair.

evidence.title: Iran: Unlawful Strikes Across Gulf Endanger Civilians - Human Rights Watch
evidence.text: The article reports that on day 20 of a war that began February 28, Israel struck Iran’s South Pars gasfield, described as the world’s largest. Hours later, Iran launched missiles at oil and gas facilities in Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. The missiles hit Qatar’s Ras Laffan Industrial City, setting off fires and heavily damaging its LNG facility. The article says the attacks knocked out 17 percent of Qatar’s LNG export capacity. It does not state the calendar year of the strike, so the text alone does not establish whether it occurred by April 30, 2026.

evidence.title: Kuwait Ministry of Defence detects 14 ballistic missiles, 46 drones in 24 hours - Gulf News
evidence.text: In a Monday phone call, Iranian Foreign Minister Araqchi and Qatar’s Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani discussed the regional conflict and Tehran–Doha relations. Qatar’s foreign minister opposed the use of force, called for respect for Iran’s sovereignty, and urged an immediate end to the war. The article says Iranian forces have retaliated with missiles and drones against American and Israeli positions, including at regional bases; it does not report an Iranian strike on Qatar.

The article does not state a year for these March dates.

evidence.text: On Saturday, March 21, 2026, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB denied the validity of an apparent Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps infographic circulating on social media that warned all residents and citizens to evacuate Doha, Qatar, immediately. The article reports threats and an unverified warning, not a confirmed Iranian strike on Qatar.

It does not report a strike on Qatar or give a calendar date for Qatar’s decision.

market.question: Will Iran strike Qatar by April 30, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Iran initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the listed country's soil or any official embassy or consulate of the listed country between market creation and April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Iranian military forces that impact a listed country's ground territory or any official embassy or consulate of that country (e.g., if a weapons depot on a listed country soil is hit by an Iranian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on a listed country's territory or cause damage.

Strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will be counted as Israel.

Only military actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran, or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory, will count toward the resolution of this market. Attacks by proxy forces (i.e., Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count toward the resolution of this market.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US or Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

If the date/time of a strike cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting by the end of the third calendar date after this market's end date, it will resolve to "No" regardless of whether a strike was later confirmed to have taken place.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the US government officially announces or confirms that the United States is engaging in military coordination with, or providing military support to, Iranian opposition groups by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For confirmations to qualify, they must be unambiguous, on-the-record public statements issued by an authorized governmental person or entity, speaking in an official capacity.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement or qualifying confirmation will not be considered.

“Iranian opposition groups” refers to organized political, paramilitary, insurgent, or resistance groups that publicly oppose the current government of the Islamic Republic of Iran and seek to alter, replace, or overthrow it. This includes groups operating inside or outside Iran that claim to represent opposition to the current governing authorities.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.
 
For the purposes of this market, military coordination or support includes but is not limited to joint operations, direct battlefield assistance, intelligence sharing, weapons or equipment transfers, training, logistics support, or other clearly stated military assistance.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

The article also cites reports that US and Israeli intelligence agencies were working with Iranian Kurdish fighters as potential ground forces. On March 5, Trump said he would support Kurdish forces if they launched an offensive against Iran and called the idea positive, but he would not say whether the US would provide air support. On March 7, he reversed course, saying he did not want Kurdish fighters to join the war or be killed. The article reports no clear US commitment to provide military support to the Iranian Kurdish opposition.

An Iranian who fled Tehran questioned why the U.S. would attack a power plant if its aim was to topple the regime rather than harm the public; that remark is not a U.S. announcement.

But Trump declined to say whether the US would provide air support. The White House confirmed the calls while denying that he had agreed to a plan for an armed Kurdish uprising. The article reports no US announcement of military support for Iranian opposition groups or specific April 30 deadline.

These are reports of discussions and conditional support, not a public US announcement of military support. A Kurdistan Freedom Party official said Wednesday that U.S. officials had contacted Kurdish opposition leaders about a potential operation; a Komala official said its forces could be ready to cross within a week to 10 days. market.question: Will SpaceX raise between $50B and $60B in its IPO?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the total gross proceeds raised by SpaceX in its initial public offering (IPO) at the time of pricing.

The amount raised is defined as the aggregate dollar value of shares sold at the final offering price at the time of IPO pricing, as disclosed in the final prospectus filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shares sold pursuant to any overallotment option (greenshoe) will not be considered.

Secondary sales of existing shares by current shareholders will be included only to the extent that they are part of the IPO offering at pricing and reflected in the total gross proceeds. Private secondary transactions conducted outside of the IPO will not be considered.

If the total proceeds fall exactly on a boundary between two ranges, this market will resolve to the higher range.

market.question: Russia x Ukraine ceasefire by May 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Russia and Ukraine by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterward.

Only ceasefires which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Ceasefires which only apply to energy infrastructure, the Black Sea, or other similar agreements will not qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A peace deal or political framework will qualify if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, effective on a specific date. Frameworks or agreements that outline terms for a future peace but do not include an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not count.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia accuse each other of violating Putin's Orthodox Easter ceasefire - CBS News
evidence.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire, from 4 p.m. (1300 GMT) Saturday through the end of Sunday. Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered it on Thursday; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had proposed it more than a week earlier. It expired Monday amid mutual accusations of violations: Ukraine reported 7,696 and Russia reported 1,971. Ukraine said there were no long-range Shahed drone attacks, guided aerial bombings or missile strikes during the truce, but fighting continued in some sectors. Zelensky sought a longer ceasefire; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected an extension unless Zelensky accepted Russia’s terms. The article says recent US-brokered talks had not brought the sides closer to a broader agreement, with disagreement over territory remaining an obstacle.

evidence.title: Russia, Ukraine accuse each other of violating Orthodox Easter ceasefire - GMA Network
evidence.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire, scheduled from 4 p.m. Saturday through Sunday. President Vladimir Putin ordered the truce on Thursday, more than a week after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed a halt to hostilities. Both sides then alleged violations: Ukraine reported 2,299 by 7 a.m. on April 12, including assaults, shelling and drone strikes; Russia alleged 1,971 Ukrainian violations. Ukraine nevertheless reported no long-range Shahed drone attacks, guided aerial bombings or missile strikes during the truce. Zelenskyy called for a longer ceasefire, but Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would not extend it unless Kyiv accepted Moscow’s terms, and that military operations would resume when it expired. The article says recent US-brokered talks had not brought the sides closer to an agreement. Ukraine proposed freezing the current front line; Russia rejected that and demanded all of Donetsk, which Kyiv called unacceptable.

evidence.title: Russia and Ukraine to hold 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter - Sky News
evidence.text: Putin announced a 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter, from Saturday at 4 p.m. until midnight Sunday; Easter falls on April 12 this year. The Kremlin said Russia’s military had been ordered to stop operations in all directions, while remaining ready to respond to provocations or attacks. Zelensky said Ukraine would abide by the measure, having previously proposed an Easter ceasefire. The article reports the announcement and Ukraine’s stated intention to comply, not that the ceasefire had taken effect or held. A similar 30-hour Easter ceasefire last year led to mutual accusations of violations. US-led settlement efforts were paused, and the Kremlin said this proposal was not linked to resuming three-way talks.

evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia move towards potential peace deal, Bloomberg reports - Reuters
evidence.text: During the week of 5–12 April 2026, Russia and Ukraine observed a formal 32-hour Easter truce, but each accused the other of violating it. President Vladimir Putin’s surprise 10 April ceasefire announcement mirrored a Ukrainian proposal he had previously dismissed. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready for reciprocal steps and willing to extend the truce; he also proposed a trilateral leaders’ meeting. The article says diplomacy was tentatively resuming, while Zelenskyy warned that spring and summer would be difficult politically and diplomatically. It characterizes Putin’s reversal as a sign of pressure on Russia, but reports no agreement on a longer ceasefire.

evidence.title: Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky agree on 32-hour Ukraine-Russia ceasefire for Orthodox Easter - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire on April 9, scheduled from 4 p.m. April 11 through the end of April 12. Ukraine had previously proposed a similar holiday truce. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine was ready to take “mirror steps,” would act accordingly, and was prepared to extend the ceasefire, while warning that Russian violations would receive a proportional response. Ukraine’s General Staff alleged 469 violations after the ceasefire began, including 22 assaults, 153 shelling incidents, 19 kamikaze-drone strikes, and 275 FPV-drone strikes. Russian authorities accused Ukraine of drone strikes in Kursk and Belgorod that injured five people. The article says the Kyiv Independent could not verify either side’s claims.

evidence.title: Trump cautions Iran against charging tolls to go through Strait of Hormuz as fragile ceasefire holds - CBS News
evidence.text: Russia announced a 32-hour ceasefire over Orthodox Easter, from 4:00 p.m. Saturday until the end of Sunday. President Vladimir Putin ordered Russian forces to cease hostilities in all directions; the Kremlin called it a “humanitarian” pause and said it assumed Ukraine would follow Russia’s example. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had proposed an Easter ceasefire and would reciprocate. The Kremlin said the pause had not been discussed with Ukraine or the United States beforehand. The article reports an announced, short truce—not that it had taken effect or held. It also says Russia has rejected a longer-term unconditional ceasefire, previous truces drew accusations of hundreds of violations, and US-brokered peace talks have been effectively frozen since late February amid unresolved territorial disputes.

evidence.title: Fact-checking Trump and Hegseth's claims of U.S. 'victory' in the Iran war - PBS
evidence.text: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to mirror ceasefire steps after Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a temporary Easter truce. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had proposed a ceasefire for the Easter holidays and urged Russia not to resume strikes afterward. Putin ordered Russian forces to halt hostilities for 32 hours, from 4 p.m. Saturday through Sunday. The article says previous ceasefire attempts had little impact, with both sides alleging violations. It also says U.S.-led talks had made no progress on key issues, Russian and Ukrainian forces remained in combat, and Moscow continued to insist on longstanding demands that have blocked an agreement.

evidence.title: Trump Renews Threat of Attacks on Iran’s Bridges and Power Plants - The New York Times
evidence.text: Ukraine and Russia appeared close to a 32-hour, theatre-wide ceasefire beginning Saturday afternoon for Orthodox Easter. It could be their first official ceasefire across the war theatre since Russia’s February 2022 full-scale invasion. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly offered an Easter pause and was ready to reciprocate; Russian President Vladimir Putin acquiesced, and the Kremlin said it had ordered hostilities to stop “in all directions.” The Kremlin also said its troops should be ready to respond to provocations or attacks. The pause had not yet begun, and the article does not establish whether it would hold or extend beyond Easter. Earlier truces were described as unofficial, localized, or limited in scope.

evidence.title: Russia’s Putin announces Orthodox Easter ceasefire, Ukraine’s Zelensky agrees - The Straits Times
evidence.text: Putin ordered Russian troops to cease fire “in all directions” from 16:00 local time (13:00 GMT) on Saturday, 11 April, through Orthodox Easter Sunday. Zelensky said Ukraine was ready to take “symmetrical steps” and urged Russia not to resume strikes afterward. Putin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, ruled out an extension, saying the ceasefire was only temporary and “exclusively humanitarian.” The article does not establish that the truce took effect or held. Kyiv wants a full, stable ceasefire before peace negotiations, while Moscow insists on agreeing a peace deal first; US-mediated talks were on hold. The article also reports Ukrainian allegations of hundreds of violations during a previous Russian-declared ceasefire.

evidence.title: Strikes, Summits and the Possibility of Boots on the Ground in Iran: The Week That Shaped Two Wars. The Big Five, 5 April Edition - Futura Doctrina | Mick Ryan
evidence.text: On April 3, 2026, the Kremlin said Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan discussed Ukraine, and Putin thanked Erdogan for his continued readiness to facilitate negotiations. The article reports no Russia–Ukraine ceasefire agreement, timetable, or commitment to a ceasefire by May 31. The leaders’ separate call for an immediate ceasefire concerned the Persian Gulf, not Ukraine.

evidence.title: Pakistan says it will host U.S.-Iran talks soon as Iran warns against U.S. ground operations - CBS News
evidence.text: Zelenskyy said he was concerned that Washington would provide Ukraine security guarantees only after a comprehensive peace agreement, not after a ceasefire. Kyiv claims Russia refuses to end the war unless it takes all of the Donbas. Russian forces hold most of the region but not a heavily fortified strip; Zelenskyy said the U.S. has not directly pressed Ukraine to withdraw from it. He also disputed Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s characterization of his account of the talks. Fighting continued: Ukrainian authorities reported that Russia launched more than 270 drones overnight, killing at least five people.

evidence.title: Trump says Iran is ready to negotiate a ceasefire but he's not ready to make a deal - NBC News
evidence.text: In a Saturday interview, President Donald Trump said he was trying to make peace between Russia and Ukraine. He claimed Russian President Vladimir Putin was willing to make a deal but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy did not want one: “Tell Zelenskyy to make a deal because Putin’s willing to make a deal.” Trump added that Zelenskyy was “far more difficult to make a deal with.” These are Trump’s assessments; the article reports no ceasefire agreement or timetable. Trump also said his temporary easing of sanctions on Russian oil, imposed after Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, would end when the current oil crisis was over.

market.question: Russia x Ukraine ceasefire by May 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Russia and Ukraine by May 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterward.

Only ceasefires which constitute a general pause in the conflict will qualify. Ceasefires which only apply to energy infrastructure, the Black Sea, or other similar agreements will not qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A peace deal or political framework will qualify if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, effective on a specific date. Frameworks or agreements that outline terms for a future peace but do not include an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not count.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia accuse each other of violating Putin's Orthodox Easter ceasefire - CBS News
evidence.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire, from 4 p.m. (1300 GMT) Saturday through the end of Sunday. Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered it on Thursday; Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had proposed it more than a week earlier. It expired Monday amid mutual accusations of violations: Ukraine reported 7,696 and Russia reported 1,971. Ukraine said there were no long-range Shahed drone attacks, guided aerial bombings or missile strikes during the truce, but fighting continued in some sectors. Zelensky sought a longer ceasefire; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected an extension unless Zelensky accepted Russia’s terms. The article says recent US-brokered talks had not brought the sides closer to a broader agreement, with disagreement over territory remaining an obstacle.

evidence.title: Russia, Ukraine accuse each other of violating Orthodox Easter ceasefire - GMA Network
evidence.text: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire, scheduled from 4 p.m. Saturday through Sunday. President Vladimir Putin ordered the truce on Thursday, more than a week after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed a halt to hostilities. Both sides then alleged violations: Ukraine reported 2,299 by 7 a.m. on April 12, including assaults, shelling and drone strikes; Russia alleged 1,971 Ukrainian violations. Ukraine nevertheless reported no long-range Shahed drone attacks, guided aerial bombings or missile strikes during the truce. Zelenskyy called for a longer ceasefire, but Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would not extend it unless Kyiv accepted Moscow’s terms, and that military operations would resume when it expired. The article says recent US-brokered talks had not brought the sides closer to an agreement. Ukraine proposed freezing the current front line; Russia rejected that and demanded all of Donetsk, which Kyiv called unacceptable.

evidence.title: Russia and Ukraine to hold 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter - Sky News
evidence.text: Putin announced a 32-hour ceasefire for Orthodox Easter, from Saturday at 4 p.m. until midnight Sunday; Easter falls on April 12 this year. The Kremlin said Russia’s military had been ordered to stop operations in all directions, while remaining ready to respond to provocations or attacks. Zelensky said Ukraine would abide by the measure, having previously proposed an Easter ceasefire. The article reports the announcement and Ukraine’s stated intention to comply, not that the ceasefire had taken effect or held. A similar 30-hour Easter ceasefire last year led to mutual accusations of violations. US-led settlement efforts were paused, and the Kremlin said this proposal was not linked to resuming three-way talks.

evidence.title: U.S. aircraft carrier in Iran war expected to leave Middle East with conflict's estimated cost at $25 billion - CBS News
evidence.text: On April 29, 2026, President Trump said he had spoken with Russian President Vladimir Putin “mostly about Ukraine” and also about Iran. Asked which war would end first, Trump replied, “I don't know, maybe they're on a similar timetable.” He also said he had urged Putin to focus on ending the war in Ukraine rather than helping with Iran’s enriched uranium. The article gives no date for an end to either war and reports no Russia–Ukraine ceasefire agreement or May 31 deadline.

evidence.title: Ukraine, Russia move towards potential peace deal, Bloomberg reports - Reuters
evidence.text: During the week of 5–12 April 2026, Russia and Ukraine observed a formal 32-hour Easter truce, but each accused the other of violating it. President Vladimir Putin’s surprise 10 April ceasefire announcement mirrored a Ukrainian proposal he had previously dismissed. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready for reciprocal steps and willing to extend the truce; he also proposed a trilateral leaders’ meeting. The article says diplomacy was tentatively resuming, while Zelenskyy warned that spring and summer would be difficult politically and diplomatically. It characterizes Putin’s reversal as a sign of pressure on Russia, but reports no agreement on a longer ceasefire.

evidence.title: Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky agree on 32-hour Ukraine-Russia ceasefire for Orthodox Easter - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a 32-hour Orthodox Easter ceasefire on April 9, scheduled from 4 p.m. April 11 through the end of April 12. Ukraine had previously proposed a similar holiday truce. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine was ready to take “mirror steps,” would act accordingly, and was prepared to extend the ceasefire, while warning that Russian violations would receive a proportional response. Ukraine’s General Staff alleged 469 violations after the ceasefire began, including 22 assaults, 153 shelling incidents, 19 kamikaze-drone strikes, and 275 FPV-drone strikes. Russian authorities accused Ukraine of drone strikes in Kursk and Belgorod that injured five people. The article says the Kyiv Independent could not verify either side’s claims.

evidence.title: Trump cautions Iran against charging tolls to go through Strait of Hormuz as fragile ceasefire holds - CBS News
evidence.text: Russia announced a 32-hour ceasefire over Orthodox Easter, from 4:00 p.m. Saturday until the end of Sunday. President Vladimir Putin ordered Russian forces to cease hostilities in all directions; the Kremlin called it a “humanitarian” pause and said it assumed Ukraine would follow Russia’s example. President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine had proposed an Easter ceasefire and would reciprocate. The Kremlin said the pause had not been discussed with Ukraine or the United States beforehand. The article reports an announced, short truce—not that it had taken effect or held. It also says Russia has rejected a longer-term unconditional ceasefire, previous truces drew accusations of hundreds of violations, and US-brokered peace talks have been effectively frozen since late February amid unresolved territorial disputes.

evidence.title: Fact-checking Trump and Hegseth's claims of U.S. 'victory' in the Iran war - PBS

The article says previous ceasefire attempts had little impact, with both sides alleging violations. The Kremlin said the pause would run from 4 p.m. Moscow time on Saturday until midnight Sunday; Russia’s defence minister instructed forces to halt operations, while remaining ready to respond to violations. Zelenskyy said Ukraine had proposed an Easter pause and would reciprocate. The article does not give calendar dates for the truce. It reports that broader peace talks remain stalled and that a similar short pause last year drew accusations of violations from both sides.

evidence.title: Trump Renews Threat of Attacks on Iran’s Bridges and Power Plants - The New York Times
evidence.text: Ukraine and Russia appeared close to a 32-hour, theatre-wide ceasefire beginning Saturday afternoon for Orthodox Easter. It could be their first official ceasefire across the war theatre since Russia’s February 2022 full-scale invasion. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had repeatedly offered an Easter pause and was ready to reciprocate; Russian President Vladimir Putin acquiesced, and the Kremlin said it had ordered hostilities to stop “in all directions.” The Kremlin also said its troops should be ready to respond to provocations or attacks. The pause had not yet begun, and the article does not establish whether it would hold or extend beyond Easter. Earlier truces were described as unofficial, localized, or limited in scope.

Putin’s spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, ruled out an extension, saying the ceasefire was only temporary and “exclusively humanitarian.” The article does not establish that the truce took effect or held. Kyiv wants a full, stable ceasefire before peace negotiations, while Moscow insists on agreeing a peace deal first; US-mediated talks were on hold. The article also reports Ukrainian allegations of hundreds of violations during a previous Russian-declared ceasefire.
