market.question: Reckless Ben arrested by July 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Reckless Ben (a.k.a. Benjamin Schneider) is arrested between market creation and July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying arrest/detention includes:
* Being taken into physical custody by law enforcement authorities (including federal, state, local, military, or international law enforcement)
* Voluntarily surrendering to law enforcement authorities in response to an arrest warrant
* Being formally booked or processed following detention
* Being handcuffed by a state authority and taken to a police station
* Surrendering at a police station or courthouse with their attorney
* Being placed under house arrest or electronic monitoring

The following scenarios will NOT qualify as an arrest/detention
* An arrest warrant being issued but not executed
* Being briefly detained but not arrested (e.g. such as in the South Korean judicial system when an individual is awaiting a judge’s decision on whether to grant a detention warrant)
* Being questioned or interviewed without arrest
* Being named in an indictment without arrest

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the arresting government and law enforcement, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.question: Will Trump speak to Elon Musk in July?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual speaks with Donald Trump between July 1 and July 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Speaking is defined as any verbal interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be credible media reporting. However, in the absence of definitive or in the case of contradictory media reporting, statements by either of the specified individuals or their official representatives will also be considered.

Statements by the specified individuals or their official representatives will only be considered conclusive if the claims explicitly, or in context unambiguously, indicate that a qualifying talk occurred within the specified timeframe and took place via verbal communication, and provided that such claims are not contradicted by the other specified individual, their representatives, or credible media reporting by the end of the third calendar date (ET) following the statement in question.

This market will resolve at the earlier of i) a qualifying verbal interaction being confirmed under the above rules or ii) 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar day following this market's above-specified timeframe.

If the date and time of a qualifying talk cannot be confirmed by a consensus of credible reporting by 11:59 PM ET on the third calendar day following this market's above-specified timeframe, it will resolve to "No" regardless of whether it was later confirmed to have taken place.

market.question: Will Russia and Ukraine hold any diplomatic meeting by August 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of Russia and Ukraine by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding Russia-Ukraine relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count.

The meeting must be in-person (including indirect in-person meetings) and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine, and a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Zelenskyy-Trump meeting at White House will focus on peace talks - CNN - ukranews.com
evidence.text: Ukrainian negotiator Sergiy Kyslytsya says U.S.-mediated official negotiations between Russia and Ukraine have stalled since early this year, while the Trump administration has focused on the U.S. war on Iran. He says Ukraine still talks with American and occasionally Russian envoys, describing the dialogue as “active and ongoing.” Kyslytsya has been on Ukraine’s negotiating team since 2025. In June, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed face-to-face talks with Vladimir Putin; Putin said the following month that he saw no point in such a meeting. Kyslytsya considers a meeting possible later this year, but the article reports no meeting scheduled by August 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Volodymyr Zelensky, Donald Trump discuss new peace push as war with Russia rages on - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: Ukraine and the US are trying to restart peace talks with Russia. After speaking with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to travel to Moscow in late July or early August to continue discussions. The article says Washington is revising a negotiating framework and will coordinate proposals with Kyiv before presenting them to Moscow. That planned trip is a US–Russia discussion, not a confirmed Russia–Ukraine meeting. Zelensky said a trilateral meeting could happen as early as the fall, but the article describes it as involving “the US, Ukraine, and Zelensky,” without clearly identifying Russian participation. Russia has said new US proposals must be acceptable to it, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio said new ideas are needed to begin Russia–Ukraine peace talks.

evidence.title: What's in the EU's 21st package of sanctions against Russia - Reuters
evidence.text: Ukraine and the U.S. are coordinating revised peace proposals for Moscow after negotiations stalled earlier in 2026. U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have no current plans to visit Kyiv, but officials expect them to travel to Russia in late July or early August after aligning positions with Ukraine. Presidents Zelensky and Trump are also preparing to meet and may discuss another attempt to arrange direct talks between Zelensky and Putin. The Kremlin has consistently rejected meetings in a neutral country and insisted Zelensky travel to Russia, which Kyiv views as a way to avoid direct talks. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on July 23 that Russia remains open to negotiations. The article describes a renewed diplomatic effort, but reports no scheduled Russia–Ukraine meeting by August 31, 2026.

evidence.title: U.S. thwarts Iranian missile attack on U.S. troops, strikes Iranian proxies in Iraq with Saudi forces - CBS News
evidence.text: Previous U.S.-led mediation efforts between Russia and Ukraine stalled over Ukrainian territory claimed by Russia. Zelenskyy spoke last week with Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about ways to “reinvigorate diplomacy,” after the Middle East war pushed Ukraine negotiations lower on Washington’s agenda. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied Monday that negotiations on an aerial ceasefire were underway. Zelenskyy said Ukraine, Trump and European countries wanted the war to end, but Putin did not. The article reports no scheduled Russia-Ukraine diplomatic meeting.

The article says US-led efforts to end the war had stalled, with previous mediation foundering over Ukrainian territory claimed by Russia. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied on Monday that talks on an aerial ceasefire were underway. The article reports no scheduled Russia–Ukraine diplomatic meeting.

evidence.title: White House says Trump, Zelenskiy to meet in Washington next week - Reuters

market.question: Will Russia and Ukraine hold any diplomatic meeting by August 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a diplomatic meeting between representatives of Russia and Ukraine by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting refers to a deliberate meeting between representatives of the listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in negotiation or diplomacy regarding Russia-Ukraine relations on behalf of their governments. Meetings conducted indirectly, for example, through designated mediators, facilitators, or interlocutors acting with the knowledge and authorization of the relevant governments, will qualify. 

Brief greetings, chance encounters, or talks otherwise not deliberately aimed at diplomacy or negotiation will not count.

The meeting must be in-person (including indirect in-person meetings) and must be publicly acknowledged by either government or reported by a consensus of credible media. Remote meetings, phone calls, or other meetings where the relevant parties are not present will not count.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Michigan are scheduled to be held on August 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Michigan Democratic Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two candidates receive the exact same highest number of valid votes and both are listed, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket for the tied candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically. If only one of the tied candidates is listed, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket for that listed candidate. If neither tied candidate is listed, this market will resolve to “Other.”

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the count has been made official.

If the results of the specified election are not known definitively by November 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the State of Michigan, such as official statewide results published by the Michigan Secretary of State (https://www.michigan.gov/sos); however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Michigan are scheduled to be held on August 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the first round of the Michigan Democratic Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher margin bracket.

If two candidates receive the exact same highest number of valid votes and both are listed, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket for the tied candidate whose last name comes first alphabetically. If only one of the tied candidates is listed, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket for that listed candidate. If neither tied candidate is listed, this market will resolve to “Other.”

Stevens, backed by Sen. Chuck Schumer and the party establishment, led non-college-educated voters by 22 points and Black voters by 46; El-Sayed, endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, led college-educated voters by seven points and White voters by 12.

market.question: Will Peggy Flanagan win the Minnesota Senate Democratic primary by 15–20%?
market.resolution_criteria:
Primary elections in Minnesota are scheduled to be held on August 11, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Senate Primary.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

market.question: Iran successfully targets shipping on August 17, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Iranian forces conduct a kinetic strike on or seize control of a commercial ship on the specified date IRST (UTC +3:30). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Attacks on military vessels will not be considered.

Only military actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory or been carried out by Iranian forces will count toward the resolution of this market. Attacks by proxy forces (i.e. Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count toward the resolution of this market.

Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to Iranian forces forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by Iranian operatives in person, such as seizing a ship by force.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

If a kinetic incident occurs, but, on the specified date, 11:59 PM IRST, material ambiguity remains as to the exact timing of the incident, or whether the incident can be attributed to Iran, this market may remain open for an additional 3 calendar days, IRST. If, at such time, the attribution or timing of the incident still cannot be confirmed, this market will resolve to “No”.

market.question: Iran successfully targets shipping on August 17, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Iranian forces conduct a kinetic strike on or seize control of a commercial ship on the specified date IRST (UTC +3:30). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Attacks on military vessels will not be considered.

Only military actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory or been carried out by Iranian forces will count toward the resolution of this market. Attacks by proxy forces (i.e. Hezbollah, Houthis, etc.) will not count toward the resolution of this market.

Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to Iranian forces forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by Iranian operatives in person, such as seizing a ship by force.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

If a kinetic incident occurs, but, on the specified date, 11:59 PM IRST, material ambiguity remains as to the exact timing of the incident, or whether the incident can be attributed to Iran, this market may remain open for an additional 3 calendar days, IRST. If, at such time, the attribution or timing of the incident still cannot be confirmed, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Iranian forces conduct a kinetic strike on or seize control of a commercial ship on the specified date IRST (UTC +3:30). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only military actions by Iranian forces explicitly claimed by the Islamic Republic of Iran or confirmed to have originated from Iranian territory or been carried out by Iranian forces will count toward the resolution of this market. Missile/drone strikes targeting a ship that are intercepted or otherwise do not directly impact the vessel will not be considered, regardless of damage through debris.

Seize control refers to Iranian forces forcefully boarding and taking control of a commercial ship.

Qualifying incidents include, but are not limited to, drone and missile strikes, aerial bombings, and kinetic actions carried out by Iranian operatives in person, such as seizing a ship by force.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Next OpenAI GPT Sol (5.7+) released by September 30, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI's next GPT Sol model (5.7+) is made available to the general public between market creation and the specified date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying model must have a name or model identifier that includes "GPT" and "Sol" and be designated as version 5.7 or higher, regardless of capitalization or surrounding prefixes, suffixes, dates, or descriptors. For example, a version 5.7 or higher named in the same manner as GPT-5.6 Sol would qualify, including a new whole-number generation such as GPT-6 Sol or an Astra-branded release meeting these criteria, while models whose name does not include "Sol" or which retain a version designation below 5.7, such as GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, or GPT-5.6 Luna, will not qualify. Fine-tunes, modes, or restricted-access variants of an existing version, such as GPT-5.6-Cyber or GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast, will not qualify.

A qualifying model must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must either be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as accessible to the general public, or otherwise be made publicly accessible and explicitly labeled on the company's official website. Labeling errors, placeholder text, or version names displayed on the website that do not correspond to a model that is actually accessible to the general public will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Next OpenAI GPT Sol (5.7+) released by September 30, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI's next GPT Sol model (5.7+) is made available to the general public between market creation and the specified date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying model must have a name or model identifier that includes "GPT" and "Sol" and be designated as version 5.7 or higher, regardless of capitalization or surrounding prefixes, suffixes, dates, or descriptors. For example, a version 5.7 or higher named in the same manner as GPT-5.6 Sol would qualify, including a new whole-number generation such as GPT-6 Sol or an Astra-branded release meeting these criteria, while models whose name does not include "Sol" or which retain a version designation below 5.7, such as GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, or GPT-5.6 Luna, will not qualify. Fine-tunes, modes, or restricted-access variants of an existing version, such as GPT-5.6-Cyber or GPT-5.6 Sol Ultrafast, will not qualify.

A qualifying model must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must either be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as accessible to the general public, or otherwise be made publicly accessible and explicitly labeled on the company's official website. Labeling errors, placeholder text, or version names displayed on the website that do not correspond to a model that is actually accessible to the general public will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will 3 Fed rate cuts happen in 2025?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the there are exactly 3 cuts of 25 basis points by the Fed's December meeting (including any cuts made during Dec meeting). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

This market may resolve to "Yes" immediately after the statement from the Fed's December 2025 meeting has been released if there has been exactly 3 rate cuts by then.

Note that cuts between 1-24 bps (inclusive) will also be considered 1 rate cut.

For example, if the FED cuts rates by 50 bps after a meeting, it would be considered 2 cuts (of 25 bps each). If there are 4 or more rate cuts at any point before this market's resolution date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be FOMC statements after meetings scheduled in 2025 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm. The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

evidence.title: Trump says US remains in pursuit of oil tanker and it’d be ‘smart’ for Maduro to step down - CNN
evidence.text: The article describes mounting pressure on Nicolás Maduro but does not report that he has left office or set a timetable for his departure in 2025. It says the Venezuelan opposition and U.S. government regularly invoke two arguments against his government: alleged links to terrorist groups and criminal networks, and claims that Maduro’s presidency is illegitimate because of accusations of fraud in the 2024 presidential election. The headline says President Donald Trump called it “smart” for Maduro to step down. The article also says Washington has recently emphasized Venezuelan oil, with Trump claiming that energy rights were taken from U.S. companies, while opposition leader María Corina Machado has promoted a vision for Venezuela beyond Chavismo.

evidence.title: Trump wants Venezuela’s leader to go. Here’s who could replace him. - San Juan Daily Star
evidence.text: The article says the Trump administration’s stated aim is to stop drugs and criminals entering the United States, but current and former officials privately say its ultimate goal is Nicolás Maduro’s departure. Trump has increased pressure through warships in the Caribbean, a claim that Venezuelan airspace is closed and suggestions of imminent strikes. Asked whether Maduro’s days as president were numbered, Trump said, “I would say yeah.” The New York Times has reported that the Pentagon drew up plans for potential military action in Venezuela, including an attempt by Special Operations forces to kill or capture Maduro. Maduro has tightened his security, according to people close to his government. His officials suggested this year that he might consider leaving office in 2027, while the Trump administration has pressed for a quicker resignation. The article reports plans and pressure, not a decision to carry out an operation or an agreement for Maduro to leave in 2025.

evidence.title: These Are The Six Figures Who Could Rule Venezuela If Maduro Steps Down or Is Forced Out - Latin Times
evidence.text: A report cited by the article says current and former U.S. officials have privately discussed replacing Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro as the real endgame of a U.S. military operation publicly described as targeting drug trafficking. Trump has hinted that Maduro’s days in office are numbered. The article does not report a decision to remove him or a timetable; it says any successor would depend on how he left power. It identifies six possible successors: Vice President Delcy Rodríguez, constitutionally first in line; Maduro allies Diosdado Cabello, Jorge Rodríguez and Gen. Vladimir Padrino López; and opposition figures María Corina Machado and Edmundo González. Experts cited in the article say González’s electoral win gives him the strongest legal claim, though his limited political network could complicate a transition.

evidence.title: Maduro says the real reason for Trump’s Venezuela fixation is oil – is he right? - theguardian.com
evidence.text: The article says Donald Trump “seems bent on regime change in Venezuela” amid a massive US military buildup in the Caribbean and a three-month campaign against Nicolás Maduro’s government. The US says its boat strikes, which have killed more than 80 people, target drug trafficking; Maduro says the real motive is Venezuela’s oil. The article also notes that Trump has reached understandings with other authoritarian leaders. Maduro reportedly offered US companies access to existing and future oil and gold projects during talks with US envoys, and Trump eased restrictions on Chevron in July. The article gives no date or concrete plan for Maduro’s removal in 2025.

evidence.title: Trump administration asking US oil industry to return to Venezuela — but getting no takers - Politico
evidence.text: As of December 18, 2025, the article refers to Nicolás Maduro’s government as governing Venezuela. It says the Trump administration contacted oil firms about a potential return to Venezuela *if* regime change occurred, but, according to Politico, received little interest. The article also reports US military pressure and threats toward Venezuela, while saying administration officials assured House Republicans that they did not plan to attack Venezuela and lacked a legal basis to do so. It reports no removal of Maduro.

evidence.title: Maduro Reportedly Asked To Keep $200 Million Of His Wealth To Relinquish Power In Venezuela - Latin Times
evidence.text: Reports of a November call between Nicolás Maduro and U.S. President Donald Trump describe negotiations over Maduro relinquishing power. Maduro reportedly sought to keep $200 million of his wealth, obtain amnesty for several officials and find safe harbor abroad. He also offered free elections while retaining control of Venezuela’s armed forces; Trump rejected that proposal. A third sticking point was Washington’s demand that Maduro resign immediately, which Caracas refused. Trump gave Maduro a week to leave Venezuela or risk forcible removal; the reported November 28 deadline passed. Maduro reportedly proposed that Vice President Delcy Rodríguez lead an interim government before elections. Another report said Maduro doubted he would receive lasting amnesty and believed the U.S. military campaign off Venezuela’s coast was a bluff.

evidence.title: US-Venezuela tensions: Your questions answered - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Trump confirmed on Sunday that he had spoken with Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro the previous week but did not disclose what they discussed. The Miami Herald reported that Trump offered to guarantee Maduro and his family safety if Maduro resigned immediately; the White House did not respond to a request for comment on that report. A separate report said U.S. officials had discussed sending Maduro to Qatar, but officials familiar with Qatar’s role said he would not go there, and no country had confirmed it would accept him. Sanctions, strikes near Venezuelan waters and a $50 million reward for information leading to Maduro’s arrest had not forced him from power. Cato Institute analyst Katherine Thompson said she saw few untried options short of military action, doubted its success, and saw little sign Maduro would accept a deal to leave.

evidence.title: Maduro asked for $200m in deal with Trump to flee - The Telegraph
evidence.text: Reuters reported that during a November 21 call, Trump offered Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro safe passage out of Venezuela. Maduro allegedly said he was willing to leave if he and his family received full legal amnesty, and reportedly sought the removal of sanctions on more than 100 Venezuelan officials. Trump rejected most of those requests but reportedly gave Maduro a week to leave with his family for a destination of his choice. Al Jazeera said it could not independently verify the report. Separately, Trump had not ruled out sending US troops into Venezuela, while Maduro publicly said he wanted peace with the US only on terms of sovereignty and equality.

evidence.title: Venezuela's president hasn’t surrendered as Trump shared - PolitiFact
evidence.text: The article describes Nicolás Maduro as still in power, not surrendered. It says Donald Trump has spent months pressuring Venezuela by attacking boats alleged to be smuggling drugs, massing naval forces and fighter jets in the Caribbean, demanding Maduro’s resignation and declaring Venezuela’s airspace closed. The author says Trump may hope these measures remove Maduro; if they do not, he appears poised to attack Venezuela directly, having told U.S. troops in a Thanksgiving address that strikes would start “very soon.” The article presents Maduro’s removal as uncertain: a conflict could leave him in power or force him out. It also notes that Trump’s first-term “maximum pressure” policy failed to break Maduro’s hold on power.

evidence.title: Nicolás Maduro, speaking to his supporters: ‘They will never be able to take us off the path of the revolution’ - english.elpais.com
evidence.text: As of December 2, 2025, Nicolás Maduro remained Venezuela’s president. An alleged ultimatum from Donald Trump giving Maduro and his family one week to leave Venezuela expired the preceding Friday without major incident. Reuters reported that Trump issued it after rejecting alleged demands for Maduro’s early exit, including lifting US sanctions, ending an International Criminal Court prosecution, and installing a transitional government led by Vice-President Delcy Rodríguez. Venezuelan officials had previously denied reports of negotiations involving Maduro stepping down; Caracas did not comment on the latest allegations. The article also reports continued US pressure, including Trump’s suggestion that strikes could begin on land, but no departure by Maduro.

evidence.title: Voters Oppose US Military Boat Strikes in Caribbean, Want Hegseth to Resign: Poll - Military.com
evidence.text: The article reports persistent speculation that the U.S. might enter Venezuela militarily to remove President Nicolás Maduro and/or seize oil, and says President Trump has alluded multiple times to a possible land war. It does not report a decision to invade or evidence that Maduro has been removed. The U.S. military began striking alleged drug-carrying boats in September; more than 20 vessel strikes had killed at least 90 people, including eight in three strikes announced on Dec. 15. In a Dec. 5–9 poll of 1,165 likely U.S. voters, only 37% called Maduro’s removal an administration priority, while 62% wanted the U.S. less involved in resolving foreign conflicts.

evidence.title: Maduro rejects a ‘slave’s peace’ for Venezuela as US ramps up pressure - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Maduro appeared at a Monday rally in Caracas after several days of rumors about his political fate and speculation about a negotiated exit. The speculation followed US President Donald Trump’s acknowledgment of a phone call with Maduro and reports of a possible US ultimatum. Maduro said his opponents would “never” take his movement off the path of revolution and described the preceding 22 weeks as a test. He swore in neighborhood-level government organizers and announced a new, 12-member political bureau to “accompany him in leading all social and political forces.” Its prominent members include Diosdado Cabello, Jorge Rodríguez, Delcy Rodríguez and Cilia Flores, whom Maduro presented and swore in. The article portrays the ruling movement as diminished but organized around Maduro, who showed no apparent intention of relinquishing power despite US pressure and disputes over his re-election.

evidence.title: Nicolas Maduro could end up in gas-rich Qatar under Trump pressure — as US weighs strikes in Venezuela’s waters - New York Post
evidence.text: Reuters reported, citing sources familiar with a November 21 call, that Trump offered Maduro safe passage out of Venezuela. Maduro reportedly said he would leave if he and his family received full legal amnesty, all US sanctions were removed, and an ICC case against him ended. He also sought sanctions relief for more than 100 Venezuelan officials. Trump reportedly rejected most requests but gave Maduro a week to leave with his family; sources said that offer expired on Friday. Neither government immediately commented on the report. Maduro appeared at a Caracas rally the following Monday, pledged loyalty to Venezuelans and rejected a “slave’s peace.”

evidence.title: Trump’s ultimatum to Maduro: “Leave the country now” - Salon.com
evidence.text: In a call thought to have taken place on 21 November 2025, Donald Trump reportedly told Nicolás Maduro to leave power and Venezuela immediately, offering safe passage for Maduro, his wife and his son if he resigned at once. Maduro reportedly refused, seeking a “global amnesty” for himself and allies; the article also says he sought worldwide immunity from prosecution and proposed ceding political control while retaining control of the armed forces. Trump confirmed the call occurred but did not describe its substance, and neither government provided further details. The article reports no agreement for Maduro to leave power in 2025.

evidence.title: How Venezuela’s Maduro became Washington’s most persistent hemispheric adversary - The Long War Journal
evidence.text: As of Dec. 1, 2025, Maduro remained in power. Trump confirmed a recent call with him but gave no account of its substance. Citing other outlets, the article says the call reached an impasse: Washington demanded that Maduro and his top allies leave Venezuela immediately to restore democratic rule, while regime leaders offered to hand political control to the opposition but keep command of the armed forces. The reported U.S. offer guaranteed safe passage for Maduro, his wife Cilia Flores, and his son only if he resigned immediately. Maduro reportedly also sought amnesty and a delayed departure; those requests and his proposal to retain military control were rejected. The article says it could not independently verify what was discussed. Trump was considering further options, but the article says U.S. forces in the region were not large enough for an invasion.

evidence.title: Trump reportedly gave Maduro ultimatum to relinquish power in Venezuela - theguardian.com
evidence.text: Trump reportedly told Nicolás Maduro during a call thought to have taken place on 21 November to leave Venezuela immediately, offering safe passage for Maduro, his wife and his son only if he resigned at once. Maduro reportedly refused and sought worldwide immunity from prosecution for himself and allies, along with permission to cede political control while retaining control of the armed forces. Neither government has provided details of the call. The Miami Herald reported no further direct contact, despite a subsequent request from Maduro for another call. Trump has mounted a four-month pressure campaign, including a large naval deployment, but observers cited in the article doubt he will use large-scale military force. The reported refusal and uncertainty over further action bear against an immediate departure.

evidence.title: Trump news at a glance: tensions with Venezuela rise after president’s reported ultimatum to Maduro - theguardian.com
evidence.text: Sources told the Miami Herald that, in a phone call last month, Trump pressed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro to leave “right away” and offered guarantees for his family only if he resigned on the spot. Maduro reportedly refused, instead seeking global amnesty and continued control of the armed forces even if he ceded political power. The paper reported no further communication, despite Maduro’s attempt to arrange another call. The White House has neither confirmed nor denied the ultimatum. US military pressure continues, while Maduro has publicly vowed to resist any attempt to force political change.

evidence.title: US Navy admiral ordered second deadly Venezuela boat strike, White House says - BBC
evidence.text: Trump confirmed on Sunday that he had a brief phone call with Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and pressured him to resign and leave Venezuela with his family. According to reports, the call took place the previous month: Trump offered Maduro a destination of his choosing if he left immediately, but Maduro refused. Trump later posted that Venezuelan airspace should be considered “closed in its entirety.” The BBC said it had not confirmed separate reports that Maduro sought amnesty for top aides and continued control of the military after leaving government, and that Trump rejected those demands. The US had expanded its military presence in the Caribbean, and Trump warned that efforts against Venezuelan drug trafficking “by land” would begin “very soon.” Venezuela’s government accused the US of seeking to topple it.

evidence.title: Venezuela’s Maduro spotted for first time in days, ending flight speculation - New York Post
evidence.text: Maduro, 63, appeared publicly on Sunday for the first time in five days, presenting prizes and speaking at an annual coffee awards ceremony in eastern Caracas, CNN reported. He led a chant calling Venezuela’s economy “indestructible, untouchable, unbeatable.” The appearance undercut speculation that he had fled; his previous reported sign of activity was a video posted Wednesday showing him driving in Caracas. The Miami Herald reported that Trump had offered Maduro, his wife and son safe passage if Maduro resigned immediately. It said Maduro’s administration instead offered to surrender political control while retaining control of the armed forces, leaving the talks at an impasse. Trump acknowledged a phone call with Maduro but would not characterize how it went.

evidence.title: Trump Confirms Phone Call With Maduro - twz.com
evidence.text: Trump confirmed a recent call with Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro but said he “wouldn’t say it went well or badly.” According to the Miami Herald, the call took place late in the week of November 16. Maduro sought global amnesty for himself and senior associates and continued control of Venezuela’s armed forces in exchange for allowing free elections. Washington reportedly rejected both proposals and demanded that he step down immediately, offering safe passage for Maduro, his wife Cilia Flores, their son, and several allies if he left. Caracas rejected the conditions, and the talks collapsed. Maduro’s government reportedly sought another call with Washington but received no response.

evidence.title: Trump gave Venezuelan dictator Maduro stern ultimatum — leave now or else: report - New York Post
evidence.text: According to the article, Washington offered Nicolás Maduro guaranteed evacuation from Venezuela with his wife, Cilia Flores, and their son if he resigned immediately, but Caracas refused. The reported talks also stalled over Maduro’s request for global amnesty for his group and a proposal to retain control of the armed forces in exchange for free elections. Trump subsequently said on Saturday that Venezuelan airspace should be considered closed, though on Sunday he cautioned reporters not to read that announcement as a sign of an imminent strike. The article reports pressure on Maduro, not that he has left office; it gives no explicit date for the reported call.

evidence.title: Venezuela denounces Trump’s airspace remarks as ‘colonialist threat’ - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The article reports that Trump and Nicolás Maduro spoke by phone late in the week of Nov. 16, but the talks broke down. According to a source cited by the Miami Herald, Maduro sought global amnesty for himself and his group and proposed retaining control of Venezuela’s armed forces in exchange for allowing free elections. Trump rejected both requests and demanded that Maduro resign immediately. Sources said Trump offered safe departure from Venezuela for Maduro, his wife and son if they left immediately. The article does not report that Maduro agreed or left office. It says Trump subsequently increased pressure, including warning that US military operations inside Venezuela could begin “very soon,” while a US senator said Trump would not put troops there.

evidence.title: US wargames played out scenarios for Maduro’s fall. None of them ended well for Venezuela - theguardian.com
evidence.text: The article says the Trump administration has escalated military pressure on Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro over several months, positioning a fleet of warships, the United States’ largest military carrier, and thousands of troops off Venezuela’s coast. It also reports Caribbean boat strikes that have killed over 80 people, and says Trump would not rule out sending troops into Venezuela. In a December 5–9, 2025 poll of 1,165 U.S. likely voters, 60% opposed sending troops to remove Maduro, 33% supported it, and 37% considered removing him at least somewhat of a priority. The article does not report that Maduro has left power or that a removal operation has been decided.

evidence.title: Trump gave Maduro ultimatum to flee Venezuela as land operations loom: report - Fox News
evidence.text: Trump confirmed in recent weeks that he authorised CIA secret operations in Venezuela, while his administration deployed the aircraft carrier USS Gerald R Ford, other warships, thousands of troops and F-35 stealth jets to the Caribbean. He said last Thursday that land strikes inside Venezuela could come imminently. The article also reports that Trump spoke with President Nicolás Maduro last week, and that on November 25 Trump said he might speak with him. Republican strategist Adolfo Franco said Trump wants Maduro to exit, peacefully if possible, but that negotiation could be difficult. Maduro, meanwhile, has called for peace and pledged to defend Venezuela against an attack. The article reports mounting pressure on him, not that he has left office.

evidence.title: Maduro ramps up repression in Venezuela as he faces growing threats abroad - CNN
evidence.text: In August, Washington offered a $50 million reward for information leading to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro’s arrest, doubling its previous offer. The article describes further US pressure: an aircraft carrier deployment to the Caribbean, deadly strikes on vessels the US accused of drug trafficking, and a US designation of the “Cartel de los Soles”—which Washington asserts is linked to Maduro—as a terrorist organisation. President Donald Trump also told airlines to consider Venezuelan airspace closed and said the US would soon target drug trafficking “by land.” A former US ambassador to Venezuela said Trump wants Maduro to leave office; experts cited in the article warned that Washington may be preparing to remove him unlawfully. Maduro said Venezuelans would not be intimidated. The New York Times reported that Trump and Maduro discussed a possible meeting, but that no meeting was planned.

evidence.title: Could Trump’s $50m reward succeed in toppling Venezuela’s Nicolas Maduro? - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Trump declined to state the goal of his four-month campaign against Venezuela while speaking on Air Force One en route to Florida; the article says many suspect it aims to overthrow Nicolás Maduro, who is widely believed to have stolen last year’s presidential election. Trump said he might speak with Maduro but warned that the US could do things “the easy way” or “the hard way.” Officially, the large US military deployment in the Caribbean targets drug trafficking. Maduro, meanwhile, urged supporters to defend “every inch” of Venezuela. A source in contact with senior Venezuelan officials said Maduro considers the US threats a bluff and believes ousting him would require troops in Caracas; the article calls a troop deployment highly unlikely. After more than 10 US strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats, observers suspect strikes on Venezuelan soil could follow. Analyst Douglas Farah warned that even an attack might fail to topple Maduro, as Trump failed to do in 2019.

evidence.title: The Reason Venezuela’s Maduro Won’t Resign Peacefully - WSJ
evidence.text: The US doubled its reward for information leading to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro’s arrest to $50 million in August. According to media reports, a US Department of Homeland Security agent then tried to recruit Maduro’s pilot, Bitner Villegas, apparently hoping he would deliver Maduro to US authorities. The attempt failed; Villegas instead appeared on Venezuelan state TV with Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello. A 2020 attempt by a former Green Beret and Venezuelan military defectors to spark an uprising also failed, leaving at least six dead and dozens arrested. Political scientist Alex Downes said he knew of no instance in which a bounty alone had brought about regime change. The article reports increased US military activity and high tensions, but no successful move to remove Maduro.

evidence.title: US slaps sanctions on Maduro family, Venezuelan tankers: What we know - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado told reporters in Oslo on Friday that Nicolás Maduro “will leave power, whether it is negotiated or not negotiated,” and said she was focused on an orderly, peaceful transition. She predicted that most Venezuelan military and police personnel would obey the elected civilian authority once a transition began. The article gives no deadline for his departure. It says the opposition maintains that Edmundo González, who replaced Machado on the ballot after she was barred from running, won the previous year’s July presidential election; Maduro continues to claim victory. The Trump administration was maintaining military pressure in the Caribbean, but experts warned that a transition would require careful negotiation with political and military officials. One analyst said patronage and corruption could make military officials reluctant to switch allegiance without amnesties.

evidence.title: ‘Maduro will leave power’: Machado vows Venezuela leadership change - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Trump’s administration has intensified pressure on President Nicolás Maduro, imposing sanctions on three nephews of Maduro’s wife, a Panamanian businessman, six shipping companies and six Venezuela-flagged oil tankers. The measures followed a US seizure of the tanker Skipper off Venezuela’s coast. The article describes the sanctions as a return to Trump’s “maximum pressure” strategy, aimed at dismantling financial networks supporting Maduro. Oil is a major vulnerability: fossil fuels account for up to 95 percent of Venezuela’s export earnings. Since September, US forces have also carried out at least 21 strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats, killing more than 80 people; political observers believe the aim is to drive Maduro from power. However, the article says sanctions may also have helped him remain in power by fostering an illicit oil trade that benefits loyal military and business elites. It reports no indication that Maduro has agreed to leave office in 2025.

evidence.title: What Was ‘Gran Colombia’ and Why do Petro and Maduro Want It Back? - ColombiaOne.com
evidence.text: UN-appointed investigators reported that Venezuela’s Bolivarian National Guard (GNB) used excessive force, including improper use of lethal weapons, during major protests in 2014, 2017, 2019 and 2024. They said the GNB has systematically repressed opponents of President Nicolás Maduro since 2014, including through arbitrary detention, torture and sexual violence, and played a key role in raids against opponents after the disputed 2024 presidential election. The investigators described structural impunity for GNB abuses. The article provides evidence of repression and opposition to Maduro, but does not say whether he will leave power in 2025.

evidence.title: Power shift in Venezuela? US prepares new phase of operations; speculation grows over Nicolás Maduro’s re - The Times of India
evidence.text: Four anonymous US officials told Reuters that the United States was preparing a new phase of operations targeting Venezuela in the coming days. Two said covert operations were expected to come first and that options under discussion could aim to push President Nicolás Maduro from power. The article does not say an operation to remove him has been approved or will succeed. It reports a months-long US military buildup near Venezuela, including the arrival of the USS Gerald R Ford and its strike group on November 16. Trump also expressed openness to talks with Maduro, while Maduro said he was ready for dialogue and that Venezuelans and the military would resist an attempt to unseat him.

evidence.title: Nobel Committee President Urges Maduro to Accept Election Results and Step Down - Curaçao Chronicle
evidence.text: Maduro remains in office after being declared the winner of last year’s presidential election, giving him a third six-year term. The article says the vote was widely dismissed internationally as neither free nor fair, and that polling-station tallies showed opposition candidate Edmundo González winning by a landslide. Opposition leader María Corina Machado says she and her team are ready to form a government and offered to discuss a peaceful transition with Maduro’s team, but “they rejected it.” Norwegian Nobel Committee chairman Jørgen Watne Frydnes said Maduro’s government has the power and responsibility to ensure a peaceful transition. The government has threatened Machado with arrest, and Venezuela’s attorney general said last month that she would be considered a fugitive if she travelled to Norway. The article reports mounting US pressure, including the seizure of a Venezuelan oil tanker on Wednesday, but no agreement or concrete path for Maduro to leave office in 2025.

evidence.title: Trump administration quietly builds plans for what would happen if Maduro were ousted in Venezuela - CNN
evidence.text: Internal U.S. documents reviewed by The Washington Post say Venezuela’s opposition is more prepared than U.S. officials had understood for a transition if President Nicolás Maduro is removed. Proposals drafted by opposition leader and 2025 Nobel Peace Prize recipient María Corina Machado call for task forces to stabilize Venezuela in the first 100 hours and 100 days after his departure, followed by elections within a year. An opposition military assessment estimates that about 20% of officers are firmly aligned with Maduro. The article reports a continuing U.S. military buildup in the Caribbean, but sources close to Maduro say he considers exile riskier than staying unless overthrow appears imminent. These are contingency plans, not a report that his departure has occurred or will occur in 2025.

evidence.title: Why the US action against Maduro recalls Panama — not Iraq - CNN
evidence.text: Machado says Maduro’s rule is ending and claims to have plans for the first 100 hours and 100 days after he leaves power, but she has not disclosed the details. The article says it remains unclear how the opposition could remove Maduro, who has ruled since 2013. Since August, Trump has built up US naval forces off Venezuela; the State Department has offered a $50 million reward for information leading to Maduro’s arrest, and the USS Gerald R Ford arrived in the Caribbean on Sunday. Nevertheless, there has been no sign of a split in Maduro’s regime, and Trump has not ordered further military action. Anticipated airstrikes did not occur. Trump said Monday that he would not rule out US ground troops, but also said he would probably talk with Maduro. The US plans to designate the alleged Maduro-linked Cartel of the Suns a foreign terrorist organization as of next Monday, a move that could provide a justification for an attack.

evidence.title: Is Venezuela prepared for a US attack as Washington ramps up forces? - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The USS Gerald R. Ford, pulled from the Mediterranean, arrived in the Caribbean on Sunday with more than 4,000 sailors and dozens of tactical aircraft, joining 15,000 U.S. service members already in the region. A U.S. military official said the “table is being set” for possible military action, and the U.S. had conducted 20 strikes on boats it said were carrying drugs from Venezuela. In August, the U.S. set a $50 million reward for Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro’s arrest. But officials told NPR the carrier’s arrival could be another pressure tactic rather than a prelude to an attack; Maduro had put his forces on high alert. Whether President Trump would use force against Venezuela remained unclear. On Friday, he said he had “sort of made up my mind” about an attack but would not disclose his decision.

evidence.title: Will Venezuela buckle under Trump? Maduro wouldn't be the first to fall - USA Today
evidence.text: Maduro remains in power in the article. He claims President Donald Trump’s real objective is to remove him through regime change and warns Venezuela would resist. Since early September, the US has struck at least 21 boats it says were trafficking drugs, killing at least 87 people; Trump has also authorized CIA operations inside Venezuela. He has given conflicting signals about strikes within the country. Analysts largely rule out a ground invasion and warn that even a limited strike could strengthen Maduro in the short term rather than produce a political transition. One analyst says Venezuela’s military and security forces are highly likely to fight, while another says the opposition lacks strong ties to them.

evidence.title: Trump Wants Venezuela's Maduro Out. Will He Pull the Trigger? - Time Magazine
evidence.text: The Trump administration has expanded a military campaign aimed in part at destabilizing Venezuela’s government, deploying an advanced US aircraft carrier to the Caribbean and considering strikes on land. It has developed options for military action in Venezuela, but Trump has not decided whether to proceed: the Justice Department has not issued updated legal guidance, and, according to the Wall Street Journal, he is uncertain about the most aggressive plan to oust President Nicolás Maduro. Trump said on 15 October that he had authorized CIA covert action in Venezuela. On Thursday, the Senate rejected a resolution requiring congressional approval for strikes in Venezuela, 49–51; only two Republicans supported it.

evidence.title: U.S. Officials Reportedly Modeled Maduro's Fall in a War Game: It Resulted In a Violent Power Struggle in Venezuela - Latin Times
evidence.text: The article reports that the Trump administration is intensifying military operations around Venezuela and signaling that a policy shift could include direct pressure on Nicolás Maduro to leave office. Trump called Maduro an “outlaw” and said he would not rule out a ground invasion over alleged drug trafficking. Since early September, U.S. forces have conducted more than 20 strikes on boats near Venezuela’s coast, killing at least 80 people, according to the article. Former Venezuelan officer José Antonio Colina said soldiers would not sacrifice themselves for Maduro and argued that U.S. military action would cause the armed forces to withdraw support. Exiled officers quoted in late October described the military as having roughly one-third operational capacity. The article does not report that Maduro has left office or give a date for his departure; a U.S. war game conducted during Trump’s first term instead warned that his fall could lead to a prolonged, violent struggle for power.

market.question: GTA VI released in 2025?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if it Grand Theft Auto VI is officially released in the US by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Rockstar Games or its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.

evidence.title: GTA 6 Is Officially Coming in 2026: The New Date, the Delays and the South African Reality Check - Memeburn
evidence.text: Rockstar announced that GTA VI was delayed to November 19, 2026, saying it needed more polish to meet fans’ standards. The announcement came days after Rockstar fired 31 GTA VI developers in late October 2025. The article says the delay pushed the planned launch back six months, so it does not support a 2025 release.

evidence.title: GTA Online A Safehouse in the Hills Release Time - Everything New In The Update - International Business Times UK
evidence.text: The article says Grand Theft Auto 6 had already been delayed twice and, as of its writing, was scheduled for release on November 19, 2026—not in 2025. Some fans feared another delay into 2027 or later, but the article says there was no indication that the November 2026 date had changed.

evidence.title: 'It's a deeply concerning case' UK Prime Minister comments on GTA 6 firings - GameRant
evidence.text: The article does not report a 2025 release for GTA VI. It says the new release date is November 2026, after a previously announced May 2026 date was delayed. A GameRant writer predicts the game may not release until 2027, but the article presents that as skepticism, not a confirmed delay.

evidence.title: "Deeply Concerning": The UK Prime Minister Just Put Rockstar Games on Notice - GTA BOOM
evidence.text: The article says Grand Theft Auto 6 was delayed again and is now set to arrive on November 19, 2026. That stated release date does not support a 2025 release.

evidence.title: Rockstar Games Launcher Update 1.0.105.2730 Notes - Rockstar Games
evidence.text: The article says GTA VI did not release in 2025. Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick, whose company is Rockstar’s parent, said in August that his “level of conviction is very, very high” about a May 2026 release. This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI shifts from its current capped-profit corporation structure to a for-profit model by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Any form of fully for-profit organization—including a Benefit Corporation (B-Corp), Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), or a modification to its existing structure to remove profit caps—will suffice for a "Yes" resolution.

If the OpenAI non-profit relinquishes control over the for-profit business, this will also qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

An announcement indicating that OpenAI is merely considering the shift will not suffice; the change must officially occur.

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.title: ChatGPT owner OpenAI hits $644 billion valuation, making it world’s most valuable start-up - The Straits Times
evidence.text: As of Oct 2, 2025, OpenAI was negotiating with Microsoft to convert into a more traditional for-profit company; the article does not say the conversion had been completed. The planned structure would give OpenAI’s existing non-profit entity control over a new public benefit corporation. OpenAI was founded as a non-profit in 2015, and co-founder Elon Musk has sued to stop the overhaul. The talks coincided with an employee share sale valuing OpenAI at US$500 billion (S$644 billion), up from US$300 billion earlier in 2025.

evidence.title: OpenAI restructure: nonprofit to take $100bn stake in public benefit corporation, Microsoft revenue share potentially diminished - Data Center Dynamics
evidence.text: OpenAI said it was getting closer to restructuring, but the article does not say the change was completed or give a firm 2025 completion date. OpenAI already has a for-profit subsidiary, OpenAI LLC, under a nonprofit parent, with investors’ returns capped. Under the revised plan, the subsidiary would become a public benefit corporation (PBC) and the cap would be removed, making it more appealing to backers. The nonprofit would remain in control and receive a stake worth more than US$100 billion. Governance details remained unsettled; California and Delaware attorneys-general were reviewing the changes, and OpenAI and Microsoft had announced a non-binding agreement in September while working toward final terms.

evidence.title: OpenAI’s nonprofit parent company secures $100B equity stake while retaining control of AI giant - Fox Business
evidence.text: OpenAI said on Thursday that its nonprofit parent would retain control of the company and gain an equity stake worth more than $100 billion. The recapitalization would allow OpenAI to raise capital. The article says OpenAI abandoned its plan to move away from a nonprofit structure and become a for-profit company in May. Its nonprofit oversees and controls an existing for-profit entity, which OpenAI converted into a public benefit corporation. CEO Sam Altman said that arrangement would not change.

evidence.title: OpenAI secures Microsoft’s blessing to transition its for-profit arm - TechCrunch
evidence.text: OpenAI announced on Thursday that it had reached a nonbinding agreement with Microsoft, its largest investor, on a revised partnership that would allow OpenAI to convert its existing for-profit arm into a public benefit corporation (PBC). Board chairman Bret Taylor said OpenAI’s nonprofit would remain in control and receive a stake in the PBC worth more than $100 billion. The companies are still working on a definitive agreement, and the transition requires clearance from state regulators, including in California and Delaware. The article does not say the conversion has occurred or give a completion date in 2025.

market.question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

evidence.title: Tracking Trump and Latin America: Trade—Tariffs Threatened on Mexico over Water Sharing - AS/COA
evidence.text: Trump told reporters he would impose “severe tariffs” on Canadian fertilizer if needed to bolster the U.S. fertilizer industry; the article reports no plan to lower tariffs on Canada by December 31. Saskatchewan producers argue that U.S. farmers depend on Canadian potash and that fertilizer tariffs would raise farmers’ costs, strain supply chains, and increase food prices. About half of Saskatchewan’s potash production goes to the United States. The article says the U.S. produces about 400,000 metric tons of potash annually but imports millions of tons more from Canada, and an expert says it could not quickly expand domestic capacity tenfold. Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe called for calm and said the goal should be free, fair, open trade.

evidence.title: If Trump tariffs fertilizer, U.S. lacks reserves ‘to meet domestic demand’ - Global News
evidence.text: Trump has already lowered U.S. tariffs on Canadian fertilizer and energy products after pushback from U.S. agriculture groups and Republican lawmakers in farming states such as Iowa. Canadian fertilizer exports exceeding CUSMA limits now face a 10% tariff, versus 25% on most other non-CUSMA exports. However, Trump said Monday that he might impose “very severe” tariffs on Canadian fertilizer to bolster U.S. production. Fertilizer Canada warned that U.S. farmers depend on Canadian potash: Canada supplied 79% of U.S. potash imports from 2020 to 2023, and the U.S. lacks sufficient reserves to meet domestic demand. The article reports no commitment to lower tariffs further by December 31.

evidence.title: Trump threatens ‘severe’ tariffs on Canadian fertilizer ‘if we have to’ - Global News
evidence.text: Earlier this year, Trump imposed a blanket 25% tariff on Canadian goods but lowered the fertilizer tariff to 10% after objections from industry groups and Republican lawmakers from farming states, including Iowa Sen. Chuck Grassley. The fertilizer tariff applies only to exports above limits under the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement. Many U.S. farmers rely on Canadian potash, and Canadian and U.S. farmers reported higher fertilizer bills in March. More recently, however, Trump said he might impose “very severe tariffs” on Canadian fertilizer to bolster U.S. production. The article reports a past, product-specific tariff reduction, but no plan to lower tariffs on Canada by December 31.

evidence.title: Export beef trade starts to react to Trump’s surprise Brazil tariff decision - Beef Central
evidence.text: Trump rolled back tariffs on dozens of food items earlier this month and has signalled openness to lowering tariffs on metals imported from Canada and Mexico if conditions on shifting production to the US are met. Before US–Canada talks stalled last month over an Ontario anti-tariff ad, Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney were discussing a metals-and-energy deal that Canadian officials hoped would ease tariffs on steel and aluminium. Talks have not formally progressed since the pause, though Carney said he and Trump exchanged texts Tuesday and could meet when Carney visits Washington next week. The US currently imposes a 35% levy on Canadian goods, with most exempt under an existing free trade agreement, plus sector-specific levies of 50% on metals and 25% on automobiles. Public hearings on the US–Canada–Mexico free trade agreement are expected in early December.

evidence.title: Trump unveils eased fuel economy rules, touts boost for affordability - The Detroit News
evidence.text: At a hearing ahead of the USMCA review, which formally begins July 1, 2026, U.S. Chamber of Commerce senior vice-president Neil Herrington urged the Trump administration to restore the agreement’s duty-free access by removing tariffs currently imposed on Canada and Mexico under Section 232. Those national-security-based tariffs include levies on steel, aluminum, cars and lumber; Canada’s industry minister said 50% steel tariffs have disrupted Canadian suppliers to U.S. automakers. The article reports no Trump decision to lower tariffs by December 31. It notes competing pressure: the Steel Manufacturers Association urged keeping Section 232 tariffs, while Trump’s trade representative discussed revising or exiting USMCA.

evidence.title: U.S. industry groups strongly back renewing CUSMA - CBC
evidence.text: After Trump raised tariffs on Canada and Mexico this year, the article says the rates remain subject to negotiation downward. Goods that do not comply with USMCA rules currently face a 35% tariff from Canada and 25% from Mexico, except Canadian energy resources, which face 10%. The White House estimated in March that 38% of Canadian imports qualified for USMCA treatment, but Canada’s realized average tariff rate was just 5% in August, suggesting more imports entered tariff-free under the agreement. The article reports no decision or timetable for lowering Canada’s tariff rates by December 31.

evidence.title: Trump's trade war with China in 2025 - The Straits Times
evidence.text: An Oct. 17 executive order gave the U.S. Department of Commerce discretion to reduce tariffs on qualifying steel and aluminum imports from Canada and Mexico by up to half—from 50% to no lower than 25%. Companies must apply, show they are expanding U.S. production, and supply metal for U.S. auto manufacturing; reduced-rate imports are limited to the amount of newly committed U.S. capacity. No company had received an exemption at the time of the article. The measure offers a possible route to limited relief by December 31, not an announced across-the-board tariff cut for Canada.

evidence.title: Twenty-nine ways Trump has changed Canada - The Globe and Mail
evidence.text: Trump has already exempted USMCA-compliant Canadian products from his blanket tariffs. USMCA replaced NAFTA in 2020; the exemption has prompted Canadian businesses to seek certification. Without it, the article says duties are generally 35%, or 10% for key resources. Most Canadian exports now cross the U.S. border duty-free, but tariffs on some products and industries reach 50%, including aluminum. Canada rolled back most of its countertariffs by early September to restart stalled trade talks. The article reports no agreement to lower the remaining U.S. tariffs and says Trump has threatened to end USMCA ahead of the trade deal’s review next year.

evidence.title: White House Says It Will Make Some SNAP Payments After Trump Threatened to Defy Court - The New York Times
evidence.text: Trump terminated trade talks with Canada in late October over an advertisement airing there that featured former President Ronald Reagan speaking negatively about tariffs; Trump called it “fraudulent.” The article says Trump imposed a 25% tariff on Canadian imports in February under emergency powers, then paused it. The Supreme Court is considering whether he had authority to impose tariffs under those powers, but the timing of its decision is unclear. A trade lawyer said that, even if the court rules against the tariffs, the administration could seek other legal authority to reinstate them.

evidence.title: Trump opens door to easing some steel and aluminum tariffs - The Globe and Mail
evidence.text: On February 1, Trump imposed a 25% punitive duty on goods from Canada and Mexico, alongside a 10% duty on Chinese goods, to press for curbs on fentanyl and illegal immigration into the United States. The article, updated November 19, reports no subsequent reduction of the Canadian duty or plan to lower it by December 31.

evidence.title: Trump drops tariffs on beef, coffee, tropical fruits amid consumer concerns - Global News
evidence.text: Trump signed an executive order on Friday removing tariffs on products including beef, coffee and tropical fruits by amending his April 2 global “reciprocal” tariff order. The amendments do not apply to his separate fentanyl-related tariff order for Canada, Mexico and China. Both that order and the global tariffs face a U.S. Supreme Court challenge, with a ruling expected by the end of the year. The article reports no decision to lower the Canada-specific tariffs.

evidence.title: Almost Half of U.S. Imports Now Have Steep Tariffs - The New York Times
evidence.text: Trump imposed tariffs of at least 10% on imports from most countries last April. Imports from Canada and Mexico were taxed at 25%, and Canada’s rate was later raised to 35%. The article reports no plan by Trump to lower Canada’s tariff by December 31. It does describe a pending Supreme Court case over his authority to impose the tariffs: lower courts ruled that he exceeded his authority, while his administration is defending the tariffs.

evidence.title: Trump Decreases Tariffs on Chinese Goods, Increases Tariffs on Canadian Goods, and Announces a Flurry of Trade Arrangements - Dorsey & Whitney
evidence.text: As of October 2025, Canadian goods faced U.S. tariffs of up to 35%, and Canada had matched many with its own levies. The article says Trump showed little urgency to negotiate, recently remarking that Canada might face “just a tariff, not really a negotiation.” Talks had been halted after an Ontario ad criticized his tariff policy. The article describes limited U.S. political and business pressure to resolve the dispute, although some industries and tourism were affected. It characterizes the situation as a stalemate, making a near-term tariff reduction appear less likely, while noting that sustained economic or voter pressure could change Trump’s position.

Qatar’s emir said the strike was intended to derail ceasefire negotiations; Israel said it would continue to pursue Hamas leaders wherever they were. Visiting Jerusalem afterward, US secretary of state Marco Rubio did not discuss ceasefire terms.
