Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appeared to endorse the plan, but Trump said its success still depended on Hamas’s cooperation. Hamas had not agreed; after Qatar’s prime minister and Egypt’s intelligence chief shared the plan with Hamas negotiators later Monday, they said they would review it in good faith and respond. The proposal calls for all Israeli hostages in Gaza to be released within 72 hours of Israel’s acceptance, in exchange for the release of more than 2,000 Palestinian prisoners. It would suspend military operations and freeze battle lines pending a staged Israeli withdrawal. Trump said Israel would have his backing to continue its campaign if Hamas rejected the terms, and Netanyahu said Israel could restart operations if Hamas refused or broke the deal.

evidence.title: Here Is the Full Text of the Gaza Plan Released by the White House (Published 2025) - The New York Times
evidence.text: In 2025, Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced a 20-point Gaza plan calling for a ceasefire, an exchange of Hamas-held hostages for Palestinian prisoners, a staged Israeli withdrawal, Hamas disarmament and transitional governance. Netanyahu said he supported the plan, but Hamas had not been consulted and its position remained uncertain. Hamas official Mahmoud Mardawi said the group had not even received the plan when it was announced; Qatari and Egyptian mediators reportedly presented it to Hamas on Monday evening. Trump said all remaining hostages would be released within 72 hours if Hamas accepted. Trump and Netanyahu warned that Israel would continue its campaign if Hamas rejected or undermined the plan. The article notes that previous US-backed ceasefire efforts had failed over differences between Israel and Hamas.

evidence.title: Here’s the full text of Trump’s 20-point plan to end Israel’s war on Gaza - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The White House’s 20-point Gaza proposal says the war would end immediately if both Israel and Hamas agree. It calls for Israeli forces to withdraw to an agreed line, military operations to be suspended, and hostages to be returned within 72 hours of Israel publicly accepting the agreement, followed by the release of Palestinian prisoners. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accepted US President Donald Trump’s plan. Hamas official Mahmoud Mardawi, however, told Al Jazeera that Hamas had not yet received a written Gaza peace plan. The article therefore reports a proposed ceasefire framework, not an agreement accepted by both sides.

evidence.title: Trump and Netanyahu to Hamas: accept Gaza peace plan or face consequences - The Guardian
evidence.text: At a Monday White House news conference, Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu backed a 20-point U.S. plan that would immediately end Israel’s war in Gaza, increase aid and require Hamas to release the remaining Israeli hostages. Netanyahu said he supported the plan because it “achieves our war aims” and called it a critical step toward ending the war. Hamas had not accepted the proposal and had resisted measures it contains, including a requirement to destroy its military infrastructure. Trump said he expected Hamas to accept, but that Israel would have his full backing to “finish the job” if it refused. The article reports a proposal, not an agreed ceasefire.

evidence.title: Rubio says Netanyahu has full support of US over plans to destroy Hamas - The Guardian
evidence.text: On 9 September 2025, Israel struck Hamas leadership in residential buildings in Doha, Qatar; Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office confirmed the Israeli military carried out the attack. The strike killed at least six people, including Hamas members and a Qatari security official, while Hamas negotiators were meeting to discuss a US-proposed ceasefire agreement. The article describes Qatar as a mediator in the conflict and reports that President Donald Trump disapproved of the strike, saying it did not advance Israel’s or America’s goals. It does not report that a ceasefire had been reached.

evidence.title: Unintended consequences of Israel’s strike on Qatar - ABC Religion & Ethics - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.text: Hamas leaders were in Doha discussing a ceasefire proposal from Donald Trump that matched Israel’s preference for a one-step deal releasing all 20 remaining hostages believed alive and the bodies of 28 believed dead. Hamas had accepted a phased ceasefire proposal along the lines put forward by US envoy Steve Witkoff in August. Israel then struck at Hamas leaders in Doha. Qatar’s emir said the strike was intended to derail ceasefire negotiations; Israel said it would continue to pursue Hamas leaders wherever they were. Visiting Jerusalem afterward, US secretary of state Marco Rubio did not discuss ceasefire terms. He said the US would continue seeking a peaceful outcome, but that it depended on eliminating Hamas and returning all 48 hostages, living and deceased. Israel was also preparing a ground offensive on Gaza City.

evidence.title: Israel attacks Hamas leadership in Qatar: What we know - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Hamas negotiators were meeting in Doha to consider the latest US ceasefire proposal when Israel struck a compound it said housed senior Hamas leaders. Qatar had been mediating ceasefire talks, and this was Israel’s first attack on Qatar, where Israeli negotiators had repeatedly visited for talks over the previous two years. Hamas said its targeted leadership survived, but six people were killed, including the son and an aide of senior leader Khalil al-Hayya. Qatar condemned the strike. Türkiye said targeting negotiators while talks continued showed Israel was not seeking an agreement; Israel said it had acted independently and took responsibility for the operation.

evidence.title: Israel Misses Its Own Deadline to Respond to Ceasefire Deal Accepted by Hamas - Truthout
evidence.text: As of late August 2025, Hamas had accepted a proposal for a temporary ceasefire and captive exchange, but Israel had missed its stated Friday, August 22 deadline to respond. Qatar Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said mediators were in contact with all parties but had received no official Israeli acceptance, rejection, or alternative proposal. The Qatar- and Egypt-mediated framework reportedly called for a 60-day pause, increased humanitarian aid, Hamas’s release of roughly half the remaining 50 Israeli captives, and Israel’s release of some Palestinian prisoners. Netanyahu’s office had instead insisted on the release of all Israeli captives. The article reports that Hamas made concessions on Israel’s presence along Gaza’s border with Egypt and on the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation. No ceasefire agreement had been reached at the time of the report.

evidence.title: Israel demands release of all Gaza hostages, casting doubt on ceasefire proposal - BBC
evidence.text: Israel said it would respond to international mediators by Friday to a new Gaza ceasefire proposal accepted by Hamas. Egypt and Qatar sent the proposal to Israel on Monday; Qatar said on Tuesday that it was almost identical to an earlier US-backed plan that Israel had previously agreed to. Reported terms envisage a 60-day ceasefire, with about half of the 20 remaining living Israeli hostages and some bodies released in phases in exchange for about 150 Palestinians held in Israeli jails. A major obstacle remains: Israeli officials say they want all hostages released in any deal, not a partial agreement, and Israel has threatened a new offensive to capture Gaza City. Mass protests in Israel demanding a hostage deal and mounting international pressure favour a truce, while Netanyahu’s far-right coalition allies oppose one.

evidence.title: Hamas accepts proposed deal for ceasefire with Israel and hostage release, Egyptian source says - Reuters
evidence.text: On Monday night, Hamas said it and other Palestinian factions had approved a ceasefire proposal presented by Egyptian and Qatari mediators to their delegations in Cairo the previous day. The proposed 60-day truce would release 10 living and 18 dead hostages in stages, in exchange for Palestinian prisoners and Gaza detainees; negotiations toward a permanent ceasefire would begin on its first day. Qatar said the proposal was 98% similar to a June US plan Israel had accepted. As of Tuesday afternoon, mediators had received no formal Israeli response. An Israeli official said Israel still demanded the release of all 50 hostages, while a government spokesman said it was not interested in partial deals. Israel had not explicitly rejected the proposal, but its position cast doubt on an agreement.

evidence.title: Hamas source says group agrees to latest Gaza ceasefire proposal - BBC
evidence.text: On Monday evening, a Hamas source told the BBC that the group had submitted a written response to mediators accepting the latest Gaza ceasefire proposal without amendments or conditions. The Egypt- and Qatar-mediated proposal reportedly calls for an initial 60-day truce, with Hamas releasing around half of the 50 remaining hostages in two batches and negotiations on a permanent ceasefire during the truce. Israel’s response was unclear: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office had said the previous week that it would accept a deal only if all hostages were released at once. Israel was also preparing to expand its Gaza offensive.

evidence.title: Hamas agrees to latest Gaza ceasefire proposal - France 24
evidence.text: Hamas said Monday it accepted a new Gaza ceasefire proposal from Egypt and Qatar without amendments. Egypt said the mediators had sent it to Israel, adding that “the ball is now in its court”; Israel had not responded. The reported proposal calls for an initial 60-day truce, the release of 10 Israeli hostages alive and some bodies, the release of some Palestinian prisoners, and provisions for aid to enter Gaza. An Islamic Jihad source said remaining captives would be released in a second phase, followed by talks on a broader settlement. The proposal comes after more than 22 months of war, but an agreement remains uncertain: Israel’s security cabinet had approved plans to expand operations into Gaza City, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the previous week that Israel would agree to a deal releasing all hostages at once under its conditions for ending the war.

evidence.title: Hamas accepts Gaza truce proposal as Israel signals will continue war - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Hamas said on Monday that it and other Palestinian factions accepted a Gaza ceasefire proposal from Qatari and Egyptian mediators; The Times of Israel and Channel 12 reported that Israel had received the response. A source familiar with the talks said the proposal called for a 60-day halt to military operations, Israeli troop relocation to allow humanitarian aid, and an exchange of half of the 50 Israeli captives for Palestinian prisoners. Acceptance does not establish that Israel has agreed: the article says Israel was proceeding with plans to seize Gaza City, while an Israeli minister opposed a ceasefire. The sides remain divided over duration—Hamas seeks a permanent end to the war, while Israel has sought a temporary truce. A prior truce began in January and ended in March; the latest indirect talks ended on July 25 without a result.

evidence.text: Weinstein is being held at Rikers Island while awaiting sentencing in September for a 2025 sexual assault conviction; the article does not report what sentence he will receive. evidence.title: Harvey Weinstein Recovering After Suffering Heart Failure in Prison - tmz.com
evidence.text: Harvey Weinstein was being held at the Queens jail complex awaiting sentencing in September for a 2025 sexual assault conviction. The article reports that a New York conviction that carried a 23-year sentence in 2020 was overturned in 2024, while a separate 2022 Los Angeles conviction carried a 16-year sentence. It also reports that Weinstein recently suffered heart failure due to pneumonia while incarcerated and is receiving treatment at Bellevue Hospital. The article does not state what sentence he will receive for the 2025 conviction.

evidence.title: Weinstein's New York rape charge dropped after accuser says she can't endure a 4th trial - PBS
evidence.text: Harvey Weinstein is awaiting sentencing in New York this fall on convictions from his retrials. Manhattan prosecutors decided on June 25 not to pursue a fourth rape trial after accuser Jessica Mann said she would not testify again. Separately, a California appeals court affirmed Weinstein’s 2022 Los Angeles sexual-assault conviction but vacated his 16-year prison sentence and ordered resentencing because the judge had relied on his now-overturned 2020 New York conviction as an aggravating factor. The article estimates his new California sentence will be 12 to 14 years, though his team plans to seek further review.

evidence.title: Appeals Court Orders Harvey Weinstein Resentencing, Though Conviction Stands - The Hollywood Reporter
evidence.text: Weinstein awaits sentencing in New York for a conviction on one count of criminal sexual act against former Project Runway assistant Miriam Haley. Prosecutors said they will seek a 20-year prison term. A judge dismissed a separate third-degree rape charge after prosecutors declined to pursue a fourth trial. Separately, a California appeals court upheld Weinstein’s rape conviction but vacated his 16-year sentence and ordered resentencing because the prior New York conviction used in setting that sentence had been overturned. The article does not report a new sentence.

evidence.title: Prosecutors drop Harvey Weinstein's New York rape charge - CBS News
evidence.text: Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said his office recommended that Harvey Weinstein be sentenced to 20 years in prison for his class B felony conviction involving the sexual assault of Miriam Haley. The recommendation is not a sentence imposed by the court. Prosecutors are dropping a separate, unresolved rape charge involving Jessica Mann rather than pursuing a fourth trial. The article also says Weinstein was sentenced to 16 years in a separate Los Angeles case, to be served after his New York sentence.

evidence.title: Weinstein’s Rape Charge Dismissed After N.Y. Prosecutors Forgo 4th Trial - The New York Times
evidence.text: New York prosecutors dropped a third-degree rape charge against Harvey Weinstein after juries twice failed to reach a verdict on Jessica Mann’s allegation. But Weinstein was convicted at a June 2025 retrial of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley, a former “Project Runway” production assistant. Prosecutors said Thursday they will ask Judge Curtis Farber to sentence him to 20 years in prison for that conviction; Weinstein’s lawyers will seek a lower sentence. His original 23-year New York sentence was overturned in 2024, but he has remained in custody and is also serving a separate 16-year sentence for a Los Angeles rape conviction.

evidence.title: Prosecutors Dismiss Rape Charge Against Harvey Weinstein, Who Won’t Be Tried a Fourth Time - The Hollywood Reporter
evidence.text: Manhattan prosecutors dismissed the rape charge involving Jessica Mann after she declined to testify again, allowing sentencing to move forward on Weinstein’s 2025 conviction for a criminal sexual act against former Project Runway assistant Miriam Haley. The DA’s office recommends 20 years in prison for that count, which carries a maximum of 25 years. Judge Curtis Farber had delayed sentencing while the Mann proceedings continued. Weinstein’s spokesperson said the defense expects to challenge the recommendation. Weinstein has also served less than half of a separate 16-year California prison sentence.

evidence.title: Harvey Weinstein Rape Case Dropped After Second Hung Jury - Bloomberg Law News
evidence.text: New York prosecutors said they would drop an unresolved rape charge against Harvey Weinstein rather than try him a fourth time, after juries deadlocked twice. He remains convicted of another sexual felony in New York and of crimes in California, and the article says he will stay behind bars. Prosecutors recommended a 20-year prison sentence for the crimes of which he was convicted.

Manhattan prosecutors decided on June 25 not to pursue a fourth rape trial after accuser Jessica Mann said she would not testify again. Separately, a California appeals court affirmed Weinstein’s 2022 Los Angeles sexual-assault conviction but vacated his 16-year prison sentence and ordered resentencing because the judge had relied on his now-overturned 2020 New York conviction as an aggravating factor. The article estimates his new California sentence will be 12 to 14 years, though his team plans to seek further review.

evidence.title: Appeals Court Orders Harvey Weinstein Resentencing, Though Conviction Stands - The Hollywood Reporter
evidence.text: Weinstein awaits sentencing in New York for a conviction on one count of criminal sexual act against former Project Runway assistant Miriam Haley. Prosecutors said they will seek a 20-year prison term. A judge dismissed a separate third-degree rape charge after prosecutors declined to pursue a fourth trial. Separately, a California appeals court upheld Weinstein’s rape conviction but vacated his 16-year sentence and ordered resentencing because the prior New York conviction used in setting that sentence had been overturned. The article does not report a new sentence.

evidence.title: Prosecutors drop Harvey Weinstein's New York rape charge - CBS News
evidence.text: Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said his office recommended that Harvey Weinstein be sentenced to 20 years in prison for his class B felony conviction involving the sexual assault of Miriam Haley. The recommendation is not a sentence imposed by the court. Prosecutors are dropping a separate, unresolved rape charge involving Jessica Mann rather than pursuing a fourth trial. The article also says Weinstein was sentenced to 16 years in a separate Los Angeles case, to be served after his New York sentence.

evidence.title: Weinstein’s Rape Charge Dismissed After N.Y. Prosecutors Forgo 4th Trial - The New York Times
evidence.text: New York prosecutors dropped a third-degree rape charge against Harvey Weinstein after juries twice failed to reach a verdict on Jessica Mann’s allegation. But Weinstein was convicted at a June 2025 retrial of sexually assaulting Miriam Haley, a former “Project Runway” production assistant. Prosecutors said Thursday they will ask Judge Curtis Farber to sentence him to 20 years in prison for that conviction; Weinstein’s lawyers will seek a lower sentence. His original 23-year New York sentence was overturned in 2024, but he has remained in custody and is also serving a separate 16-year sentence for a Los Angeles rape conviction.

evidence.title: Prosecutors Dismiss Rape Charge Against Harvey Weinstein, Who Won’t Be Tried a Fourth Time - The Hollywood Reporter
evidence.text: Manhattan prosecutors dismissed the rape charge involving Jessica Mann after she declined to testify again, allowing sentencing to move forward on Weinstein’s 2025 conviction for a criminal sexual act against former Project Runway assistant Miriam Haley. The DA’s office recommends 20 years in prison for that count, which carries a maximum of 25 years. Judge Curtis Farber had delayed sentencing while the Mann proceedings continued. Weinstein’s spokesperson said the defense expects to challenge the recommendation. Weinstein has also served less than half of a separate 16-year California prison sentence.

evidence.title: Harvey Weinstein's rape charge to be dropped by New York prosecutors, bringing closure to #MeToo case - Livemint
evidence.text: New York prosecutors said on Thursday, June 25, that they will drop the rape charge against Harvey Weinstein rather than try him a fourth time. The charge arose from Jessica Mann’s allegation that he raped her in a Manhattan hotel room in 2013. A 2020 conviction on that charge was overturned on procedural grounds, and juries deadlocked in retrials in 2025 and again this year. Dropping it does not mean Weinstein will serve no prison time: the article says he remains incarcerated under separate sexual assault-related convictions in New York and California that carry longer sentences. The dropped charge carried a maximum of four years, less time than he has already served.

evidence.title: Harvey Weinstein Rape Case Dropped After Second Hung Jury - Bloomberg Law News
evidence.text: New York prosecutors said they would drop an unresolved rape charge against Harvey Weinstein rather than try him a fourth time, after juries deadlocked twice. He remains convicted of another sexual felony in New York and of crimes in California, and the article says he will stay behind bars. Prosecutors recommended a 20-year prison sentence for the crimes of which he was convicted.

market.question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by December 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria  by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Tesla to Launch Larger FSD Model After the Holidays; Will Remove Robotaxi Safety Monitors in Three Weeks - Not a Tesla App
evidence.text: Musk said Tesla plans to remove safety drivers from its Austin Robotaxi service within three weeks. The article says Tesla has not yet provided a commercial ride without an in-car safety supervisor and describes its current FSD system as requiring constant human attention. It presents the three-week timeline as Musk’s claim, not a confirmed launch, and does not give a publication date from which to determine whether it falls by December 31. Removing Austin Robotaxi safety drivers would also not, by itself, establish a broader launch of unsupervised FSD.

evidence.title: Tesla CEO Elon Musk claims driverless Robotaxis coming to Austin in 3 weeks - electrek.co
evidence.text: Tesla CEO Elon Musk claimed driverless Robotaxis would come to Austin in three weeks. According to the article, he has said Tesla would remove Safety Monitors from its Austin Robotaxis three times this year—in September, October, and November. These are claims about a planned change, not evidence that unsupervised driving has launched.

evidence.title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Blew Me Away. I Still Wouldn't Buy It - InsideEVs
evidence.text: In November, the author tested Tesla’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised) version 13.2.9 in a Model Y, letting it control about 145 of 150 miles. It handled many complex situations but made two safety-related mistakes requiring intervention. Tesla is trying to remove the driver from the loop through a robotaxi pilot in Austin, Texas—a goal Musk has promised for years. The author says that goal seems closer but remains out of reach: drivers must still watch for unexpected errors. Tesla says FSD is a driver-assistance system that owners must supervise, not a system that legally drives the car. The article gives no December 31 launch date.

evidence.title: FSD v14.2 parking lot handling tests give mixed results (videos), Tesla expands the rollout circle - Tesla Oracle
evidence.text: The article reports that Tesla had released FSD v14.2 (2025.38.9.5) to early-access customers and expanded its rollout, but only about 4% of its US/Canada fleet had received it. Although many owners reported successful automatic parking, some situations still required human supervision to prevent mistakes; the system remained labeled “FSD (Supervised).” One Model Y owner reported that it rubbed a parking-space boundary and that he stopped it when it tried to leave the spot incorrectly. The article does not report an unsupervised FSD launch or a commitment to launch one by December 31. It only speculates that Tesla might expand v14.2 availability near Christmas.

evidence.title: Tesla opens Robotaxi access to everyone — but there’s one catch - Teslarati
evidence.text: The article provides no launch date for unsupervised FSD. It says Tesla’s San Francisco Bay Area ride-hailing service is branded as using “Robotaxi technology,” but operates at SAE Level 2 with a driver in the driver’s seat holding the steering wheel, using the same supervised FSD available to customers. Tesla’s filing says “almost 100%” of its California Robotaxi rides engaged FSD (Supervised) at some point—not necessarily for the entire ride. The article says Tesla does not currently operate a Level 4 system in California; it describes the status of its Austin service as debatable and notes that Tesla has obtained an Arizona permit.

evidence.title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Swerves To Avoid A Sideswipe In This Test - InsideEVs
evidence.text: The article says improvements in Tesla’s FSD v13 and v14 have made its claimed autonomous-driving lead more visible. It acknowledges that v14 still has issues, which the author considers fixable, and says FSD is not yet Level 5 autonomous software. It reports that Tesla vehicles have driven billions of miles using FSD. The article does not say Tesla has launched unsupervised FSD or give a December 31 launch date.

evidence.title: License Tesla FSD or face the disruption — Musk once again warns legacy automakers - Tesla Oracle
evidence.text: The tested Model 3 ran FSD **Supervised** version 14.1.7; the article says the newer version, 14.2, launched on Nov. 20. In closed-track tests, the car avoided simulated aggressive driving, but the article cautions that this may not reflect real-world performance. It says FSD remains dangerous without close human supervision and reports no launch of unsupervised FSD.

evidence.title: Tesla FSD Supervised ride-alongs in Europe begin in Italy, France, and Germany - Teslarati
evidence.text: Teslarati’s title says Tesla FSD Supervised ride-alongs have begun in Italy, France, and Germany. The program lets members of the public ride as non-driving observers while FSD navigates urban streets. This is evidence of supervised demonstrations, not a launch of unsupervised FSD; the relevant text gives no December 31 launch date.

evidence.title: Tesla Finally Releases FSD Crash Data That Appears More Honest - Forbes
evidence.text: Tesla began rolling out FSD v14.1.7 (firmware 2025.38.8.7) to additional Cybertrucks in the US and Canada. Unlike the earlier v14.1.5 release, which was limited to a handful of early-access testers, mostly influencers, this update also reached some general Cybertruck owners. TeslaFi tracking showed more than 200 Cybertrucks had installed it or were awaiting download within eight hours of deployment. The article says this was not a wide release; Elon Musk said a later v14.2 release would be wide. One owner reported a drive without touching the wheel, but the article does not say Tesla launched *unsupervised* FSD or give a December 31 launch date.

evidence.title: When Tesla’s FSD works well, it gets credit. When it doesn’t, you get blamed. - electrek.co
evidence.text: Musk had recently said Tesla would deliver unsupervised FSD to consumer vehicles by year-end, less than two months away at the time of the article. At Tesla’s shareholders meeting, he revised the timeline to “a few months away,” potentially pushing a launch into 2026. The article says Tesla had not yet delivered unsupervised self-driving despite similar annual promises for six years. It also says Tesla’s ride-hailing pilots still used in-car supervisors and that there was no evidence Tesla had begun the legal and regulatory steps needed to take responsibility when consumer vehicles drive autonomously.

market.question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by December 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria  by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Inside Tesla’s Unsupervised FSD Geofence for Data Gathering - Not a Tesla App
evidence.text: Tesla began testing self-driving cars on public roads in Austin, Texas, on December 15, 2025, without onboard human safety monitors; CEO Elon Musk confirmed the driverless tests. However, Tesla said these tests are for internal validation, not daily commercial use, and are not open to paying customers. Its earlier limited Austin robotaxi service used human safety monitors, and Tesla has not given a date for fully autonomous public rides. The tests show progress toward unsupervised FSD, but the article does not report a public launch by December 31.

evidence.title: Tesla stock closes at 2025 high after Musk confirms driverless Robotaxi tests underway in Austin - cnbc.com
evidence.text: The article says Tesla recently removed safety monitors from test vehicles in Austin, which are now driving without passengers. It also reports that a researcher found a “Bay Unsupervised CA DMV” geofence in Tesla’s public software update 2025.44. The article interprets this as a possible way to collect Bay Area data for California driverless-permit requirements, but says the geofence does not mean Tesla is enabling unsupervised FSD for customers immediately. It reports no public launch or confirmed December 31 launch date.

evidence.title: California regulator puts Tesla sales suspension order on hold - Reuters
evidence.text: Elon Musk said unsupervised Tesla Robotaxis would reach Austin streets by year-end and, according to the article, later confirmed that testing is underway with no occupants in the vehicle. It characterizes these as tests ahead of a possible public rollout, not evidence that unsupervised FSD has launched for the public.

The tokenized equities must track the price of U.S. stocks such as those listed on the NYSE or Nasdaq. They may be structured as synthetic assets, wrapped instruments, or token representations of real equities, but do not need to confer voting rights or direct ownership.

To qualify, U.S.-based users must be able to buy or sell the tokenized equities during the market period.

It also describes Israeli control in the Golan Heights buffer zone, strikes on Damascus and its outskirts, and helicopter-borne troop deployments, without placing those troops in Damascus. It reports no Israeli troop entry into Damascus or plan to enter by October 31.

market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump issues a presidential veto of any bill by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

evidence.title: Gov. JB Pritzker signs bills protecting Illinois immigrants from federal immigration enforcement - cbsnews.com
evidence.text: White House officials recently told lawmakers that Trump would veto the fiscal 2026 NDAA unless Congress removed House- and Senate-passed provisions preventing U.S. military bases from bearing names associated with Confederate officers, according to the sponsor of one provision. A source said the administration also threatened a veto over protections for Pentagon civilian employees’ collective bargaining rights. Both sets of provisions remained in a negotiated compromise, but Speaker Mike Johnson removed them from the final text, finalized Sunday. The article reports a conditional veto threat, not a 2025 veto. It also notes that Trump vetoed the fiscal 2021 NDAA over a related base-renaming measure, and Congress overrode that veto.

evidence.title: Court seems likely to side with Trump on president’s power to fire FTC commissioner - SCOTUSblog
evidence.text: The final version of this year’s National Defense Authorization Act would prevent the Pentagon from keeping fewer than 76,000 U.S. troops in Europe for more than 45 days unless the defense secretary and U.S. European Command leadership demonstrate to Congress that they consulted NATO allies and that the reduction serves U.S. national security interests. The article says this contrasts with the Trump administration’s recently released National Security Strategy, which encourages Europeans to take responsibility for their defense needs. It also says lawmakers were concerned about the administration’s push to remove troops from Romania. The article reports no statement from Trump that he will veto the bill.

evidence.title: Capitol Hill revolt threatens Trump’s Venezuela playbook amid Caribbean strike oversight - Fox News
evidence.text: Sens. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) and Tim Kaine (D-Va.) introduced the Prohibiting Unauthorized Military Action in Venezuela Act of 2025 on Thursday. It would bar federal funding for Trump administration military strikes within or against Venezuela without congressional approval, while allowing action in self-defense against an armed attack or imminent threat. A separate war powers resolution introduced Wednesday would bar U.S. forces from engaging in hostilities within or against Venezuela; the article says previous war powers resolutions had failed to gain enough support to pass. Cato Institute fellow Katherine Thompson said Trump might be more cautious about land strikes if both chambers could pass a resolution opposing them, adding that even a veto would be politically significant if Congress appeared to have a veto-proof majority. The article reports neither passage of these measures nor a Trump veto.

evidence.title: Will Trump sign the Epstein bill and when could the files be released? - theguardian.com
evidence.text: Trump told reporters on Monday that he would sign the Epstein Files Transparency Act if it reached his desk. He had reversed his opposition on Sunday and called for the files’ release. The House passed the bill 427–1 on Tuesday, and the Senate agreed to pass it by unanimous consent. The article says Trump could still veto it despite his pledge, but notes that Congress can override a veto with two-thirds support in both chambers; the votes already exceeded that threshold.

evidence.title: Column: Presidents can no longer be trusted with pardons - Los Angeles Times
evidence.text: Trump initially opposed the Epstein Files Transparency Act but reversed his position and urged Republicans to support it. The day before the vote, he said he would sign it if it reached his desk. The House voted 427–1 in favor, and the Senate agreed to pass it without amendments once paperwork arrived. The article says the bill was headed to Trump for signature; it does not report a veto. It notes that Congress could override a veto with two-thirds majorities in both chambers.

evidence.title: US House votes on releasing Epstein files: What to expect - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The House was set to vote on a bill to release the remaining Jeffrey Epstein files after Trump urged Republicans to support it and said he would not veto it if Congress passed it. On Monday, he said he would sign the bill if it cleared the Senate—a reversal of his earlier stance calling the files a “Democratic hoax” and discouraging Republicans from pursuing them. The article reports no final vote or veto. Bill sponsor Thomas Massie said he hoped for a veto-proof majority and estimated that 100 or more House Republicans could support the bill.

evidence.title: In reversal, President Donald Trump says House Republicans should vote to release Epstein files - WABC-TV New York
evidence.text: Trump said House Republicans should vote to release the Jeffrey Epstein files, reversing his earlier opposition as support for the bill grew within his party. The bill would require the Justice Department to release Epstein-related files and communications, with redactions allowed for victims’ information and ongoing investigations. Supporters expected it to pass the House, though its prospects in the Senate were unclear. Rep. Thomas Massie said he hoped for a veto-proof majority; the article does not say whether Trump would sign or veto the bill if it reached him.

evidence.title: How Many Republicans Will Defy Trump and Vote to Release the Epstein Files? - Mother Jones
evidence.text: The Epstein Files Transparency Act would require the Justice Department to release unclassified Epstein-related records within 30 days of enactment. On November 12, supporters reached the 218 signatures needed to force a House vote; Speaker Mike Johnson said he would bring it to a vote the week of November 17. Trump opposed further releases, saying Republicans should focus on reopening the government and that there should be “no deflections to Epstein.” If the House passes the bill, it would need 60 Senate votes to advance, including at least 13 Republicans if all 47 Democrats and Democratic-aligned independents support it. The article says Trump could veto it even if it passes the Senate; an override would require two-thirds support in both chambers. It does not report that the bill has reached Trump or that he has decided to veto it.

evidence.title: Here's what an Epstein files vote in the House could look like - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
evidence.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
evidence.text: Speaker Mike Johnson said the House would vote the following week on the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which would compel the Justice Department to release its unclassified Epstein files. The article says House passage is almost certain if the bill is considered under a rule requiring a simple majority, but passage under a procedure requiring a two-thirds majority is less certain. If it passes the House, Senate Majority Leader John Thune does not have to bring it to a vote. If it also passes the Senate, the bill would go to President Donald Trump, who, the article says, would most likely veto it. Overriding a veto would require two-thirds votes in both chambers.

evidence.title: What's next in U.S. Congress after Jeffrey Epstein petition passes - CBC
evidence.text: A petition to force a House vote on releasing the Jeffrey Epstein files reached the necessary 218 signatures this week after Democratic Representative Adelita Grijalva was sworn in. Trump had tried to stop the vote, but Republican Representatives Lauren Boebert and Nancy Mace reportedly refused to withdraw their support. Representative Ro Khanna predicted that 40 to 50 Republicans could join Democrats in a final House vote. The article says the legislation would then need to pass the Senate, where passage is unlikely. Trump could veto it if it passed both chambers, but the article does not say he has decided to do so.

evidence.title: Trump signs bill releasing Epstein documents amid fears of cover-up - France 24
evidence.text: Trump did not veto the Epstein Files Transparency Act: the article says he signed it into law on Wednesday and announced the signing on social media late that day, without a media event. He had opposed the bill for months but reversed course before it passed Congress on Tuesday with bipartisan support. House Speaker Mike Johnson had previously been asked whether he would urge Trump to veto it.

market.question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by October 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

It discusses an earlier version as Full Self-Driving (Supervised) v13 and does not report a launch of unsupervised FSD or give a date for one.

market.question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact the ground territory of the West Bank (e.g., if a weapons depot on West Bank soil is hit by an Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on West Bank territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the U.S. tariff rate on China be between 60% and 100% on November 12?
market.resolution_criteria:
On August 11, 2025, the United States and China announced a 90-day extension of the mutual reduction in tariffs as part of a temporary trade de-escalation agreement.

This market will resolve according to the general tariff rate on imports into the United States from the People's Republic of China on November 12, 2025, 12:00 PM ET.

The general tariff rate refers to the base tariff rate paid on imports, including any general tariff the U.S. imposes on all imports (e.g. a 10% tariff on all U.S. imports and a 50% tariff on top of that on Chinese imports would equal a 60% tariff).

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Item specific exceptions or increases will not be considered (i.e. this market does not refer to the effective tariff rate).

Only tariffs which are in effect will qualify. Tariffs which are paused, or which have been announced but not yet gone into effect will not be considered.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible information will also be used.

Merz said this differed from what President Donald Trump and Putin had agreed the previous week in Washington. Earlier that week, Trump had also cast doubt on a meeting, after previously saying arrangements had begun. The article gives no meeting date. It notes that neither leader attended earlier direct talks in Istanbul, which made no meaningful progress toward a peace agreement or ceasefire. Turkey’s president said Ankara was prepared to facilitate high-level talks.

evidence.title: Zelenskyy says aides to meet Trump team in New York on Friday - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: A Putin–Zelenskyy meeting remained elusive. Zelenskyy said on Wednesday that Moscow was sending “very arrogant and negative signals” about negotiations and called for pressure on Russia to take real steps. Trump said Tuesday that a meeting was uncertain; Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the previous week that none was planned, though Putin would be ready once a clear agenda was established. Putin had refused Zelenskyy’s invitation to direct talks in Türkiye in May. Despite Trump’s August 15 summit with Putin and subsequent talks with Zelenskyy and European leaders, the article says negotiations had made little progress. Zelenskyy said his officials would meet Trump representatives in New York on Friday as mediation efforts intensified.

evidence.title: Trump says Putin and Zelenskyy are 'not ready' for peace as Europe faces pressure to step up - NBC News
evidence.text: The article reports no scheduled meeting between Putin and Zelenskyy before September 30. It says a peace agreement remains out of reach because Zelenskyy, Putin and Trump have not agreed on terms. At a summit with Trump in Alaska one week before August 18, Putin rejected a ceasefire before a peace deal and urged Ukraine to surrender eastern territory. Russia has also rejected proposed foreign security forces in Ukraine, including after a peace deal. These unresolved disagreements offer little evidence that a Putin–Zelenskyy meeting is imminent.

The article reports no scheduled Putin-Zelenskyy meeting.

The White House hoped to settle on a date and location by the end of that week; German Chancellor Merz said Monday that the goal was a meeting within two weeks. Budapest was among the locations under consideration. Zelenskyy said no date had been set, while a Russian spokesperson said only that high-level talks would take place and did not confirm Putin’s participation. The article does not give a confirmed meeting date or say whether the meeting will occur by September 30.

market.question: US strikes Yemen by September 30?

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Yemen ground territory or any official Yemen embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Yemen soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Yemen territory or cause damage.

market.question: Trump imposes tariff on semiconductors by September 30?

evidence.text: New York City Mayor Eric Adams abruptly ended his 2025 reelection campaign in a Sunday video, less than two months before Election Day. Days earlier, he had insisted he would stay in the race and was the only candidate who could defeat Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani. Reports said Trump administration allies had raised a possible federal job if Adams withdrew, but Adams said he had received no formal offer. The article reports no Trump endorsement of Adams. Instead, Trump said the field needed to narrow to beat Mamdani and that former Gov. Andrew Cuomo “might have a chance” in a one-on-one race.

The article says President Trump and White House officials had held talks aimed at getting Adams, Sliwa or both to leave the race, amid concerns that the crowded field would help Mamdani win. Trump officials had also floated administration jobs for Adams, but those talks did not succeed. The article reports no Trump endorsement of Adams. Adams will remain on the November 4 ballot despite ending his campaign.

market.question: Will Yōko Kamikawa be the next Prime Minister of Japan?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the next appointed Prime Minister of Japan, succeeding Shigeru Ishiba. 

Any PM formally appointed by the Japanese Emperor will qualify.

If no new PM is appointed by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “No new PM”. 

If early general elections are called before the new PM has officially been appointed, this market will resolve to “Election called”.

The resolution of this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Japan PM Ishiba resigns after election defeats - Asia Media Centre
evidence.text: The article does not mention Yōko Kamikawa. It identifies Shinjiro Koizumi and Sanae Takaichi as the clear favourites among five candidates to replace Shigeru Ishiba as Liberal Democratic Party leader. With just over a week before LDP lawmakers and rank-and-file members vote, it says Koizumi appears on course to become Japan’s youngest postwar prime minister; Takaichi would be Japan’s first female prime minister. Becoming prime minister is not certain because the LDP and its coalition partner have lost their majority in both houses of parliament, though the article says Koizumi would likely be approved because the LDP remains the largest party in the lower house. The leader will be chosen by 295 LDP lawmakers and party-member ballots worth another 295 votes, with a runoff if no candidate wins a majority.

evidence.title: What Awaits Japan’s Next Prime Minister - Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
evidence.text: The LDP leadership race to succeed outgoing Prime Minister Ishiba Shigeru began on September 22, with an election scheduled for October 4. Its five candidates are former economic security minister Takaichi Sanae, 64; agriculture minister Koizumi Shinjiro, 44; former LDP secretary general Motegi Toshimitsu, 69; Chief Cabinet Secretary Hayashi Yoshimasa, 64; and former economic security minister Kobayashi Takayuki, 50. Yōko Kamikawa is not among them. The article describes Takaichi and Koizumi as the leading contenders: a September 13–14 Yomiuri poll put them at 29% and 25%, respectively, while a September 18 Jiji poll favored Koizumi over Takaichi.

evidence.title: Japan PM Ishiba resigns after bruising election losses - Reuters
evidence.text: Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba announced his resignation on Sunday, less than a year after taking office in October 2024, following the ruling Liberal Democratic Party’s historic defeat in July’s parliamentary elections and two earlier electoral setbacks. His departure opens the way for leadership rivals, including hawkish conservative Sanae Takaichi and political heir Shinjiro Koizumi, to renew their bids for power. The article does not mention Yōko Kamikawa or assess her prospects of becoming the next prime minister.

market.question: Will Russia capture all of Pokrovsk by December 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the entirety of Pokrovsk by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Pokrovsk will be considered captured if the entirety of the municipality is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

The territory of the municipality is shaded in light grey and is distinguished from bordering municipalities such as "Rih" with a darker grey line.  If all area within the municipality is shaded in red, however the shading does not precisely match up with the border such that there is a tiny amount of grey along the border of the city, this will still qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

Once Russia captures the Pokrovsk, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Pokrovsk Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Pokrovosk+Location.png
Location on Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/ixAs4fF8n8ccVeL17

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map which will not be considered.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of if it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

evidence.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, December 8, 2025 - understandingwar.org
evidence.text: As of December 8, 2025, the article says Ukrainian forces still held part of Pokrovsk despite repeated Russian claims that they had captured it. The battle had entered its second year, and Russia had concentrated 170,000 troops on that front without quickly taking the city. The article does not establish whether Russia will capture the remaining part by December 31.

evidence.title: ‘What choice do we have?’: no end in sight for Ukraine’s war-weary frontline troops - The Guardian
evidence.text: Pokrovsk had not fallen at the time of reporting, despite President Vladimir Putin’s recent claim that Russian forces had taken it. Russian forces had been advancing from the south, and Ukraine was losing ground. Ukrainian troops said they still held the north of the city up to the railway line that bisects it, though observers of the Russian advance suggested their hold was tenuous. The battle had lasted nearly 18 months, and the article did not establish whether Russia would capture all of Pokrovsk by December 31.

evidence.title: ISW: Russia's Huliaipole breakthrough came from months of preparation, not sudden Ukrainian collapse (MAP) - Euromaidan Press
evidence.text: By Dec. 3, most independent mapping projects, including Ukraine’s DeepState, assessed almost all of central Pokrovsk and the built-up area south of its main railway line as under Russian control. Russia claimed to have captured the city on Dec. 1, but Ukraine denied it on Dec. 2. Control of northern Pokrovsk remained uncertain: strikes on both sides’ soldiers had been recorded there, and Ukrainian reinforcements and drone teams were making it difficult for Russian troops to establish positions. A Ukrainian drone pilot said Ukrainian soldiers still held some northern positions, though they were mostly cut off on the ground and supplied only by drone. The article describes full Russian control as close to being secured, but not yet established.

evidence.title: Why Russia Didn’t Capture Kupiansk or Pokrovsk: Zelenskyy and OSINT Analysts Push Back - UNITED24 Media
evidence.text: Putin claimed on Monday evening that Russian forces had captured Pokrovsk, but Ukrainian officials disputed that claim. Ukrainian analysts and military bloggers acknowledged that Russia held most of the city, and battlefield maps showed Russian forces largely in control. Russia had spent more than a year trying to seize Pokrovsk, a former Ukrainian logistical hub seen as a gateway to Donetsk, and had suffered heavy losses. The article does not establish that Russia held all of Pokrovsk or whether it would do so by December 31.

evidence.title: Ukraine maps: Tracking di war wit Russia so far - BBC
evidence.text: The article describes the 18-month battle for Pokrovsk as nearing an endgame, but says Ukraine still holds positions in the city. Russia’s advance reached within seven miles of Pokrovsk by August 2024; although the city was then expected to fall within weeks, it did not. Russia instead gradually semi-encircled it, with Russian forces outnumbering defenders eight to one, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Russian troops have infiltrated in small groups since October, using rain and fog to evade drones. They continue to enter on foot, motorbikes and pickup trucks. A larger, irregular group dubbed the “Mad Max convoy” appeared in a 10 November video emerging from fog; its goal was to gather in Pokrovsk, then find and attack Ukrainian positions. A Ukrainian raid at the end of October had reopened an exit route. Zelenskyy said Russia suffered 25,000 killed and wounded in October, mostly around Pokrovsk. These facts indicate mounting Russian pressure, but not that Russia has captured all of the city.

evidence.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, December 2, 2025 - understandingwar.org
evidence.text: In October 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed that Russian forces had surrounded Pokrovsk in Donetsk Oblast and Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast. The article says online maps such as DeepState’s quickly showed that claim was wrong. It does not establish whether Russia controlled Pokrovsk as of December 2 or would capture all of it by December 31. It cautions that Russian troops appearing in a settlement or raising a flag may be infiltrators, not evidence of territorial control, and that DeepState’s updates can lag developments on the ground by two to three days.

market.question: Will Larry Ellison/Oracle acquire TikTok?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes"  if it is officially announced that the listed individual, either personally or through an entity, enters into an agreement with TikTok to acquire its US operations by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An official announcement will qualify for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the acquisition is ultimately completed.

The entity entering into the agreement does not need to be controlled by the listed individual; their involvement as a partial owner, investor, or similar role will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market is official information from the listed individual and/or TikTok, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

evidence.title: Ellison’s Oracle poised to run TikTok, raising hopes for tougher rules against antisemitism - Jewish Telegraphic Agency
evidence.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Thursday that China had approved a multibillion-dollar deal to put TikTok’s US operations under American control. The agreement’s details have not been released, but the White House previously said a US investor consortium led by Oracle would acquire a controlling stake in TikTok. Larry Ellison is Oracle’s co-founder; the article does not say he would acquire TikTok personally. The proposed deal follows a law passed last year requiring TikTok’s China-based owner, ByteDance, to sell the app or face a ban.

The White House said the deal would create a U.S.-based joint venture with majority-American investors and directors. A consortium of American investors, including Oracle, would have a stake; ByteDance and its affiliates would own less than 20%. Oracle was cofounded by Larry Ellison, but the article does not say Ellison would personally acquire TikTok or that Oracle would own it outright.

market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

market.question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

market.question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

evidence.title: What’s Next for the Fed in 2026? - Morningstar
evidence.text: Markets expect the Federal Reserve to hold interest rates steady at its Jan. 27–28 meeting, though the article says that outcome is probable, not certain. The Fed cut rates in October and December, but an October government shutdown disrupted economic data and has made the outlook harder to judge. November inflation came in lower than expected, yet Fed Chair Jerome Powell cautioned on Dec. 10 that the data might be distorted. The article does not predict a Fed cut of 50 basis points or more at the January meeting.

evidence.title: Challenges likely for REITs - The Star
evidence.text: The Fed cut its benchmark rate by 25 basis points at its December 2025 meeting, bringing the target range to 3.50%–3.75%. It is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at its Jan. 27–28 meeting. For later in 2026, the Fed’s own forecast anticipates one cut, while market pricing implies just under one cut by April and another later in the year. The article does not specify the size of those anticipated cuts.

evidence.title: To hike or to hold: What's going to happen to interest rates in 2026? - Nine.com.au
evidence.text: The article says the Fed cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points in September 2025, another 25 basis points in October, and a third time in December. It does not report a rate decision after the January 2026 meeting or say whether a cut of 50 basis points or more will occur then.

evidence.title: Minutes of latest Federal Reserve meeting reveal deep divide over interest rates - The Guardian
evidence.text: At its 9–10 December meeting, the Fed approved a quarter-point cut, lowering its benchmark overnight rate to 3.5%–3.75%. The decision was closely contested: six officials opposed a cut in their projections, including two voting members who dissented. New projections showed only one cut expected the following year, and the policy statement indicated the Fed would likely hold rates until data showed inflation falling again or unemployment rising more than anticipated. The Fed’s next meeting is 27–28 January; investors expected rates to remain unchanged. The article reports no decision after that meeting.

evidence.title: What to expect for interest rate cuts in January 2026 - businesstech.co.za
evidence.text: At its December 9–10, 2025 meeting, the FOMC cut rates by 25 basis points, setting the federal funds target range at 3.5%–3.75%; two voters preferred no change. The article says inflation remained relatively elevated while downside risks to jobs had increased. It identifies January 27–28, 2026 as the next meeting, with a decision due January 28, but does not report or predict a cut of 50 basis points or more at that meeting.

evidence.title: Will the Stock Market Crash in 2026? The Federal Reserve Sends a Silent Warning to Investors. - The Motley Fool
evidence.text: At its December meeting, the FOMC cut interest rates by 25 basis points, not 50. Three members dissented in opposite directions: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee and Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid wanted no cut, while Governor Stephen Miran wanted a 50-basis-point cut. Schmid had favored holding rates steady at two consecutive meetings; Miran had favored a larger cut at three consecutive meetings. The article attributes the division to uncertainty over tariffs, inflation and unemployment. It does not state what the Fed will do after its January 2026 meeting.

evidence.title: Is Sherwin-Williams Still a Buy After Its 115,000% Run? - The Motley Fool
evidence.text: The article says the Federal Reserve’s next interest-rate decision is scheduled for its Jan. 27–28 meeting, about five weeks away. It reports a third rate cut earlier that month and argues another cut is likely, citing November’s 64,000 jobs added and Fed Chair Jerome Powell’s concern that job gains may be overstated by as much as 60,000 per month. For Sherwin-Williams, the article says a further 25-basis-point cut would likely bring the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate below the 6% level its CEO identified as important for demand. It does not report a January decision or predict a cut of 50 basis points or more.

evidence.title: Federal Reserve Makes Third Cut in December - The Mortgage Reports
evidence.text: On December 10, Jerome Powell’s FOMC cut the federal funds rate for the third consecutive time, to 3.50%–3.75%, its lowest level since 2022. The Fed had cut by 25 basis points in both September and October, for 75 basis points of cuts that year in total. Nine of 12 members supported the December cut; one favored a 50-basis-point cut. market.question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.question: Russian strike on a NATO member by October 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between September 24 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Russian strike on a NATO member by October 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between September 24 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: US strikes Yemen by December 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Yemen soil or any official Yemen embassy or consulate by  December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Yemen ground territory or any official Yemen embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Yemen soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Yemen territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Pressure grows on ‘reckless’ Hegseth as twin scandals engulf Pentagon chief - The Guardian
evidence.text: In a 6 December 2025 article, The Guardian reports that a Defense Department investigation released that Thursday found US defense secretary Pete Hegseth violated Pentagon policies by sharing sensitive details on Signal hours before airstrikes in Yemen. The article describes the airstrikes as already having occurred by 6 December 2025, supporting a “yes” answer for strikes by 31 December 2025. It does not give the strikes’ exact date.

evidence.title: Top admiral briefs lawmakers on boat strike as watchdog faults Hegseth for Signal use - NPR
evidence.text: A Pentagon watchdog report found that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth violated agency policy by using Signal on his personal phone to discuss U.S. airstrikes in Yemen earlier this year. The report said he sent nonpublic details—including the number of manned U.S. aircraft and strike times—about 2 to 4 hours before the strikes were carried out. The investigation followed a March report that a journalist had been added to a Signal chat in which senior officials discussed plans to strike Houthi rebels in Yemen. This is evidence that U.S. strikes in Yemen occurred, though the article does not give their exact date.

evidence.title: Pentagon Investigator Faults Hegseth for Improper Use of Signal - The New York Times
evidence.text: The article reports that the US carried out an air strike on Yemen’s Houthi rebels on March 15. It says Trump administration officials accidentally added journalist Jeffrey Goldberg to an 18-person Signal chat where they disclosed the strike’s timing hours before it happened, including when US F-18 aircraft and drones would launch. Goldberg reported the chat on March 24 and said its messages matched the air strikes. The article says the strikes killed at least 53 people, including children, and identifies the Yemen bombing campaign as Operation Rough Rider.

evidence.title: The Axis of Resistance - Middle East Institute
evidence.text: A Department of Defense inspector general report found that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shared secret information in a Signal chat in March, including details of a planned US airstrike in Yemen against Houthi fighters. The article describes the attack as pending at the time; Congressman Mark Warner said American pilots aboard the USS Harry S. Truman were preparing to launch the mission. Hegseth later wrote, “Houthis bombed into submission.” The article does not give the strike’s exact date or year.

evidence.title: Pentagon watchdog finds Hegseth risked the safety of U.S. forces with use of Signal - NPR
evidence.text: The article reports that the U.S. carried out airstrikes in Yemen against the Houthis on March 15. It says the Trump administration launched a military campaign in response to Houthi attacks on ships in the Red Sea, and that the airstrikes ended after a few weeks. The Pentagon’s watchdog found that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth put U.S. personnel and the mission at risk by discussing sensitive operational details on Signal before the March 15 strikes.

evidence.title: Pentagon report concludes Hegseth put troops in danger with Signal chat | Signal group chat leak - The Guardian
evidence.text: A Pentagon inspector general report, expected as early as Thursday, followed a journalist’s March disclosure that he had been added to a Signal chat where Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and other senior officials discussed plans for U.S. airstrikes against Houthi rebels in Yemen. According to the article, Hegseth shared information about targets, timing and aircraft, and the report found that interception could have endangered U.S. servicemembers and the mission. This is evidence of strike planning, but the article does not explicitly say whether U.S. strikes in Yemen occurred by December 31.

evidence.title: Has the Pentagon really exonerated Pete Hegseth over Signal leaks? - aljazeera.com
evidence.text: The article refers to a U.S. airstrike in Yemen and says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth shared operational information about U.S. military operations there in a Signal chat on March 15, 2025. A Pentagon inspector general found that some of the information matched material U.S. Central Command had classified SECRET/NOFORN. After officials said the chat information was unclassified, CBS News filed a Freedom of Information Act request in March asking U.S. Africa Command whether similar information could be released about a separate March 25 strike on ISIS operatives in Somalia. The Yemen strike is directly relevant to whether the U.S. struck Yemen by December 31; the Somalia strike was only a comparison in the records request.

evidence.text: The article says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and other senior U.S. officials discussed pending military strikes in Yemen in a Signal group chat about three months after his confirmation earlier this year. market.question: Will Trump and Putin meet next in Ukraine?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the location of the next meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin between September 30 and June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

This market will resolve to "No meeting by June 30" if no qualifying meeting occurs during this market's timeframe.

A meeting is defined as any encounter where Putin and Trump are all present and interact with each other in person.

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

For this market, Gulf states are defined as the six members of the Gulf Cooperation Council (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.
