market.question: Will the Government shutdown end November 12-15?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to the calendar date range (ET) of the first day after September 30, 2025 which the U.S. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is not shut down due to a lapse in appropriations. 

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown. 

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

evidence.title: CMS recalls nearly 3,000 employees to manage open enrollment amid shutdown - Federal News Network
evidence.text: The shutdown entered its 21st day on Oct. 21. Because funding had lapsed, many government employees were not being paid, and federal workers were set to miss their Oct. 24 paycheck. The article says the shutdown will end once Congress agrees on government appropriations. Democrats were pressing for health care funding, while Republicans wanted the government reopened before a health care debate. The White House said on Oct. 14 it was preparing to ride out the shutdown. The article gives no agreement or forecast for an end on Nov. 12–15.

evidence.title: Senate votes fail again as government shutdown drags on - CBS News
evidence.text: As of the article’s October 9, 2025 update, the shutdown remained unresolved. On Wednesday, the House-passed bill to fund the government through November 21 failed to advance in the Senate, 54–45—the sixth failed vote on the measure. Republicans gained no new Democratic support; they needed at least five more Democrats to advance it. A competing Democratic bill also failed, 47–52, short of the 60 votes needed. Democrats sought an extension of expiring health insurance tax credits, while Senate Majority Leader John Thune said the government should reopen before talks on health care. The article gives no specific forecast for November 12–15.

evidence.title: The federal government is still shut down. Here's what that means across the country - NPR
evidence.text: The shutdown began Oct. 1 and was still ongoing when the article was written. Senators voted again on a House-passed bill to reopen the government on Tuesday, but the vote failed, as had other attempts since Oct. 1. Senate Democrats opposed the Republican short-term funding bill because it did not extend Affordable Care Act marketplace tax credits; the article identifies that dispute as the cause of the shutdown. It reports no agreement or specific plan to end the shutdown on Nov. 12–15.

Federal employee unions sought to pause layoffs already underway and prevent further notices; the administration opposed the request. The article provides no agreement, reopening date, or other indication that the shutdown will end November 12–15.

evidence.title: With some shutdown pain points delayed for now, talks in Congress are 'nowhere' - NPR
evidence.text: The shutdown was ongoing: the Department of Education’s out-of-office reply said staff were furloughed “due to the lapse in appropriations” and would respond to emails once government functions resumed. Some employees said they could not access work email to check for layoff notices. An Education Department notice cited the “continued lapse in funding” as the reason for layoffs and gave a December 9 separation date. The article does not report an agreement to end the shutdown or a projected reopening date of November 12–15.

evidence.title: Judge pauses shutdown layoffs at more than 30 federal agencies - NPR
evidence.text: The federal government shutdown was two weeks old and ongoing when U.S. District Judge Susan Illston temporarily halted Trump administration layoffs at more than 30 federal agencies where the plaintiff unions represent workers. Her order pauses layoffs, not the shutdown; a further hearing on the layoffs was set for Oct. 28. The article gives no agreement, reopening date, or forecast indicating whether the shutdown will end November 12–15.

The article gives no expected end date and does not indicate whether the shutdown will end November 12–15.

The article says the shutdown will end when Congress passes funding bills the president is willing to sign; it gives no indication that this will happen on Nov. 12–15.

market.question: Will Israel annex Gaza territory by June 30 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel officially annexes any territory in the Gaza Strip by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Annexation is defined as an official declaration or legal act by the Israeli government claiming sovereignty over territory in the Gaza Strip that they were not claiming at the time of this market's creation.

Qualifying examples of annexation include the 1980 Jerusalem Law, and the Golan Heights Law. Instances where Israeli settlers claim administrative control over land in the Gaza Strip without formal annexation will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli government. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

evidence.title: Israel's widening Lebanon offensive 'cause for serious concern': Germany warns of severe humanitarian fallout - Gulf News
evidence.text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in an interview at a West Bank conference that he had directed the military to expand its control of the Gaza Strip incrementally. He said Israeli forces controlled 60% of Gaza, up from 50%, and that his first objective was 70%. The article also cites earlier reports that IDF maps given to aid agencies showed control of approximately 64%; CNN reported that further expansion would compress nearly 2 million Palestinians into a smaller area. These claims bear on the prospect of greater Israeli territorial control, but the article does not report a decision to annex Gaza or give a timeline for annexation by June 30, 2026.

evidence.title: UK readies sanctions against Israel to deter proposed illegal West Bank settlement - The Guardian
evidence.text: According to draft conclusions for an EU summit scheduled for June 18–19, EU leaders plan to say they “firmly reject” Israel’s announcement that it will seize 70% of Gaza’s territory, in a rebuke to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The article reports an announced plan and anticipated EU opposition; it does not say Israel has annexed Gaza territory or give a date for doing so.

evidence.title: Israeli attacks in Lebanon kill 12 people, including high-ranking officers - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Meetings are under way in Cairo with Hamas, the dominant Palestinian faction in Gaza, to break a deadlock over the territory. The article says Israel is threatening to expand the areas it controls in Gaza and has stepped up its attacks. Hamas told envoys from Donald Trump’s Board of Peace and mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkey that ending Israeli attacks is essential for progress. The article describes a threat to expand control, not a decision to annex Gaza territory by June 30, 2026.

evidence.title: Iran war: US to lift naval blockade of ports, Trump says - DW.com
evidence.text: In a May 29 update, the article reports that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced plans to expand Israel’s territorial control of Gaza. Hamas spokesman Bassem Naim told AFP that Netanyahu had announced expanding control over 70% of the Gaza Strip, calling it a “blatant violation” of agreements. The article says an October 2025 ceasefire deal calls for Israeli forces to gradually hand over control to an International Stabilisation Force rather than occupy and annex Gaza, but implementation and talks have stalled. It reports a plan to expand control, not an annexation.

evidence.title: 'Use antiquities for annexation' • Israel advances bill granting sweeping control over West Bank archaeology sites - Haaretz
evidence.text: The article says the Knesset advanced a Likud-backed bill that would create a government body with powers to purchase and expropriate land in the West Bank. It says there are plans to potentially extend that body’s authority to Gaza, but does not report that the bill has passed, that its powers have been extended to Gaza, or that Israel has annexed Gaza territory. It gives no timetable for doing so by June 30, 2026.

evidence.title: Zehut party leader to run in elections on joint list with ex-Otzma Yehudit chair - The Jerusalem Post
evidence.text: Zehut founder Moshe Feiglin and former Otzma Yehudit chairman Michael Ben-Ari agreed to run on a joint list in an upcoming Israeli election. Zehut said the alliance advocates defeating the enemy, conquering territories within the borders of the biblical Land of Israel from which Israel has been attacked, expelling terrorist elements there, and applying full Israeli sovereignty in the West Bank and Gaza. The article also says Zehut previously advocated annexing both territories. This is a proposed party policy, not an announced Israeli government decision to annex Gaza. Zehut failed to enter the Knesset in 2019 despite polls projecting eight to 10 seats; Ben-Ari was disqualified from running that year. The article gives no timetable for annexation.

market.question: Will Russia capture all of Pokrovsk by November 30?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the entirety of Pokrovsk by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Pokrovsk will be considered captured if the entirety of the municipality is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

The territory of the municipality is shaded in light grey and is distinguished from bordering municipalities such as "Rih" with a darker grey line.  If all area within the municipality is shaded in red, however the shading does not precisely match up with the border such that there is a tiny amount of grey along the border of the city, this will still qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

Once Russia captures the Pokrovsk, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Pokrovsk Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Pokrovosk+Location.png
Location on Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/ixAs4fF8n8ccVeL17

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map which will not be considered.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of if it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

evidence.title: Ukraine’s defense of Pokrovsk on a knife-edge as high command resists calls to withdraw - The Kyiv Independent
evidence.text: As of November 6, 2025, the article says the battle for Pokrovsk, ongoing since 2024, appears to be nearing its end, but it does not report that Russia controls the entire city. Open-source videos indicate that units of Russia’s 2nd Guards Combined Arms Army have taken the central railway station, the northern outskirts—including exits toward Dnipro and Rodynske—and eastern and northern high-rise districts. The article says it is unclear whether significant Ukrainian forces remain in Pokrovsk; footage shows small Ukrainian groups fighting Russian troops or surrendering. It reports no larger Ukrainian attack reversing the situation, though a small Ukrainian unit raided the center and raised a flag. Russian forces are also advancing near Rodynske and Myrnohrad, threatening to cut off Ukrainian units if they link up. Ukraine’s command has not officially announced a withdrawal and says it intends to counterattack or clear Pokrovsk. The article says a counterattack near Rodynske could prolong the defense, but its success is uncertain.

evidence.title: Ukraine: Russia says advances made in key city of Pokrovsk - DW.com
evidence.text: As of Nov. 6, most of Pokrovsk’s urban area remained a contested “gray zone” on open-source battlefield maps, including Deep State, a map widely trusted in Ukraine. Both the gray zone and areas assessed as firmly Russian-controlled had expanded over the preceding week, but Ukrainian positions remained inside the city, intermingled with Russian-held streets and buildings. Russian troops were continuing to infiltrate northward, while Ukrainian defenders faced worsening supply access and a growing threat of encirclement. Deep State co-founder Roman Pohorilyi described Pokrovsk as being ‘absorbed’ rather than encircled. A Ukrainian flag-raising at the city council building on Nov. 6 showed that central Pokrovsk was not then fully under Russian control, but did not demonstrate that Ukraine had cleared the city.

evidence.title: Russian gains in Pokrovsk after 21 months may not repeat on other fronts - The New Voice of Ukraine
evidence.text: DeepState, a Ukrainian project tracking the frontline with verified open-source imagery, showed on Tuesday that Russian forces had advanced further into Pokrovsk and its outskirts, but much of the area remained contested. Ukrainian military analysts described a sharp deterioration and said battlefield maps put Russian forces only a few miles from encircling the remaining Ukrainian troops. On Wednesday, Ukraine’s general staff denied Russian claims of encirclement and said it was reinforcing the flanks around Pokrovsk and nearby Myrnohrad. A Ukrainian soldier said Russian troops were present in every district, but had not fully taken the city and fighting continued. Ukraine deployed special forces over the weekend, though the article says the operation did not appear to shift momentum. Russian advances have been slow and costly. The article does not establish whether Russia will capture all of Pokrovsk by November 30.

evidence.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 4, 2025 - understandingwar.org
evidence.text: As of November 5, 2025, battlefield maps showed Russian forces a few kilometres from fully encircling Pokrovsk, which Russia calls Krasnoarmeysk. Russia claimed Ukrainian troops there were already encircled and should surrender, but the maps did not show a complete encirclement. Russia had been trying to capture Pokrovsk since 2024; the article described pincer movements, mobile units and drones disrupting Ukrainian logistics, while noting that neither side had full control in contested areas. The article does not establish whether Russia will capture all of Pokrovsk by November 30.

evidence.title: Russian and Ukrainian troops battle in ruins of Pokrovsk - Reuters
evidence.text: Russian forces have pushed farther into Pokrovsk from the south, but the Ukrainian open-source mapping project Deep State showed most of the city as a contested gray zone controlled by neither side. Russia said Wednesday that its troops were advancing north and had trapped Ukrainian forces; Ukraine denied any encirclement. The Ukrainian commander said Monday that 200–300 Russian soldiers were inside the city and that Ukrainian forces could still reach their troops. A Ukrainian sergeant said the situation was worsening and there was no stable defensive line. Ukraine has sent reinforcements and launched operations to restore supply routes. These accounts indicate growing Russian pressure, but not Russian control of all Pokrovsk; the article gives no specific forecast for November 30.

evidence.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Zelenskyy says 1.7 lakh Russian troops in Donetsk as fight for Pokrovsk intensifies; - The Times of India
evidence.text: Pokrovsk had not been fully captured at the time of the article. The US-based Institute for the Study of War said Ukrainian forces had “marginally advanced” in recent counter-attacks north of the town, while Pokrovsk remained “mainly a contested ‘grey zone’.” Ukrainian monitoring group DeepState estimated that about half the town was a grey zone. Ukraine’s top commander described difficult conditions against a large Russian force but denied that Ukrainian troops were surrounded or blocked. Ukrainian supply lines were under Russian fire, and Ukraine had deployed special forces to protect them. Russia had been trying to seize Pokrovsk for more than a year; the article does not establish whether it will capture all of the town by November 30.

evidence.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment October 31, 2025 - understandingwar.org
evidence.text: As of October 31, 2025, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the situation in Pokrovsk as “difficult” and claimed Russia had deployed about 170,000 troops in eastern Donetsk region as it pressed to seize the city. He acknowledged that Russian units had infiltrated parts of Pokrovsk, but said Ukrainian defenders were gradually eliminating them while preserving personnel. He rejected Moscow’s claim that the city was fully surrounded. President Vladimir Putin claimed Russian forces had made “significant advances,” though the article says those gains had come at a high cost in manpower and armour.

evidence.title: Ukraine says 170,000 Russian troops deployed in Donetsk - DW.com
evidence.text: As of Friday, October 31, Russia was trying to capture Pokrovsk, with around 170,000 troops deployed in the Donetsk region and a focus on the city, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. He called the situation “difficult” but denied Russian claims that Pokrovsk was fully surrounded. “There are Russians in Pokrovsk,” he said, adding that they were being “gradually destroyed” as Ukraine sought to preserve its personnel. The article describes the battle as one of Russia’s largest offensives in months. Ukraine faces troop shortages and has previously withdrawn from cities to preserve its forces, but had held Pokrovsk through more than a year of intense fighting. The article does not establish whether Russia will capture all of the city by November 30.

evidence.title: The Russia-Ukraine War Report Card, Oct. 29, 2025 - Russia Matters
evidence.text: As of the Oct. 29 report, Russia had not established control of Pokrovsk. The article shows a major Russian push but does not establish that capture of all Pokrovsk by Nov. 30 is imminent.

market.question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
market.resolution_criteria:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

evidence.text: Minutes of the Fed’s Jan. 27–28 Federal Open Market Committee meeting, released Wednesday, say “almost all” participants supported holding the federal funds rate at 4.25%–4.5%. The article says the Fed had cut rates by a cumulative 75 basis points in the last four months of 2024, but does not identify a December decision separately. It reports no March decision: some officials favored keeping rates restrictive, several expected cuts later in 2025, and several wanted to leave open a hike if inflation remained above target.

evidence.title: Markets react as US Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged - news.cgtn.com
evidence.text: The Fed held its target rate at 3.5%–3.75% at its first policy meeting of 2026, on January 28, following three consecutive cuts in the second half of 2025. Ten of 12 FOMC members voted to hold; Stephen Miran and Christopher Waller preferred a 25-basis-point cut. This supports a cut followed by a January pause, but the article does not establish a March decision. The FOMC said economic activity was expanding solidly, job gains remained low, unemployment showed signs of stabilizing, and inflation remained somewhat elevated. Chair Jerome Powell said future rate decisions would be made meeting by meeting based on incoming data, not a preset course.

evidence.title: Fed Keeps Rates Steady - The New York Times
evidence.text: The article supports a Cut–Pause–Pause sequence, though the March decision is not yet known. The Fed cut rates by 25 basis points in September, October and December, then voted 10–2 on Wednesday to hold the federal funds rate at 3.5%–3.75%; Governors Stephen Miran and Christopher Waller favored another 25-basis-point cut. Policymakers cited a stabilizing but slow labor market and inflation still above the 2% target. Powell said the current policy stance was appropriate while the Fed assessed new data. For the next meeting in March, CME FedWatch showed an 86% probability of another hold, up from 82.7% a week earlier and 46.7% a month earlier.

evidence.title: Fed holds interest rates steady, pausing rate cuts amid economic uncertainty - Fox Business
evidence.text: The Fed voted Wednesday to hold its benchmark rate at 3.5%–3.75% after three straight cuts last fall, supporting the pause portion of a cut–pause–pause sequence. Governors Chris Waller and Stephen Miran favored another quarter-point cut. Officials upgraded their assessment of the economy from “moderate” to “solid” and saw signs of labor-market stabilization, but said inflation remained somewhat elevated. Powell said future decisions, including whether to cut at the next meeting, would depend on incoming data; the article does not establish a March pause.

evidence.title: Bitcoin hits breaking point this week as the Fed’s hidden liquidity trap threatens to drain markets despite a rate hold - cryptoslate.com
evidence.text: As of late January 2026, before the Fed’s January 27–28 meeting, the federal funds target range was 3.50%–3.75%. market.question: Will the next US x Venezuela military engagement occur on December 29?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) of the next military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela. 

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Trump can’t close Venezuela airspace ‘in its entirety’, but what can he actually do? Explained - The Indian Express
evidence.text: Trump told US military service members last week that land strikes in Venezuela could start “very soon,” but told reporters not to “read anything into it” when asked whether his airspace comments signaled an imminent strike. The article reports US air strikes on vessels it says were involved in drug trafficking, killing more than 80 people since early September. US bombers have flown near Venezuela, and the USS Gerald R Ford is stationed in the region as part of a buildup involving nearly a dozen Navy ships and about 12,000 sailors and Marines. The article gives no date for a next military engagement and does not identify December 29 as a likely date.

evidence.title: Venezuela: Trump signals imminent land attacks - DW.com
evidence.text: Trump said on Thursday that American troops would begin land strikes on suspected Venezuelan drug traffickers “very soon.” On Saturday, he said the airspace above and around Venezuela would be closed entirely. Since early September, US attacks on around 20 suspected drug-smuggling speedboats, mostly from Venezuela, have killed more than 80 people. The article says targeted missile or air strikes on suspected smuggling infrastructure are conceivable, but also reports that Trump has offered Maduro talks. It gives no date for a next military engagement and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: Resistance builds within the United States against Trump’s drive to war with Venezuela - Peoples Dispatch
evidence.text: The article gives no indication that a U.S.–Venezuela military engagement is scheduled for December 29. It says the Trump administration has built up warships near Venezuela, including the USS Gerald R. Ford, the largest U.S. aircraft carrier, while U.S. forces have struck small boats accused of smuggling drugs. The administration reports at least 87 people killed in 22 known strikes since early September; the latest listed strike was on December 4. The Ford arrived in the Caribbean on November 16, bringing the regional U.S. presence to about 12,000 troops on nearly a dozen Navy ships. Trump said land attacks were coming soon but gave no location or date. Venezuela’s government conducted military exercises in response to the buildup. The article reports no direct U.S.–Venezuela clash or December 29 plan.

evidence.title: A Timeline of the US Military's Buildup Near Venezuela and Attacks on Alleged Drug Boats - Military.com
evidence.text: The article says the US has carried out nearly two dozen strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean since September, killing more than 80 people; the latest reported strike, on a Thursday, killed four. It says the Trump administration has not presented evidence that the boats carried drugs or smugglers. Trump has said the US is preparing to attack alleged drug traffickers “on land,” which the article says suggests a direct operation against Venezuela might be imminent. It also reports that the US deployed the USS Gerald R Ford, thousands of troops and F-35 jets to the Caribbean in recent weeks. The article gives no date for a planned operation and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: Concerning Kinetic Strikes on Drug Boats: Law, Not Hyperbole | Proceedings - December 2025 Vol. 151/12/1,474 - U.S. Naval Institute
evidence.text: The article says President Donald Trump was considering US land operations in Venezuela against people he called “narco-terrorists”; it does not say he had decided to launch them. US Ambassador to Guyana Nicole Theriot said the US would stand with Guyana if Nicolás Maduro’s administration attacked it, amid renewed Venezuelan claims to Guyana’s 160,000-square-kilometre Essequibo Region. She said US officials were considering whether Venezuela might attack Guyana in response to US operations on Venezuelan soil. Analyst Evan Ellis said substantial US forces in the Caribbean would deter such an attack and described a serious Venezuelan attack as highly unlikely. The article gives no date for a planned US operation or the next US–Venezuela military engagement and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: ‘The homeland is the homeland’: Venezuelans brace for possible US attack - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The article reports a US military strike on an alleged Venezuelan drug boat on September 2, followed by a second strike that killed two survivors; nine people died in the first strike, according to the Washington Post. The Trump administration says the strikes complied with the law of armed conflict and describes its Caribbean operations as a “non-international armed conflict” with alleged drug traffickers. UCLA legal expert Jessica Peake disputes that characterization, saying the US is neither in an international armed conflict with Venezuela nor in a non-international armed conflict with criminal gangs or drug cartels. The article gives no indication that another US–Venezuela military engagement is planned for December 29.

evidence.text: The article reports that the US has amassed 15,000 troops in the region and deployed an aircraft carrier to the Caribbean. It says the US has carried out at least 21 strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean and Pacific since September, killing up to 83 people. On November 20, President Trump said land strikes inside Venezuela could come imminently, though he later told reporters not to “read anything” into his recent moves. The article raises the possibility of further military action but gives no indication that an engagement will occur specifically on December 29.

It gives no indication that the next military engagement will occur on December 29.

evidence.title: Venezuela calls on OPEC to counter US threats - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: The article reports escalating US–Venezuela tensions but gives no date for a future military engagement and does not mention December 29. The article says US strikes on vessels that President Donald Trump claimed were carrying drugs have killed at least 83 people. It also reports a substantial US deployment to the Caribbean: the USS Gerald R Ford, described as the world’s largest aircraft carrier, other warships, thousands of troops and F-35 fighter jets. market.question: Will the next US x Venezuela military engagement occur on December 29?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) of the next military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela. 

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: US seizes oil tanker off coast of Venezuela, Trump says - ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
evidence.text: As of December 11, 2025, the article reported a rapid U.S. military buildup under Operation Southern Spear, a mission that began as a counter-narcotics effort and was increasingly aimed at Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Reuters photos showed HC-130J rescue planes and HH-60W rescue helicopters at Roosevelt Roads, Puerto Rico. The article said their deployment could signal that the Trump administration is preparing to increase pressure on Maduro and strike cartels inland; the aircraft could rescue crews lost during operations over contested territory. It also reported refueling aircraft operating from the Dominican Republic and U.S. Virgin Islands, electronic-attack jets in Puerto Rico, and F-35As being sent to the Caribbean. White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt said Trump did not want a prolonged war in Venezuela. The article gives no plan or date for a strike or other engagement, and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: Colombian guerrillas declare nationwide armed strike to protest US aggression - Latin America Reports
evidence.text: The article reports a US seizure of a crude oil tanker off Venezuela’s coast on a Wednesday. Attorney General Pam Bondi said the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations and US Coast Guard executed a seizure warrant with support from the Department of War; she said the tanker had carried sanctioned oil from Venezuela and Iran. Reuters reported that the vessel was the Skipper, seized early Wednesday. The article also says the US had carried out strikes on at least 21 suspected drug-trafficking vessels since September. It gives no date for a next US–Venezuela military engagement and does not identify December 29 as one.

evidence.title: Global Outcry as US Escalates Military Threats Against Venezuela - Orinoco Tribune
evidence.text: In a December 8, 2025 article, Francisco Dominguez reports that the US had deployed a war fleet in the South Caribbean since August and that US forces had struck more than 20 small boats since early September, killing 83 people. The article says President Donald Trump recently declared the airspace above and around Venezuela “closed in its entirety” and said land strikes in Venezuela “could start very soon.” These claims point to a risk of further military action, but the article gives no date for a next engagement and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: Did the U.S. attack? Maduro flee? No, but in Venezuela, rampant rumors fly - Los Angeles Times
evidence.text: Since the fall, the U.S. has carried out more than 20 known strikes on boats near Venezuela, killing more than 80 people. The Trump administration says, without providing evidence, that the boats were trafficking drugs. Trump has also sent the U.S.S. Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier, fighter jets and guided-missile destroyers to the Caribbean. On December 10, the U.S. seized the sanctioned oil tanker Skipper and threatened further seizures. The article describes continuing escalation but gives no indication that the next U.S.–Venezuela military engagement will occur on December 29.

evidence.title: Trump can’t close Venezuela airspace ‘in its entirety’, but what can he actually do? Explained - The Indian Express
evidence.text: Trump told US military service members last week that land strikes in Venezuela could start “very soon,” but told reporters not to “read anything into it” when asked whether his airspace comments signaled an imminent strike. The article reports US air strikes on vessels it says were involved in drug trafficking, killing more than 80 people since early September. US bombers have flown near Venezuela, and the USS Gerald R Ford is stationed in the region as part of a buildup involving nearly a dozen Navy ships and about 12,000 sailors and Marines. The article gives no date for a next military engagement and does not identify December 29 as a likely date.

evidence.title: Venezuela: Trump signals imminent land attacks - DW.com
evidence.text: Trump said on Thursday that American troops would begin land strikes on suspected Venezuelan drug traffickers “very soon.” On Saturday, he said the airspace above and around Venezuela would be closed entirely. Since early September, US attacks on around 20 suspected drug-smuggling speedboats, mostly from Venezuela, have killed more than 80 people. The article says targeted missile or air strikes on suspected smuggling infrastructure are conceivable, but also reports that Trump has offered Maduro talks. It gives no date for a next military engagement and does not mention December 29.

evidence.title: Resistance builds within the United States against Trump’s drive to war with Venezuela - Peoples Dispatch
evidence.text: The article gives no indication that a U.S.–Venezuela military engagement is scheduled for December 29. It says the Trump administration has built up warships near Venezuela, including the USS Gerald R. Ford, the largest U.S. aircraft carrier, while U.S. forces have struck small boats accused of smuggling drugs. The administration reports at least 87 people killed in 22 known strikes since early September; the latest listed strike was on December 4. market.question: Will the next US x Venezuela military engagement occur on December 29?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the date (ET) of the next military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela. 

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Israel strike 2 countries in December 2025?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between December 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of November 26, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Israel strike 2 countries in December 2025?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between December 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of November 26, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.title: Georgia 14th election: Harris takes first, Trump-backed Fuller advances to runoff - Atlanta News First
evidence.text: The special election for the northwest Georgia 14th congressional district seat vacated by Marjorie Taylor Greene is headed to an April 7 runoff between Democrat Shawn Harris and Republican Clayton Fuller. Harris led Tuesday’s 17-candidate election with 37.3% of the vote; Fuller finished second with just under 35%. Harris may have benefited from a field that included more than a dozen Republicans. The district is considered strongly Republican and backed Donald Trump by more than 30 percentage points in the last presidential election. Trump has endorsed Fuller. The runoff will decide who serves the remainder of Greene’s term, through January.

evidence.title: Georgia special election to replace Greene heads to runoff - Roll Call

market.question: Russian strike on a NATO member by March 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between December 4, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.text: The article says the war has extended beyond Ukraine into “gray zone” provocations, citing frequent drone incursions into NATO territory in Poland, Romania and Latvia. It also says Russia is likely to continue high-intensity strikes, but does not report a strike on a NATO member or predict one by March 31. It gives no dates or details for the incursions.

evidence.text: In 2025, Russia launched an estimated 50,000–55,000 Shahed-type drones at targets inside Ukraine. A small number flew through Ukrainian airspace onward to Poland and Romania, both NATO members, as well as Belarus and Moldova. The article reports these crossings but does not say the drones struck targets in NATO territory. Ukrainian air defenders describe Shaheds as relatively inaccurate because of their primitive navigation electronics.

evidence.text: The article says CNN reported on 7 March 2026 that the US had decided to deploy its Merops anti-drone system to the Middle East, drawing on lessons from Ukraine. It describes Merops as having been proven in combat against Russian drones in Poland and Romania, both NATO members. The article does not say when those drone encounters occurred or whether Russia deliberately targeted either country.

The article does not report a Russian strike on a NATO member or predict one by March 31.

evidence.title: Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, February 13, 2026 - Institute for the Study of War

He examines five possible scenarios, ordered from least to most risk for Russia: occupying Svalbard, occupying the Åland islands, seizing territory in eastern Estonia, seizing Gotland, and conducting operations to establish a land corridor to Kaliningrad. The article says senior NATO military and intelligence leaders warn that near-term aggression on NATO territory is a serious threat, while Western intelligence services say Russia is reconstituting its forces. It argues that if the Ukraine war becomes a prolonged frozen conflict, Russia will rearm and Putin may test NATO’s Article 5 response where he judges the chance of a robust response low or success attainable at acceptable cost. This is an assessment of possible future aggression, not a claim that Russia will strike a NATO member by March 31; it gives no date for any of the five scenarios.

market.question: Russian strike on a NATO member by March 31?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between December 4, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Michael Saylor said the company may sell Bitcoin in the future to help cover dividends on STRC, its Bitcoin-backed perpetual preferred stock; the article gives no date or commitment for a sale. Strategy also has preferred-dividend and debt-interest obligations. Critics say falling Bitcoin prices, weaker investor demand or rising dividend costs could create pressure, while the company has used stock, debt and preferred equity to finance Bitcoin purchases. It held 818,334 BTC, and JPMorgan projected that its 2026 purchases could reach about $30 billion if its current pace continues.

The article reports no Bitcoin sale and provides no evidence of whether Strategy will sell any by December 31, 2026.

evidence.title: Peter Schiff Warns STRC Crash Could Come Before Strategy Has The Chance To Sell Its Bitcoin - Stocktwits
evidence.text: On a call for its first-quarter 2026 results, announced on the 5th, Strategy’s CEO said the company would consider selling Bitcoin to obtain dollars or reduce debt if doing so increased Bitcoin value per share. market.question: Will Marco Rubio be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

evidence.title: Outrage as Trump withdraws from key UN climate treaty along with dozens of international organisations - The Guardian
evidence.text: The article says that, after less than 12 months in office, many Trump Cabinet members had faced calls to resign. It gives a specific example: on 11 December, Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson urged Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem to resign or be fired. It also criticizes Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Attorney General Pam Bondi, but does not report their departures. Marco Rubio is not mentioned, and the article provides no direct evidence that he will be the first to leave the Cabinet before 2027.

evidence.title: Who is Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela's interim president after Maduro's ouster? - PBS
evidence.text: The article identifies Marco Rubio as Trump’s secretary of state and reports that he appeared on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Rubio called Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado “fantastic” and said he had known her for a “very long time.” Although Trump had questioned whether Machado could lead Venezuela, Rubio said the immediate reality was that most of the opposition was no longer inside the country. He said the administration’s first priorities were stopping drug trafficking, an Iran/Hezbollah presence, and use of Venezuela’s oil industry to enrich U.S. adversaries—not pushing for an election. The article reports no indication that Rubio plans to leave the Cabinet.

evidence.title: The top- and bottom-performing Trump Cabinet members, ranked - Washington Examiner
evidence.text: Trump’s first 14 months in his first term had the highest Cabinet turnover of any president in a century, but his second-term Cabinet has remained almost entirely intact since he returned to office in January. Trump recently called the Cabinet “fantastic” and denied reports that he was unhappy with Pete Hegseth or Kristi Noem. The article says the closest brush with dismissal was national security adviser Mike Waltz being replaced by Marco Rubio; Waltz was then nominated for UN ambassador. It reports no indication that Rubio is at risk of leaving. Commentators cited in the article say Trump may be reluctant to fire Cabinet members because replacements could face difficult Senate confirmations and because firing someone would acknowledge a mistake.

evidence.title: Outrage and legal threats: Trump justice department slammed after limited Epstein files release - The Guardian
evidence.text: The article provides no information about Marco Rubio or whether he might leave the Cabinet before 2027. It does report pressure on another Cabinet member, Attorney General Pam Bondi, over the Justice Department’s limited, heavily redacted release of Jeffrey Epstein files despite a law requiring near-complete disclosure by 19 December. After at least 16 files disappeared from the department’s website without explanation, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez accused “Pam Bondi, Kash Patel, [and the] whole admin” of protecting “rapists and pedophiles” because of their money, power and connections, and said Bondi “should resign tonight.” Other lawmakers raised possible legal action against Justice Department officials. The department said it was complying with the law and protecting victims. The article reports a demand for Bondi’s resignation, not an actual departure.

evidence.title: Voters Oppose US Military Boat Strikes in Caribbean, Want Hegseth to Resign: Poll - Military.com
evidence.text: A Dec. 5–9 Data for Progress poll of 1,165 likely U.S. voters found that a plurality wanted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to resign; the pollster said that included 41% of independents. The article links scrutiny of Hegseth to U.S. strikes on alleged drug-carrying boats and questions about their legality. It says Secretary of State Marco Rubio was among officials briefing Congress on the strikes, but reports no call for Rubio to resign or indication that he plans to leave. The evidence therefore concerns potential pressure on Hegseth, not a departure by Rubio.

evidence.title: Alina Habba Resigns as Trump Loses Yet Another Totally Inept Nominee - The New Republic
evidence.text: The article does not mention Marco Rubio or report that he plans to leave the Cabinet. It concerns Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, whose potential departure would matter to whether Rubio is the first to leave. Hegseth faces calls to resign over a September Caribbean boat strike in which two survivors were killed in a follow-up attack, and a Defense Department inspector general report released Thursday that found he violated Pentagon policies by sharing sensitive details of 15 March Yemen airstrikes on Signal. Democratic lawmakers called for his resignation, and some Republicans expressed concerns about his leadership. Nevertheless, the article says Hegseth shows no sign of stepping down, Donald Trump continues to support him, and the White House has expressed “the utmost confidence” in its national security team.

market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, Netflix (directly or through a subsidiary) acquires control of Warner Bros.’ film and TV studios and associated streaming/pay-TV businesses (including HBO / HBO Max and related content libraries), as described in the companies’ December 5, 2025 acquisition announcement by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. If the transaction is terminated, allowed to lapse past its contractual outside date without closing, blocked by regulators, or replaced by an alternative structure in which Netflix does not acquire control of Warner Bros.’ film/TV studios and streaming business, this market will resolve to “No”.

If the acquisition closes on substantially similar terms—even with changes to price, mix of cash/stock, or required divestitures—but Netflix still ends up in control of the Warner Bros film and TV studios and the HBO/HBO Max streaming business, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

market.question: Israel strike on Damascus by March 31, 2026?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Damascus Governorate, or any target within it, between December 8, 2:20 PM ET, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact within Damascus Governorate.

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land in Damascus Governorate, or cause damage.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting and video evidence. If there is ambiguity over whether a strike occurred, or whether the drone/missile was intercepted, this market will resolve based on whatever is most likely according to a consensus of credible reporting and video evidence.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Apple officially releases iPhone 18 by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A qualifying product must be named "iPhone" and be recognized as a successor to the original iPhone product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 15 and iPhone 16. A new iPhone product released without a number, under a designation other than iPhone 18, will qualify if it retains the original functions of the iPhone and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from Apple. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

market.question: Will SpaceX's public ticker be $SPC?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the public ticker symbol used by SpaceX in an IPO (Initial Public Offering) by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET.

An official announcement from SpaceX that they will IPO under a specific ticker symbol will be sufficient to resolve this market.

If a ticker used by SpaceX in a qualifying IPO is a variant of a ticker symbol listed in this market group with additional letters to denote a specific class of shares, it will be considered to be that ticker (e.g. if SpaceX uses a ticker symbol of $MARS.A or $MARSA, this market will resolve to $MARS).

If SpaceX announces an IPO with multiple tickers that are not considered the same ticker under the previous rule (i.e. $MARS.A and $MARS.B would be considered the same ticker), this market will remain open until SpaceX’s first day of public trading and will resolve according to the ticker symbolizing the security class with the greatest market capitalization. Market capitalization is calculated as the number of shares outstanding multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day. If this also results in a tie, this market will resolve according to the ticker symbol that comes first in alphabetical order.

If SpaceX IPOs with a non-listed ticker, or does not IPO or officially announce an IPO and ticker symbol by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from SpaceX and the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

Note: In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on SpaceX’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will use the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will use the closing price on the next trading day for which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading for purposes of this market.

market.question: Will SpaceX's public ticker be $SPC?
market.resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the public ticker symbol used by SpaceX in an IPO (Initial Public Offering) by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET.

An official announcement from SpaceX that they will IPO under a specific ticker symbol will be sufficient to resolve this market.

If a ticker used by SpaceX in a qualifying IPO is a variant of a ticker symbol listed in this market group with additional letters to denote a specific class of shares, it will be considered to be that ticker (e.g. if SpaceX uses a ticker symbol of $MARS.A or $MARSA, this market will resolve to $MARS).

If SpaceX announces an IPO with multiple tickers that are not considered the same ticker under the previous rule (i.e. $MARS.A and $MARS.B would be considered the same ticker), this market will remain open until SpaceX’s first day of public trading and will resolve according to the ticker symbolizing the security class with the greatest market capitalization. Market capitalization is calculated as the number of shares outstanding multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day. If this also results in a tie, this market will resolve according to the ticker symbol that comes first in alphabetical order.

If SpaceX IPOs with a non-listed ticker, or does not IPO or officially announce an IPO and ticker symbol by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from SpaceX and the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

Note: In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on SpaceX’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will use the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will use the closing price on the next trading day for which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading for purposes of this market.

market.question: Will the Prosperity Party (Prosperity) win the most seats in the 2026 Ethiopian general election?
market.resolution_criteria:
General elections are scheduled to be held in Ethiopia on June 1, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party that wins the greatest number of seats in the next Ethiopian House of Peoples' Representatives election. 

If the results are not known definitively by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition that received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose listed abbreviation appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party in the Ethiopian Parliament.

This market will resolve based on the results of this election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Ethiopian government, specifically the National Election Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) (nebe.org.et/en).

The exception was the House seat in Gondar Zuria Constituency No. 4, won by Tahir Mohammed Tahir of the National Movement of Amhara; Prosperity did not field a candidate there. The article says 353 House seats and 463 regional council seats have been confirmed, but does not give a party-by-party breakdown for those totals. Voting covered 1,139 constituencies, including contests for 501 House seats; NEBE had verified results from 816 constituencies, with others still being processed. Officials cautioned that results remain preliminary while verification, tabulation and reconciliation continue.

evidence.title: Ethiopia goes to the polls with the result widely seen as a foregone conclusion - RFI
evidence.text: RFI reported on 1 June 2026 that analysts expect Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party to win Ethiopia’s parliamentary election by a large margin. Voters are choosing 547 members of the lower house; Prosperity won 410 of 484 seats in the 2021 election. The article says the party is expected to dominate a fragmented opposition weakened by internal rivalries, and an ACLED expert told RFI it was “obvious” Prosperity would win. Tigray is not participating, and voting will not take place in at least eight of Amhara’s 138 constituencies. Results are not expected until 11 June.

evidence.title: Ethiopia holds elections with PM Abiy’s party expected to dominate - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: Ethiopians have begun voting in parliamentary and regional elections, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s Prosperity Party projected to win by a landslide. The party won 410 of 484 parliamentary seats in 2021 and is expected to dominate a fragmented opposition weakened by internal rivalries. More than 50 million people are registered, but significant unrest will prevent voting in Tigray and at least eight of Amhara’s 138 constituencies. Opposition parties allege the government has arrested their leaders and obstructed their activities; the government denies this. Results are expected by June 11.

evidence.title: Ethiopia’s election: Parties, coalitions and candidates explained - Al Jazeera
evidence.text: As of May 31, 2026, the article says Ethiopia’s June 1 election is expected to return Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s ruling Prosperity Party to power. Prosperity won 96% of parliamentary seats in 2021 and is running uncontested in 64 of Ethiopia’s 547 constituencies this time. The article says none of the roughly 40 opposition parties is a serious contender; the largest, Ezema, is fielding candidates in fewer than 60% of seats and currently has four MPs. Voting will not take place on June 1 in 46 constituencies in Amhara and Tigray because of instability and political tensions. Results are due June 11.

evidence.title: Ethiopia Heads To Seventh Election Amid Unsettled Debates Over Security, Fairness - The Reporter Ethiopia
evidence.text: Ahead of Ethiopia’s June 1, 2026 election, the incumbent Prosperity Party (PP) held major final campaigns in towns and cities across the country, though party leader and Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed attended none of them. The article reports no polling or seat projections. Of 547 federal parliamentary seats, 501 are due to be contested; Tigray’s 38 constituencies and eight in Amhara will not vote. More than 54 million voters are registered, and 42 political parties, including coalitions and fronts, are running in the federal election. Opposition parties say conflict and insecurity have restricted their campaigning, and accuse the government of proceeding under conditions that favor PP. The election board says conditions are suitable in almost all areas outside Tigray, despite opposition objections.

evidence.title: Valerie Foushee faces contentious rematch with Nida Allam in NC’s bluest district - Raleigh News & Observer
evidence.text: Nida Allam is challenging incumbent Rep. Valerie Foushee for the Democratic nomination in North Carolina’s 4th Congressional District. Foushee defeated Allam by about 10 percentage points in the 2022 primary and now has the advantages of incumbency and an established campaign team. Both candidates raised more than $300,000 in 2025, but as of Dec. 31, Allam had $306,000 cash on hand versus Foushee’s $194,000. The article says part of that gap reflects Foushee’s $244,000 in campaign spending that year—about 10 times Allam’s spending—while Allam was building her campaign. Bernie Sanders plans to campaign with Allam as early voting begins; Foushee has endorsements from Gov. Josh Stein and former Gov. Roy Cooper. National groups are also buying television ads for Allam, including $116,000 in WRAL ads from Leaders We Deserve and at least $92,000 in local ads from American Priorities PAC.
